一.originText: a horizontal stroke, indicating the number.

丁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – different theories exist:
* the head of a nail. The derivative {{zh-l|*釘}} is now used to represent this sense. This interpretation was formulated by Liu Xinyuan (劉心源), Lin Yiguang (林義光), and Wu Qichang (吳其昌).
* a head. The derivative {{zh-l|*天}} and {{zh-l|*頂}} is now used to represent this sense. Characters like {{zh-l|*元}} contain it as a semantic component. This is interpretation was formulated by Gao Hongjin (高鴻縉) and could be linked to the first interpretation ("head of a nail").
* a city wall. In ancient China, city walls were square-shaped. The derivative {{zh-l|*成}} and later {{zh-l|*城}} is now used to represent this sense. The character {{zh-l|*正|征}} contains it as a semantic component (but in {{zh-l|*邑}}, the top component is [[囗]], not 丁). This interpretation was formulated by He Linyi (何琳儀).
* Pictogram of the Great Square of [[Pegasus]], related to {{zh-l|*定}} and {{zh-l|*正}} (David W. Pankenier).

See also [[旦]].
丁.originText: different theories exist: See also 旦.

七.originText: a vertical stroke and a horizontal stroke bisecting each other – original character of 切. The top-most horizontal stroke is done from left to right. The vertical stroke and bottom-most horizontal stroke are done as one stroke, from top-left to bottom-right.

万.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{unk|zh}}. Used as a tribal name in oracle inscriptions. Used as a number since the {{w|Spring and Autumn period|Spring and Autumn}} and {{w|Warring States period}}s.

Various theories have been proposed for its original meaning:
* [[w:zh:屈萬里|Qu Wanli]], {{w|Qiu Xigui}} and others propose that it originally refers to a type of dancer-musicians. This usage is attested in the oracle inscriptions. This may be supported by ancient literature, e.g. ''{{w|Shijing}}'', which mentions a type of dance called {{zh-l|萬舞}}.
* Lin Yiguang proposes that it is an ancient form of {{och-l|丏}}, acting as a phonetic component in {{och-l|賓}}.
* Some propose that it is a differentiated form of {{zh-l|*亥}}.
万.originText: Used as a tribal name in oracle inscriptions. Used as a number since the and s. Various theories have been proposed for its original meaning:

丈.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|十|又|ls=ic|t1=ten|t2=hand}} – ten ''chi'' ({{zh-l|*尺}}) is one ''zhang'' ({{lang|zh|丈}}). Similar but unrelated to [[支]].
丈.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 十 (ten) + semantic 又 (hand) – ten chi (尺) is one zhang (丈). Similar but unrelated to 支.

三.originText: three parallel strokes. Compare with 一, one stroke meaning “one”, 二, two strokes meaning “two”, and 亖, four strokes meaning “four”. tripled 一 (one). See also 畺. Unrelated to 丰.

上.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: short horizontal above long arc (contrast {{l|zh|下}}).
上.originText: short horizontal above long arc (contrast 下).

下.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}}: short horizontal below long arc (contrast {{l|zh|上}}).
下.originText: short horizontal below long arc (contrast 上).

不.originText: the calyx of a flower. 不 was composed into a phono-semantic character with the pictograph for mouth (口), to form 否, representing “no” (negation). This composed meaning then spread back to the original character 不, making it a synonym of 否. A new character of 柎 was eventually created to represent the original meaning of calyx. Following '’s interpretation, Karlgren and Wieger interpret it as a bird flying toward the sky (一). The sky being the limit for the bird, thus the idea of negation.

且.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}. Multiple interpretations:
* A stone altar – original form of {{och-l|祖}}.
* A sacrificial vessel used for chopping and holding meat, as viewed from above ({{zh-ref|Wang, 1923}}) – original form of {{och-l|俎}}.
* An erect penis, the symbol of the male ancestor ({{zh-ref|Guo Moruo, 1931}}) – original form of {{och-l|祖}}.

In the oracle bones and bronze inscriptions, this character was commonly used as {{och-l|祖}}; usage as {{och-l|俎}} is not attested until the Warring States period in the bamboo script. See also the original version of [[查]].
且.originText: Multiple interpretations: In the oracle bones and bronze inscriptions, this character was commonly used as 祖; usage as 俎 is not attested until the Warring States period in the bamboo script. See also the original version of 查.

世.originText: Variant form of 枼 (the original form of 葉) with the tree removed. ' interprets it as 十 triplicated: thirty years make one generation (thirty times twelve months gives 360 months).

丘.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}} – hill. Earlier form closer to {{zh-l|*丠}}, as in {{och-l|虛}}. Compare {{zh-l|*山}}. Unrelated to [[兵]] and [[斤]].
丘.originText: hill. Earlier form closer to 丠, as in 虛. Compare 山. Unrelated to 兵 and 斤.

丙.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Shang bronze script Geng Bing combined.svg|thumb|right|Late Shang bronze script clan insignia forms of {{l|zh|𫷻}}, composed of {{l|zh|庚}} and {{l|zh|丙}}.]]
Various theories:
* {{liushu|p}} – shoulders (''{{w|Shuowen}}'').
* {{liushu|p}} – the tail of a fish (''{{w|Erya}}''). See also [[再]].
* {{liushu|p}} - part of a chariot, as seen in the original form of [[更]].
* {{liushu|p}} – pedestal.
* {{liushu|p}} – small table.
* Original form of {{och-l|柄}}.

Whatever its original sense may be, it has been lost and replaced by its early use as a [[heavenly stem]]. See also the original version of [[更]] (< [[㪅]]).
丙.originText: Various theories: Whatever its original sense may be, it has been lost and replaced by its early use as a heavenly stem. See also the original version of 更 (< 㪅).

並.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
From the {{w|clerical script}} ({{zh-l|*隸書}}) of {{och-l|竝}}, originally depicting two people standing side-by-side.
並.originText: From the (隸書) of 竝, originally depicting two people standing side-by-side.

中.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}} – a flagpole, as depicted in its original form [[𠁩]]. Based on archaeological evidence, the middle box has been interpreted as a drum ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|建鼓}}). This flagpole with a drum was placed in the center of a field to gather people and to detect the direction of the wind. In addition, the pronunciation of {{och-l|中}} is reminiscent of the beating of a drum.

''[[w:Shuowen|Shuowen]]'' interprets the character as a vertical stroke {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|丨}} passing through the center of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|口}}, indicating the center.

It has also been interpreted as an arrow in the center of a target.
中.originText: a flagpole, as depicted in its original form 𠁩. Based on archaeological evidence, the middle box has been interpreted as a drum (建鼓). This flagpole with a drum was placed in the center of a field to gather people and to detect the direction of the wind. In addition, the pronunciation of 中 is reminiscent of the beating of a drum. Shuowen interprets the character as a vertical stroke 丨 passing through the center of 口, indicating the center. It has also been interpreted as an arrow in the center of a target.

丸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}, differentiated form of {{och-l|夗}}, which was originally the same character. 

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' suggests that it is an {{liushu|i|nocap=1}} from flipped {{zh-l|*仄|to tilt}} – something that can be tilted and turned; something round.

Unrelated to the right component of characters like {{zh-l|*執}} and {{zh-l|*孰}}, which comes from {{zh-l|*丮}} (a kneeling person with stretched arms to indicate "to hold").
丸.originText: , differentiated form of 夗, which was originally the same character. ' suggests that it is an from flipped 仄 – something that can be tilted and turned; something round. Unrelated to the right component of characters like 執 and 孰, which comes from 丮 (a kneeling person with stretched arms to indicate "to hold").

丹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of a well or mine with [[cinnabar]] inside. It can also indicate "red cinnabar" used in dyeing clothes (e.g., [[彤]]). The original version is [[𠂁]].
丹.originText: of a well or mine with cinnabar inside. It can also indicate "red cinnabar" used in dyeing clothes (e.g., 彤). The original version is 𠂁.

主.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}. Three distinct forms can be observed in ancient scripts, all of which have merged into the same character in modern script:
# A lamp or torch with a flame at the top. Original form of {{zh-l|*炷}}.
# Wood ({{och-l|*木}}, now {{och-l|*王}}) on fire.
# A {{w|spirit tablet}}. Same character as {{och-l|*示}}.

Unrelated to the right component of [[往]] (< [[𢓸]]).
主.originText: Three distinct forms can be observed in ancient scripts, all of which have merged into the same character in modern script: # A lamp or torch with a flame at the top. Original form of 炷. # Wood (木, now 王) on fire. # A. Same character as 示. Unrelated to the right component of 往 (< 𢓸).

丼.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|i}}. Originally, it was a variant form of [[井]] (“water well”). The dot (丶) represents the shape of the well’s pulley bucket. By extension, it is used to signify the sound of something being thrown into a well.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
丼.originText: Originally, it was a variant form of 井 (“water well”). The dot (丶) represents the shape of the well’s pulley bucket. By extension, it is used to signify the sound of something being thrown into a well.

久.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Used interchangeably with {{och-l|氒}} in oracle bone script. Likely a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of an arrow tip.
久.originText: Used interchangeably with 氒 in oracle bone script. Likely a of an arrow tip.

乏.originText: Chen Jian suggests that the graph derives from ⿱口⿰止止, an ideogram shared by 範 and 圍: one 止 was omitted, and one stroke was slanted to avoid confusion with 正.

乗.originRaw: Variant form of {{l|zh|乘}} written in {{w|clerical script}} found in the <big>《魯峻碑陰》</big> stone tablet of the {{w|Han dynasty#Eastern Han|eastern Han}} period.
乗.originText: Variant form of 乘 written in found in the 《魯峻碑陰》 stone tablet of the period.

乙.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}}. Origin obscure.
* ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets it as a plant struggling to sprout.
* Ancient texts associate the shape with a fish's intestine (''{{w|Erya}}'') or gill bone (''{{w|Book of Rites|Liji}}'').
* Some modern scholars suggest it represents a water flow.
The character should not be confused with 𠃉 > 鳦.
乙.originText: Origin obscure. The character should not be confused with 𠃉 > 鳦.

九.originText: a stylized hand, with bent wrist/forearm (hence the hook stroke at lower right). Earlier forms resemble 手, 寸. The original meaning of the glyph was “elbow”, which is now written 肘. After the meaning “elbow” was forgotten, 九 was taken to symbolize a fist tightening to bump up against something; thus, there is a metaphorical bumping up of nine against ten, which is the last number when counting on one's fingers.

乞.originText: Variant of 气, distinguished to indicate a phonetically borrowed meaning “to beg”. The top component of the character is unrelated to 旅, 傷, 复, 每 as well as 人.

乳.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: A kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child. The woman resembles the character [[母]].
乳.originText: A kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child. The woman resembles the character 母.

乾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 倝 + semantic 乙.

亀.originRaw: Variant of {{l|mul|龜}}, {{Han simp|龜|nocap=1}}. The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
亀.originText: Variant of 龜, 龜. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

了.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
According to the {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}, a {{liushu|p|nocap=yes}} of a baby without arms. Compare with {{zh-l|*子}}, where the arms are visible. The Shuowen defines {{lang|zh|了}} as "the crossing of lower legs". 

In the {{w|Shuowen Jiezi Zhu}}, a commentary to the Shuowen Jiezi, it is said that the pictogram instead depicts entangled legs ({{zh-l|*了戾}}). 

Its relation with the meaning "to finish" is likely via sound loan, but an argument can be made about "entangled legs" → "tie"→ "finish".

Unrelated to [[亨]].
了.originText: According to the, a of a baby without arms. Compare with 子, where the arms are visible. The Shuowen defines 了 as "the crossing of lower legs". In the, a commentary to the Shuowen Jiezi, it is said that the pictogram instead depicts entangled legs (了戾). Its relation with the meaning "to finish" is likely via sound loan, but an argument can be made about "entangled legs" → "tie"→ "finish". Unrelated to 亨.

予.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|j}}: originally written as {{och-l|呂}}, phonetically borrowed for the meanings "I; give". Later, {{zh-l|*亅}} was added at the bottom as a distinguishing mark and the whole character was heavily stylized. See also {{zh-l|*幻}}.
予.originText: originally written as 呂, phonetically borrowed for the meanings "I; give". Later, 亅 was added at the bottom as a distinguishing mark and the whole character was heavily stylized. See also 幻.

事.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|又|t1=hand|中|t2=a flagpole with a drum|ls=ic}} – flag in hand > to perform one's job. Compare {{zh-l|*吏}}. Furthermore, both characters are related to {{zh-l|*史}}, which is a variant without the horizontal stroke on top.
事.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 又 (hand) + semantic 中 (a flagpole with a drum) – flag in hand > to perform one's job. Compare 吏. Furthermore, both characters are related to 史, which is a variant without the horizontal stroke on top.

二.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}} - two parallel strokes. Compare with {{l|zh|一}}, one stroke meaning one, {{l|zh|三}}, three strokes meaning three, and {{l|zh|亖}}, four strokes meaning four. {{zh-etym-double|一|one}}.
二.originText: two parallel strokes. Compare with 一, one stroke meaning one, 三, three strokes meaning three, and 亖, four strokes meaning four. doubled 一 (one).

互.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: {{zh-l|*牙}} and a distinguishing mark. Early texts often used {{lang|zh|互}} and {{lang|zh|牙}} interchangeably.
互.originText: 牙 and a distinguishing mark. Early texts often used 互 and 牙 interchangeably.

五.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally written {{zh-l|*𠄡}}, consisting of {{zh-l|*㐅}} with a bar on the top and bottom. Original meaning is unclear. Theories include:

* Yu Shenwu: a tally mark.
* Ding Shan: original form of {{och-l|互|to cross}}.
* Zhang Bingquan: {{liushu|p}}: palm lines from extending ones fingers
* Ji Xusheng: {{och-l|*亖|four}} with an added stroke.
* Lin Yiguang: original meaning is ''jiāowǔ'' {{zh-l|交午}}, with {{och-l|午}} being the original form of the wooden pestle.

In [[韋]], the upper component ([[𫝀]]) is the stylization of a footprint, hence it is similar but unrelated to 五.
五.originText: Originally written 𠄡, consisting of 㐅 with a bar on the top and bottom. Original meaning is unclear. Theories include: In 韋, the upper component (𫝀) is the stylization of a footprint, hence it is similar but unrelated to 五.

井.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Square well (Longgang Museum of Hakka Culture).jpg|thumb|井 – an old well in a historic area in [[Shenzhen]]. Notice the square shape.]]
{{liushu|p}} – a square well, with supports on four sides.

Some forms have a stone inside the well, as in [[丼]].

Alternatively, original character of [[刑]], [[形]] and [[型]]<ref>張富海.説“井”[J].出土文献与古文字研究,2021,(00):126-136.
</ref>.
井.originText: Notice the square shape.]] – a square well, with supports on four sides. Some forms have a stone inside the well, as in 丼. Alternatively, original character of 刑, 形 and 型.

亡.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: a line on {{zh-l|*刀}} – [[cutting edge]] of a [[knife]]; the original form of {{och-l|芒|edge of a knife}}.
亡.originText: a line on 刀 – cutting edge of a knife; the original form of 芒.

交.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a human with crossed legs. In today's writing, the upper part of the human is similar to [[立]], which in turn depicts a man standing. Unrelated to [[父]].
交.originText: a human with crossed legs. In today's writing, the upper part of the human is similar to 立, which in turn depicts a man standing. Unrelated to 父.

享.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} - An ancestral shrine. See also {{l|zh|亯}} and {{l|zh|亨}}. Unrelated to [[郭]].
享.originText: An ancestral shrine. See also 亯 and 亨. Unrelated to 郭.

京.originText: a tall building. Compare 高. When used as a component on top of the character, the character loses the bottom part 小. (e.g., 亮 and 亭).

亭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The Kangxi radical of the tower [[京]] (or [[髙]] > [[高]] according to its variants) with the phonetic component [[丁]] ([[nail]]). In the variant [[𠅘]], the body of the tower is more recognizable.
亭.originText: The Kangxi radical of the tower 京 (or 髙 > 高 according to its variants) with the phonetic component 丁 (nail). In the variant 𠅘, the body of the tower is more recognizable.

人.originRaw:
{{Han etyl|人}}
{{liushu|p}} – side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg. Compare {{l|zh|大}}, {{l|zh|立}}, {{l|zh|卩}}, {{l|zh|夭}}, and {{l|zh|氏}} according to one interpretation. See also the original version of [[年]].

[[亼]] is similar but unrelated; it represents an open mouth flipped upside down and appears on top of characters such as [[食]], [[金]], [[令]], [[龠]], and [[今]].

It represents a roof in the characters [[余]], [[茶]], [[舍]], and [[倉]]. It represents a flag on a flagpole in [[㫃]]. Eventually, it represents two parallel mountain walls in [[谷]].

The stylized version to the left of the characters is [[亻]] (see also [[千]]). Similar but unrelated to [[彳]].
人.originText: side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg. Compare 大, 立, 卩, 夭, and 氏 according to one interpretation. See also the original version of 年. 亼 is similar but unrelated; it represents an open mouth flipped upside down and appears on top of characters such as 食, 金, 令, 龠, and 今. It represents a roof in the characters 余, 茶, 舍, and 倉. It represents a flag on a flagpole in 㫃. Eventually, it represents two parallel mountain walls in 谷. The stylized version to the left of the characters is 亻 (see also 千). Similar but unrelated to 彳.

仁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 人 + semantic 二.

今.originText: An inverted 曰 ("to speak"), hence 亼 with a horizontal stroke at the bottom, so the inverted mouth means "not to speak". Another theory suggests that it depicts something in the mouth. Maybe the original form of 噤 or 吟. If so, the derivative 含 refers to the original word.

介.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}: {{zh-l|*人|person}} + two marks encompassing, indicating "in between". Folk etymology interprets the two marks as two components of an armor.
介.originText: 人 + two marks encompassing, indicating "in between". Folk etymology interprets the two marks as two components of an armor.

仏.originRaw: Used since the {{w|Northern and Southern dynasties}}. To avoid using the character {{lang|zh|佛}}, {{zh-l|某|someone}} is used instead; the character is {{Han compound|人|厶|alt1=亻|ls=ic|nocap=1}}, where {{lang|zh|厶}} is a variant form of {{lang|zh|某}}.
仏.originText: Used since the. To avoid using the character 佛, 某 is used instead; the character is Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 + semantic 厶, where 厶 is a variant form of 某.

components.sense: a person engaged in an official position

仕.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|人|alt1=⺅|士|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=s|c2=p|t1=person|t2=a person engaged in an official position}}. It is mainly used as a verb meaning "to serve."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
仕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 士 (a person engaged in an official position). It is mainly used as a verb meaning "to serve."

他.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (man) + phonetic 也. Corrupted form of 佗, which is found in.

付.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|alt1=亻|t1=person|又|t2=hand|ls=ic}} or {{Han compound|人|alt1=亻|t1=person|寸|t2=hand|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – to deliver, to give to someone.
付.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 又 (hand) or Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 寸 (hand) – to deliver, to give to someone.

仙.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 山 (mountain) — a person moving into a mountain to practise becoming immortal. Originally 僊. The current form is first attested in the clerical script of the Han dynasty.

代.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 弋

令.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|亼|卩|ls=ic}}. The upper part is an open mouth to convey the idea of giving orders, while the bottom part is a kneeling man. Compare [[兄]], in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders.
令.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 亼 + semantic 卩. The upper part is an open mouth to convey the idea of giving orders, while the bottom part is a kneeling man. Compare 兄, in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders.

以.originText: a person (人) carrying something. It is often simplified to 㠯 in pre-Qin ancient scripts. Today, the person is partly visible on the right (see also the stylization in 从). See also 重, in which a person is carrying a bag, 央, in which a person is carrying a pole, and 年, in which a person is carrying the harvest.

仰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 卬.

仲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 中 (middle).

件.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (man) + semantic 牛 (cow).

任.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 壬 – to carry on a shoulder pole. Note that its phonetic part 壬 may be the graphical representation of 任, depicting a shoulder pole rotated by 90 degrees.

企.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|止|t1=person|t2=foot}} – a person standing on tiptoes.
企.originText: Compound: 人 (person) + 止 (foot) – a person standing on tiptoes.

伎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 支.

伏.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|犬|t1=person|t2=dog|ls=ic}} – meaning “prostrate”.
* A dog at the side of a person.
* A person adopting the position of a dog.
伏.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 犬 (dog) – meaning “prostrate”.

伐.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|人|alt1=⺅|戈|ls=ic|t1=person|t2=spear}}. Based on the image of cutting a person’s neck with a spear, it expresses the meanings of "to cut off" or "to strike."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
伐.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 戈 (spear). Based on the image of cutting a person’s neck with a spear, it expresses the meanings of "to cut off" or "to strike."

休.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|t1=man|木|t2=tree|ls=ic}} – a man leaning against a tree, resting.
休.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (man) + semantic 木 (tree) – a man leaning against a tree, resting.

会.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{l|mul|會}}. From {{w|cursive script (East Asia)|cursive script}}.

伝.originRaw: From {{bor|zh|ja|伝}}. Limited to {{w|Northeast China}}. Recorded from as early as 1954.<ref>{{cite-book|en|author=Roar Bökset|url=https://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archivedate=2021-12-02|series=Stockholm East Asian Monographs|volume=11|year=2006|publisher=Stockholm University|title=Long Story of Short Forms: The Evolution of Simplified Chinese Characters|isbn=978-91-628-6832-1|page=97|pageurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01#page=101}}</ref>
伝.originText: From 伝. Limited to. Recorded from as early as 1954.

伯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 白.

伴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 半.

伸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (man) + phonetic 申.

伺.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|t1=person, man|司|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a person stands beside (attends), looks in.

何.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the {{w|oracle bone script}}, a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}}: a man carrying something on their shoulder – the original form of {{och-l|荷|id=3|gloss=to carry}}.

The object being carried may have been {{m|zh|戈}}, in which case the character is also an {{Han compound|人|戈|c1=s|c2=p|t1=person|t2=dagger-axe|ls=ic|ls2=psc|nocap=y}}.

In the {{w|bronze inscriptions}}, some forms of the character were {{Han compound|人|可|c1=s|c2=p|t1=person|ls=psc|nocap=y}}, from which the modern form derives.
何.originText: In the, a : a man carrying something on their shoulder – the original form of 荷. The object being carried may have been 戈, in which case the character is also an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 戈 (dagger-axe). In the, some forms of the character were Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 可, from which the modern form derives.

使.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 吏. However, the phonetic component should add part of the meaning since it represents a hand holding perhaps a flag to mean "representative, ambassador".

例.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 列.

侍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 寺.

供.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 共.

依.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (human) + phonetic 衣.

侵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
According to ''{{w|Shuowen Jiezi|Shuowen}}'', an {{Han compound|人|帚|又|t1=person|t2=broom|t3=hand|ls=ic|nocap=1}} – a person with a broom in hand.
侵.originText: According to ', an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 帚 (broom) + semantic 又 (hand) – a person with a broom in hand.

侶.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|人|alt1=⺅|呂|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=person}}.<!-- It expresses the meaning of “companion.”--><ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
侶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 呂.

便.originText: According to ', an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 更 (to change) – to change one's posture to make oneself comfortable. Alternatively, this may be the original character for 鞭, from Compound: 人 (person) + 𠓥 (whip), as seen in the bronze script.

係.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 系. The simplified form 系 also exists as a traditional character, and is also used to simplify 繫. In ancient times, 系, 係*, and 繫* were usually interchangeable graphic variants, although in some compounds, only one form is acceptable (e.g. 世系 and 繋辭). The meaning “yes” in Cantonese and Hakka is likely an independently created, only associated with this character by.

促.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 足.

俊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 夋.

俗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 谷 – customs of people.

保.originText: In the oracle script, this character was an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 子 (child) – a person carrying a child on his back; to carry (a child) > to protect. See also 好. In early bronze inscriptions, 爪 was added to the person to emphasize that the person was carrying the child. This was later simplified into one or two strokes. The current form has two.

信.originRaw:
{{Han etym}} {{Han compound|人|言|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc|t2=words}}.王國維 「桐郷徐氏印譜序」 『観堂集林』巻六 20頁。
方国瑜 「字説（六則）」 『師大国学叢刊』第1巻1期 1931年。
張世超、孫凌安、金国泰、馬如森 『金文形義通解』 中文出版社、1996年、487-488頁。
季旭昇撰 『説文新証』 芸文印書館、2014年、162-163頁。 {{Shuowen}} interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
信.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 人 + semantic 言 (words). interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.

修.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 攸 + semantic 彡.

俳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 非.

俺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 奄.

倉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, {{liushu|p|nocap=yes}}: a granary, depicting its roof ({{zh-l|*亼}}), a door ({{zh-l|*戶}}), and a pit for storing grain ({{zh-l|*口}}). Alternatively an {{Han compound|合|戶|t1=gather|t2=door|ls=ic|nocap=yes}} – a warehouse. The component {{zh-l|*戶}} corrupted into {{zh-l|*𠁣}} in Qin bamboo slips. This form was inherited in small seal script and was misinterpreted as cognate with the unrelated {{zh-l|*食}} in the {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}.
倉.originText: In oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, : a granary, depicting its roof (亼), a door (戶), and a pit for storing grain (口). Alternatively an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 合 (gather) + semantic 戶 (door) – a warehouse. The component 戶 corrupted into 𠁣 in Qin bamboo slips. This form was inherited in small seal script and was misinterpreted as cognate with the unrelated 食 in the.

候.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 + phonetic 矦, as 𠊱. The 矦 component (modified so that ⺈ becomes 乛 on top and 丿 at left becomes 丨) is an ancient form of 侯.

値.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 直. The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to stand upright." Associated with the character 直, it meant "to hit" or "to be correct," and by extension, it came to mean "value" or "worth."

偵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 貞 (to inquire). It expresses the idea of “asking” or “inquiring.”

僕.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

In the oracle bone script and the early Western Zhou bronze script, it was a {{liushu|p|nocap=1}} of a slave or prisoner, with hands holding a basket ({{zh-l|*其}}) to pick up garbage, an instrument of punishment ({{zh-l|*辛}}) above the head{{,}} and a tail ({{zh-l|*尾}}) to represent the slave's low status, akin to animals.

{{zh-l|*其}} later corrupts into {{zh-l|*甾}}, the hands ({{zh-l|*廾}}) move below {{zh-l|*辛}}, and the slave's body ({{zh-l|*人}}) moves to become the left component. Later, {{zh-l|*辛}} corrupts into {{zh-l|*丵}} (probably by fusing with {{zh-l|*甾}}) and combines with {{zh-l|*廾}} to give {{och-l|菐}}, which functions as a phonetic component.

In the current form, it is essentially a {{Han compound|人|菐|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=man|nocap=1}}.
僕.originText: In the oracle bone script and the early Western Zhou bronze script, it was a of a slave or prisoner, with hands holding a basket (其) to pick up garbage, an instrument of punishment (辛) above the head and a tail (尾) to represent the slave's low status, akin to animals. 其 later corrupts into 甾, the hands (廾) move below 辛, and the slave's body (人) moves to become the left component. Later, 辛 corrupts into 丵 (probably by fusing with 甾) and combines with 廾 to give 菐, which functions as a phonetic component. In the current form, it is essentially a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (man) + phonetic 菐.

僚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 尞.

{{Han compound|人|alt1=亻|t1=person|曾|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a kind of person (a Buddhist monk).
