元.originText: a figure with two lines 上 for a head (one connected to body, one above it), emphasizing the head.

兄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|儿|ls=ic}} to convey the idea of giving orders. The original meaning of "elder brother" refers to the fact that the elder brother gives order to the younger brothers and his sisters. Compare [[令]], in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders. Similar to [[欠]], in which there is a kneeling man with an open mouth.
兄.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 口 + semantic 儿 to convey the idea of giving orders. The original meaning of "elder brother" refers to the fact that the elder brother gives order to the younger brothers and his sisters. Compare 令, in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders. Similar to 欠, in which there is a kneeling man with an open mouth.

充.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|𠫓|儿|ls=ic|t1=a newborn|t2=standing person}} – A newborn grows to stand and become mature.
充.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𠫓 (a newborn) + semantic 儿 (standing person) – A newborn grows to stand and become mature.

兆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|水|人|t1=person|t2=water|t3=person|ls=p}} – two people fleeing with their backs to a flood ({{zh-ref|Yu Xingwu, 1999}}).

Some oracle bone script variants are written identically to {{zh-l|*化}} (one upright person and one upside-down person). {{zh-ref|Meng (2022)}} suggests that this variant uses {{zh-l|*化}} as a phonetic component due to their phonological connection in Old Chinese.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'', without access to oracle bone script, considered it a {{liushu|p|nocap=1}} of cracks formed on a heated tortoise shell or bone during divination.
兆.originText: Pictogram: 人 (person) + 水 (water) + 人 (person) – two people fleeing with their backs to a flood . Some oracle bone script variants are written identically to 化 (one upright person and one upside-down person). suggests that this variant uses 化 as a phonetic component due to their phonological connection in Old Chinese. ', without access to oracle bone script, considered it a of cracks formed on a heated tortoise shell or bone during divination.

先.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|止|儿|t1=foot|t2=person}} – to go forward.
先.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 止 (foot) + semantic 儿 (person) – to go forward.

光.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 火 (fire) + semantic 卩 (kneeling person) – fire over a person's head, emphasizing the shining of light (').

克.originText: Origin uncertain. Oracle bone and bronze forms consist of 由 (or simply 口) over a sideways-standing basin (see also 般). The sideways basin may signify overturning, extending to mean "to change"—representing the word 革.

免.originText: a man wearing a ceremonial hat. Then borrowed for abstract meanings. The derivative 冕 refers to the original word. See also 敖, 冒, and 美.

党.originRaw:
{{Han compound|尚|儿|c1=p|c2=s|t2=human|ls=psc}}.

Besides its original senses, it is used as a simplified substitute for the character {{zh-l|*黨}}.
党.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尚 + semantic 儿 (human). Besides its original senses, it is used as a simplified substitute for the character 黨.

入.originText: an arrowhead indicating "to enter". Compare 人.

全.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|入|玉|ls=ic|t2=jade}} – a whole piece of jade; pure jade.
全.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 入 + semantic 玉 (jade) – a whole piece of jade; pure jade.

八.originText: two bent lines indicating the original meaning of "to divide". This character is later borrowed to mean "eight" because of homonymy, making the original meaning obsolete (now represented by 分 and 別). Unrelated to the bottom part of 兵, 共, 具, and 興, in which it represents two hands holding an object. Also unrelated to 只 and 兑 in which it represents air coming out of a mouth. Unrelated to 貝. Eventually, unrelated to the bottom part of 其, 真, and 典, in which it represents the legs of a table.

公.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Yanzhou Museum 2015.08.13 15-15-43.jpg|thumb|100px|A {{zh-l|*瓮}} from the {{w|Longshan culture}} (also called Black Pottery Culture) {{defdate|3000 – 1900 BC}}.]]

The traditional interpretation as given by ''{{w|Han Feizi}}'' is that {{lang|zh|公}} is a compound of {{zh-l|*八}} (= {{zh-l|*背|to deviate; opposite}}) and {{zh-l|*厶}} (original form of {{zh-l|*私|individual; private}}), i.e. the opposite of “private” — “public”. This theory is supported by Sun Yirang and Qiang Kaiyun, despite the somewhat different shape of the bottom component from {{lang|zh|厶}}.

This is disputed in modern times by Gao Hongjin, who thinks that the {{lang|zh|八}} on top stands for {{zh-l|*分|to divide; to distribute}} and the bottom round component {{zh-l|*口}} symbolises a generic object. {{lang|zh|公}} thus represents “equally dividing resources so that they are '''communal'''”.

Another theory put forth by Zhu Fangpu is that {{lang|zh|公}} is a {{liushu|p|nocap=1}}, being the original form of {{och-l|瓮|a wide-mouthed round-bottomed [[jar]]}}, and later borrowed for the meanings of “public” and “male of older generation or higher rank”.
公.originText: The traditional interpretation as given by ' is that 公 is a compound of 八 (= 背) and 厶 (original form of 私), i.e. the opposite of “private” — “public”. This theory is supported by Sun Yirang and Qiang Kaiyun, despite the somewhat different shape of the bottom component from 厶. This is disputed in modern times by Gao Hongjin, who thinks that the 八 on top stands for 分 and the bottom round component 口 symbolises a generic object. 公 thus represents “equally dividing resources so that they are communal”. Another theory put forth by Zhu Fangpu is that 公 is a, being the original form of 瓮, and later borrowed for the meanings of “public” and “male of older generation or higher rank”.

六.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – perhaps a shed. Originally using the similar-sounding word {{och-l|廬|shed, cabin}} to represent the concept “six” (Liu Xinglong). Alternatively, it may be an ancient counting symbol.
六.originText: perhaps a shed. Originally using the similar-sounding word 廬 to represent the concept “six” (Liu Xinglong). Alternatively, it may be an ancient counting symbol.

共.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 廾 (two hands) + semantic 口 (an object) – holding up an object with two hands. Eventually 口 (not ) came to be written 廿 (not ), which later fused with 廾 to form the modern 共. Possibly the original form of 供.

兵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|斤|t1=a short axe|廾|t2=2 hands|ls=ic}} – a pair of hands holding a weapon. Unrelated to [[丘]].
兵.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 斤 (a short axe) + semantic 廾 (2 hands) – a pair of hands holding a weapon. Unrelated to 丘.

具.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 鼎 (cauldron) + semantic 廾 (two hands) – to prepare food. A semi-conservative variant 𥃲 is similar but unrelated to 算. mistakes the middle component to be 貝 and interprets the character as referring to currency.

典.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 冊 (books) + semantic 丌 (table) – (official) books on a table. Unrelated to 曲 and 曹.

兼.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|ic|rs=八}}: Hand {{zh-l|*又}} (as in {{zh-l|*肀}}) holding two grain stalks {{zh-l|*禾}}. Compare: {{zh-l|秉}}, a hand holding one plant.
兼.originText: 八: Hand 又 (as in 肀) holding two grain stalks 禾. Compare: 秉, a hand holding one plant.

内.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han simp|內}}. {{Han compound|入|冂|ls=ic|c1=s|c2=s|t1=to enter|t2=house}}. It originally conveyed the meaning of "to bring into the house," and by extension, came to mean "inside" or "within."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
内.originText: 內. Ideogrammic compound: semantic 入 (to enter) + semantic 冂 (house). It originally conveyed the meaning of "to bring into the house," and by extension, came to mean "inside" or "within."

円.originRaw:
Japanese simplification of [[圓]], via a simplified character similar to [[𠮚]].<ref>Toshinobu Sakaida, [http://www.akaenpitsu.gr.jp/kakioroshi001.pdf 円（圓）の異体字]</ref>

Specifically, starting in the beginning of the [[Meiji period]], the {{m|ja|員}} in the middle of the character was abbreviated to 丨 in handwriting. As time went on, the bottom stroke of 囗 gradually rose, until by the time of the adoption of the {{ja-glossary|shinjitai}} characters, it had reached or even surpassed the box's centre.
円.originText: Japanese simplification of 圓, via a simplified character similar to 𠮚. Specifically, starting in the beginning of the Meiji period, the 員 in the middle of the character was abbreviated to 丨 in handwriting. As time went on, the bottom stroke of 囗 gradually rose, until by the time of the adoption of the characters, it had reached or even surpassed the box's centre.

冊.originText: strung together. See also 侖, 扁, and 典. Similar but unrelated to 龠. The contemporary stylized form 册 is unrelated to 朋.

再.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Uncertain. There are some hypotheses:
* Xu Zhongshu: Bottom half of {{zh-l|*冓}}, {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a fish, then drawn in a similar way to 丙 (perhaps a fish tail). See {{zh-l|*魚}} and {{zh-l|*丙}}<ref name="漢語多功能字庫">[https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf/search.php?word=再 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「再」]</ref>
* Shizuka Shirakawa：{{liushu|p}} of tools used for weaving ropes.<ref name="漢語多功能字庫"/>
* Ji Xusheng: {{Han compound|ls=ic|魚|二|t1=fish|t2=two}} – to catch two fish at once ([[kill two birds with one stone]]).<ref name="說文新證">季旭昇《說文新證》 p316</ref> Compare the oracle bone script form of [[亟]].
* Xu Shen: {{Han compound|ls=ic|一|冓|t1=one|abb2=yes}} – to catch two fish at once.<ref>[https://www.zdic.net/hans/%E5%86%8D Shuowen Jiezi]</ref>
* {{Han compound|一|冓|ls=ic|t2=the shape of a basket repeatedly woven from bamboo}}. It signifies the concept of repeating something that was once done, conveying the meaning of "again."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>

冒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 冃 (hat) + semantic 目 (eyes). 冃 is the original form, 目 was added later. Original form of 帽. See also 敖, 免, and 美.

冗.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宀|儿|ls=ic|t1=roof|t2=person}} — a person at home without work to do.
冗.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + semantic 儿 (person) — a person at home without work to do.

冠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 冖 (hat) + phonetic 元 (head) + semantic 寸 (hand) – a hand putting a hat on the head. Earlier forms are Phono-semantic compound: semantic 冃 (hat) + phonetic 元.

冥.originText: Originally Ideogrammic compound: semantic 冖 (cloth cover) + semantic 日 (sun) + semantic 廾 (two hands) – "dark". The upper part of the character is 𠕾. The 廾 was later corrupted to 六. May also be a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 冖 + semantic 日 + semantic 廾 (').

冬.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Unclear. One hypothesis derives {{och-l|冬|tr=*tˤuŋ}} from the antenna-like upper part of an oracle-bone graph formerly read as {{zh-l|鼉}} (“crocodilian”) (e.g. {{w|甲骨文合集|合集}} 6163反, 7405反), but reinterpreted as {{och-l|螽|tr=*tuŋ}} (“katydid; locust”).<ref>羅睿晣（2025）。釋甲骨文的「鼉」字－兼論「冬」字構形可能來源。中國文字，(總第十四)，187-211。https://www.airitilibrary.com/Article/Detail?DocID=P20241129001-N202603170001-00009
</ref>

The word may be related to {{och-l|統|tr=*tʰˤuŋh}}(“thread-end; leading strand of silk”) and {{och-l|終|tr=*tuŋ}}.
冬.originText: Unclear. One hypothesis derives 冬 from the antenna-like upper part of an oracle-bone graph formerly read as 鼉 (“crocodilian”) (e.g. 甲骨文合集合集 6163反, 7405反), but reinterpreted as 螽 (“katydid; locust”). The word may be related to 統(“thread-end; leading strand of silk”) and 終.

冶.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 呂 (metal ingots) + semantic 刀 (ladle) + semantic 口 (a decorative component) — to cast metal. The ingots have simplified into 冫 (compare 金 where they appear as 丷) and the 刀 and 口 have combined together, forming the phonetic component 台.

冷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 仌 (ice) + phonetic 令 – cold as ice.

凄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 仌 (ice) + phonetic 妻.

凍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 仌 + phonetic 東.

凝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 仌 (ice) + phonetic 疑

凡.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – origin unknown. It consists of two vertical strokes of unequal length. In oracle bone script, it was primarily used as a phonetic component in {{och-l|*鳳|tr=*bəm}}. In some oracle bone forms of {{zh-l|*鳳}}, this component is written resembling {{zh-l|*戌}}.
凡.originText: origin unknown. It consists of two vertical strokes of unequal length. In oracle bone script, it was primarily used as a phonetic component in 鳳. In some oracle bone forms of 鳳, this component is written resembling 戌.

処.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 夂 + semantic 几 (table).

凶.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} and/or {{liushu|i}}- with the '[[凵]]' component representing a hole in the ground and with the '[[㐅]]' component (if an ideogram) indicating the existence of a hole and/or (if a pictogram) representing rock, mud, stone or bamboo in the hole. Alternately, could be derived from the upper component of '[[㚇]]'.
凶.originText: and/or - with the '凵' component representing a hole in the ground and with the '㐅' component (if an ideogram) indicating the existence of a hole and/or (if a pictogram) representing rock, mud, stone or bamboo in the hole. Alternately, could be derived from the upper component of '㚇'.

出.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 止 (foot) + semantic 凵 (cave) – to step out of a cave; to exit. Compare 各. By the, the character has lost its original shape. Based on the distorted form, ' mistakenly interprets the character as a pictogram of a plant (屮) growing outwards.

刀.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a knife. The original form was 𠚣, which can be found in a variant of [[利]], [[𥝢]] (in turn used on the top of the character [[黎]]).
刀.originText: a knife. The original form was 𠚣, which can be found in a variant of 利, 𥝢 (in turn used on the top of the character 黎).

刃.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: a {{och-l|*刀|knife}} with an emphasis mark on the blade.
刃.originText: a 刀 with an emphasis mark on the blade.

分.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|八|刀|ls=ic|t1=to separate|t2=knife}} – to separate with a knife.
分.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 八 (to separate) + semantic 刀 (knife) – to separate with a knife.

切.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 七 + semantic 刀 (knife).

刈.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally written as {{zh-l|*乂}}. Now {{Han_compound|乂|刀|alt2=刂|t1=to mow|t2=knife|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=y}}. The phonetic component originally indicates a sickle, hence it also adds part of the meaning.
刈.originText: Originally written as 乂. Now 乂刀刂. The phonetic component originally indicates a sickle, hence it also adds part of the meaning.

刊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 干 + semantic 刀 (knife).

刑.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|井|刀|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. Originally written as {{och-l|*㓝}}, the {{och-l|*井}} later corrupted into {{och-l|幵}}, forming {{och-l|*𠛬}}.
刑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 井 + semantic 刀. Originally written as 㓝, the 井 later corrupted into 幵, forming 𠛬.

列.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 歹 (skeletal remains) + semantic 刀 (knife) – to tear apart. The seal script form can be analyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𡿪 + semantic 刀 (knife).

初.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + semantic 刀 (knife; to cut) – start making clothes by cutting the cloth. The various 𢀰-shaped glyphs are or are evolved from.

判.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 半 + semantic 刀 (knife).

別.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|冎|刀|alt2=刂|ls=ic|t1=bone|t2=knife}}, hence [[𠛰]] – to cut up bone and flesh. Later, the character was stylized as 別. See also [[另]].
別.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 冎 (bone) + semantic 刀 (knife), hence 𠛰 – to cut up bone and flesh. Later, the character was stylized as 別. See also 另.

利.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|禾|t1=[[grain]]|刀|t2=[[knife]]|ls=ic}} – to reap grain ({{zh-l|*禾}}) with a knife ({{zh-l|*刀}}). See also the variant [[𥝢]], which appears on top of the character [[黎]].
利.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + semantic 刀 (knife) – to reap grain (禾) with a knife (刀). See also the variant 𥝢, which appears on top of the character 黎.

到.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 至 (to arrive) + phonetic 刀.

制.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|朱|刀|t1=tree|t2=knife|ls=ic}} – to cut a tree.
制.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 朱 (tree) + semantic 刀 (knife) – to cut a tree.

刷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 刀 (knife) + phonetic 㕞.

券.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|𠔉|刀|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=knife}} – contract. Ancient contracts were cut in half.
券.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𠔉 + semantic 刀 (knife) – contract. Ancient contracts were cut in half.

刺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朿 + semantic 刀 (knife).

刻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亥 + semantic 刀.

components.sense: ding, a bronze cauldron for cooking or sacrificial rituals

則.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 鼎 (ding, a bronze cauldron for cooking or sacrificial rituals) + semantic 刀 (knife); hence, the original version is 𠟭. Perhaps it's a reference to carving something (e.g., characters) with a knife on a bronze. Its original meaning was "rule; law". 鼎 was simplified to the unrelated 貝 in the small seal script. Compare 貞 (< 鼑), which underwent the same stylization.

削.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 肖 + semantic 刀.

前.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{zh-l|*歬}}, an {{Han compound|止|t1=foot|舟|t2=boat|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – a foot on a boat moving forward.

In the current form, {{zh-l|*止}} is simplified to {{zh-l|*䒑}} and {{zh-l|*舟}} to {{zh-l|*月}}. The current form with an additional {{zh-l|*刀|knife}} ([[𠝣]] > [[𣦃]] > 前) is the original form of {{och-l|剪|to cut}}.

Unrelated to [[俞]].
前.originText: Originally 歬, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 止 (foot) + semantic 舟 (boat) – a foot on a boat moving forward. In the current form, 止 is simplified to 䒑 and 舟 to 月. The current form with an additional 刀 (𠝣 > 𣦃 > 前) is the original form of 剪. Unrelated to 俞.

剖.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|刀|alt1=刂|咅|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=knife}}. It expresses the idea of cutting something in two with a knife.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
剖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 刀 (knife) + phonetic 咅. It expresses the idea of cutting something in two with a knife.

剛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 岡 + semantic 刀 (knife).

剝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 彔 + semantic 刀 (knife).

副.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 畐 + semantic 刀 (knife).

割.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 害 + semantic 刀.

創.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 倉 + semantic 刀 (knife) – wound.

劇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 豦 + semantic 刀 (knife).

力.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – alternative interpretation, either an arm bending out from the side of the body, or a wooden plough.
力.originText: alternative interpretation, either an arm bending out from the side of the body, or a wooden plough.

功.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 工 (labour; work) + semantic 力 (strength).

加.originText: ': Ideogrammic compound: semantic 力 (strength) + semantic 口 (mouth) — exaggerate; slander. Sun Changxu: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 力 (plowing) + semantic 口 (mouth) — to put more effort. 口 here indicates exclamations or breath associated with the effort.

劣.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 少 (little, less) + semantic 力 (strength).

助.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|且|力|t2=strong arm|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – to help with one’s strength.
助.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 且 + semantic 力 (strong arm) – to help with one’s strength.

努.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 力 (strength) + phonetic 奴 – exert one’s strength.

効.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 交 + semantic 力

劾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亥 + semantic 力 (power).

勃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 孛 + semantic 力 (power).

勇.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|甬|力|t2=strong|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – brave and strong.
勇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 甬 + semantic 力 (strong) – brave and strong.

勉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|免|力|t2=strong|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – make a strong effort.
勉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 免 + semantic 力 (strong) – make a strong effort.

動.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|重|力|c1=p|c2=s|t2=strength|ls=psc}}. However, the phonetic component is a reference to a heavy bag ready to be moved by a human being.
動.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 重 + semantic 力 (strength). However, the phonetic component is a reference to a heavy bag ready to be moved by a human being.

勘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|力|t1=strong|甚|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to look at carefully, strongly.
勘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 力 (strong) + phonetic 甚 – to look at carefully, strongly.

務.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敄 + semantic 力 (strength).

勝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朕 + semantic 力 (strength). Graphically, the character decomposes as Compound: 月 + 劵 (which gives rise to the simplified form 胜), though this is not the etymology.

募.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 莫 + semantic 力 (strength).

勢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 埶 + semantic 力 (power).

勾.originText: Variant of 句, via 口 → 厶.

包.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a fetus ({{l|zh|巳}}) in the womb ({{l|zh|勹}}), or a swaddled baby. ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' gives both interpretations.
包.originText: a fetus (巳) in the womb (勹), or a swaddled baby. ' gives both interpretations.

化.originText: of two 人, one upright (亻) and one upside down (𠤎) — reversal; change. ' also considers 𠤎 to be a phonetic component. Compare 并, 比, 卬, 尼 and 北.

北.originText: two men back to back. Originally meaning “back”; the character 背 refers to the original word. Compare 化, 比, 卬, and 尼.

匠.originText: Traditionally thought to be an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 匚 (box) + semantic 斤 (axe) (e.g. '). In more recent scholarship (e.g.; ), an alternative glyph origin has been proposed, suggesting that it is a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 匚 + semantic 斤 (axe).

匹.originText: Uncertain. Various theories have been proposed based on the evidence from the bronze inscriptions: ' considers it to be an Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 八 (eight) + semantic 匸 (to conceal) – unit of measuring cloth. 八 refers to eight folds in one 匹 of cloth (two bolts of cloth), and 匸 refers to concealing the two ends of the cloth when rolling it up. This interpretation is not likely since the older forms do not evidently have these components.

components.sense: that which hides; that which stores

医.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|匸|矢|t1=that which hides; that which stores|t2=arrow|ls=ic}}.
医.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 匸 (that which hides; that which stores) + semantic 矢 (arrow).

匿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 匸 (to conceal) + phonetic 若.

十.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In oracle-bone script, {{lang|zh|十}} is mostly written as a single vertical stroke; a few examples add a central dot, as in HJ 9204. Later forms added {{lang|zh|一}}, making a cross.

One view identifies it as the original graph of {{och-l|針|needle|tr=*kim}}, later borrowed for {{och-l|十|ten|tr=*gip}}. See {{och-l|針|tr=*kim}}.<ref>https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf/search.php?word=%E5%8D%81</ref>

Another view sees it as a knotted-cord or thread-joining form, cf. {{och-l|什|tr=*gip}} ({{zh-l|三蒼}} glosses it as “to gather”), {{zh-l|揖|tr=*ʔip}} (the {{zh-l|詩}} commentary glosses {{lang|zh|揖揖}} as “gathered”), {{zh-l|緝}} (“to join hemp fibres into thread”), and {{zh-l|輯}} (glossed in {{zh-l|說文}} as “to collect” and in {{zh-l|爾雅}} as “to harmonize”).

Unrelated to [[支]], [[卖]], [[直]], [[真]], [[德]], [[甫]], and [[七]], but related to the original form of [[丈]].
十.originText: In oracle-bone script, 十 is mostly written as a single vertical stroke; a few examples add a central dot, as in HJ 9204. Later forms added 一, making a cross. One view identifies it as the original graph of 針, later borrowed for 十. See 針. Another view sees it as a knotted-cord or thread-joining form, cf. 什 (三蒼 glosses it as “to gather”), 揖 (the 詩 commentary glosses 揖揖 as “gathered”), 緝 (“to join hemp fibres into thread”), and 輯 (glossed in 說文 as “to collect” and in 爾雅 as “to harmonize”). Unrelated to 支, 卖, 直, 真, 德, 甫, and 七, but related to the original form of 丈.

千.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 一 (one, signifying a number) + phonetic 人. The Old Chinese pronunciations of 千 and 人 were similar. For the component 人, compare its combining form 亻. The traditional explanation holds that the extra line indicates an extension (see the etymologies of 年 and 延). 千 has the meaning one thousand because one thousand is a number that is reached by extending one's counting.

升.originText: era bronze standard dipper measuring one 升 (sheng)]] of a dipper, compare 斗.

午.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} –  a [[pestle]] (now written {{zh-l|*杵}}). Unrelated to [[干]]. See the central component of [[舂]] and [[秦]] in their original version.
午.originText: a pestle (now written 杵). Unrelated to 干. See the central component of 舂 and 秦 in their original version.

半.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|八|牛|t1=to divide|t2=cow|ls=ic}} – to cut a cow into two halves.
半.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 八 (to divide) + semantic 牛 (cow) – to cut a cow into two halves.

卑.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|甲|𠂇|t1=fan|t2=hand}} - a man holding a fan, indicating that he is a servant.
卑.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 甲 (fan) + semantic 𠂇 (hand) - a man holding a fan, indicating that he is a servant.

卒.originText: There were 5 forms of 卒 in Shang oracle bone script (; ): # : same as 衣 (> Western Zhou bronze script ); # : a crisscross 衣 - a completed clothing; # (卒): : 衣 with a mark - a completed clothing to be folded (> Warring States bronze script; Chu slip and silk script ); # (𧙻): : 衣 + 聿 (hand (又) holding a brush); #,: 𧙻 having 又 omitted. The brush shape in form (5) was often placed upside down. Later the inverted brush shape was mistaken as 又 and then moved to the top as in Chu slip and silk script (𰠄) to avoid obscuration with 袁 (衣 + 又) .

卓.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}} of a child ({{l|zh|子}}) with a type of flag (ㅏ) on its head. ([[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#J|Ji Xusheng, 2004]]).

According to Zhang Shichao (張世超), the character represents a man (ㅏ) standing in a higher position on an altar illuminated by the sun ([[昜]]).

An ancient variant of the character is [[㔬]]. The child (or the altar) is now written in a way similar to {{zh-l|*早}} in the modern script.
卓.originText: of a child (子) with a type of flag (ㅏ) on its head. (Ji Xusheng, 2004). According to Zhang Shichao (張世超), the character represents a man (ㅏ) standing in a higher position on an altar illuminated by the sun (昜). An ancient variant of the character is 㔬. The child (or the altar) is now written in a way similar to 早 in the modern script.

協.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|十|劦|t2=to collaborate|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=p}} — a variant form of {{och-l|*劦}} with a phonetic {{och-l|*十}} added.<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref>
協.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 十 + phonetic 劦 (to collaborate) — a variant form of 劦 with a phonetic 十 added.

南.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|j}}: The oracle-bone form depicts a lidded {{zh-l|同|tube; cylindrical vessel}}. Some forms contain strokes inside the vessel, probably representing its contents. In Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, the {{zh-l|同}} element changed into {{zh-l|用}}. One proposal identifies this graph as the original character of {{zh-l|醓}} (“meat sauce; minced meat preserved in brine”).<ref>黄博.甲骨文“南”及相关字补说[J].出土文献,2020,(04):24-37+155.
</ref>

{{och-l|南|tr=*nˤəm}} may be related to {{och-l|腩|tr=*nˤəmʔ}} and {{och-l|納|tr=*nˤəp}} (“to put in; to receive”).
南.originText: The oracle-bone form depicts a lidded 同. Some forms contain strokes inside the vessel, probably representing its contents. In Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, the 同 element changed into 用. One proposal identifies this graph as the original character of 醓 (“meat sauce; minced meat preserved in brine”). 南 may be related to 腩 and 納 (“to put in; to receive”).

単.originText: 單吅𭕄. Compare 厳 (from 嚴).

博.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 十 (ten) + phonetic 尃.

占.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 卜 (divination) + semantic 口 (mouth).

印.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 爪 (hand) + semantic 卩 (kneeling person) – a hand suppressing a kneeling person. According to 羅振玉 in his book 《增訂殷墟書契考釋》(1915), the character is an ideogram of a hand suppressing a kneeling person. The character 抑 (to suppress) was used to preserve the original meaning.

components.sense: person on a cliff or mountain

危.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 厃 (person on a cliff or mountain) + semantic 卩 (kneeling person). Written like 𡴲 during the, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 山 (mountain).

即.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|皀|卩|ls=ic|t1=ancient round-mouthed food vessel|t2=to kneel}} – to come near to eat; to approach.
即.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 皀 (ancient round-mouthed food vessel) + semantic 卩 (to kneel) – to come near to eat; to approach.

却.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Variant of {{zh-l|卻*}}. The modern mainland China usage is of reform nature.
却.originText: Variant of 卻*. The modern mainland China usage is of reform nature.

卸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Omission of {{zh-l|*彳}} in {{zh-l|*御}}. {{och-l|午}} still gives the sound.
卸.originText: Omission of 彳 in 御. 午 still gives the sound.

厄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Possibly an {{liushu|2|nocap=yes}} of a person kneeling ({{zh-l|*卩}}), and a small stroke to accentuate the knee (now {{zh-l|*厂}}).<ref>季旭昇，2002《說文新證.下冊》，台北：藝文印書館，2002年10月第1版。p.72</ref> Not cognate with {{zh-l|戹}} (“yoke”) but eventually they shared meanings. 

{{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} interprets it as {{Han compound|厂|卪|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=joint; node|nocap=yes}} – {{w|Wood#Knots|wood knot}}.

<references/>
厄.originText: Possibly an of a person kneeling (卩), and a small stroke to accentuate the knee (now 厂). Not cognate with 戹 (“yoke”) but eventually they shared meanings. interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 厂 + semantic 卪 (joint; node) –.

厘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Variant of {{l|zh|釐}} by omitting the top part of it.
厘.originText: Variant of 釐 by omitting the top part of it.

厚.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|厂|𣆪|t1=cliff; cave on a cliff|t2=jug|ls=ic}}. According to Shuowen, 𣆪 is an inverted {{zh-l|*亯}}.
厚.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 厂 (cliff; cave on a cliff) + semantic 𣆪 (jug). According to Shuowen, 𣆪 is an inverted 亯.

原.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|泉|厂|t1=spring|t2=cliff|ls=ic}} – a spring bursting from a cliff-side – origin. A conservative variant is [[厡]], in which water is well visible at the bottom.
原.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 泉 (spring) + semantic 厂 (cliff) – a spring bursting from a cliff-side – origin. A conservative variant is 厡, in which water is well visible at the bottom.

去.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|大|t1=man|口|t2=mouth, object|ls=ic}}. Top figure simplified to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|土}}, unrelated to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|士||scholar, gentleman}}, while bottom simplified to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|厶}}; a conservative variant is [[厺]].

There are various interpretations of the combination of “man” and “mouth, object”. One is that the ideograph represented a man with a hole marked in his crotch, with the idea of “anus” (i.e. getting rid of) ({{zh-ref|Schuessler, 2007}}). Another is that it represented a man ''departing'' from a cave or city.

Alternatively, it may be the original character of {{och-l|呿|to open one's mouth}}, the meaning given by the combination of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|大||big}} and {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|口||mouth}}. The meaning “to depart” would be an extension of the meaning “to open one's mouth”, as the lips ''depart'' from each other when one's mouth is open.

{{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} interprets the character as a {{Han compound|大|𠙴|t1=man|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|nocap=1}}.

In addition, {{lang|zh|去}} is also the original character of {{och-l|盍|gloss=to cover}}. The {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|大}} could be a cover on top of an object {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|口}}.

The man on top is simplified as 土 as in [[赤]] and [[走]] (< [[𧺆]]).
去.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大 (man) + semantic 口 (mouth, object). Top figure simplified to 土, unrelated to 士, while bottom simplified to 厶; a conservative variant is 厺. There are various interpretations of the combination of “man” and “mouth, object”. One is that the ideograph represented a man with a hole marked in his crotch, with the idea of “anus” (i.e. getting rid of) . Another is that it represented a man departing from a cave or city. Alternatively, it may be the original character of 呿, the meaning given by the combination of 大 and 口. The meaning “to depart” would be an extension of the meaning “to open one's mouth”, as the lips depart from each other when one's mouth is open. interprets the character as a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 大 (man) + phonetic 𠙴. In addition, 去 is also the original character of 盍. The 大 could be a cover on top of an object 口. The man on top is simplified as 土 as in 赤 and 走 (< 𧺆).

参.originRaw: {{Han simp|參}}, which is in turn {{Han simp|曑|nocap=yes}}.
参.originText: 參, which is in turn 曑.

又.originText: a right hand. Original form of 右. Unrelated to 𠬤 (> 译). Often written as ⺕ in many modern characters such as 事, 聿, 雪, 急, 爭, 尹, and 建 (which is unrelated to 聿).

及.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|人|又|ls=ic|t1=person|t2=hand}} – a hand grabbing a person.
及.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 又 (hand) – a hand grabbing a person.

友.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 又 + phonetic 又 Shuowen: two hands, therefore friendship.

双.originRaw:
{{zh-etym-double|又|}}.

{{Han simp|䨇|f=雔|t= }}, which is also a [[w:Variant Chinese character|variant form]] of {{zh-l|雙*}}.

The earliest known record can be found in [[w:Ming dynasty|Ming dynasty]] {{lw|zh|pref=《|s:俗書刋誤_(四庫全書本)/卷01#嘗|俗書刊誤|suf=》}}.

The character {{l-self|zh|双}} bears superficial similarity to the early form of {{zh-l|友}}. However, the former is not a direct descendant of the latter.
双.originText: doubled 又. 䨇雔, which is also a variant form of 雙*. The earliest known record can be found in Ming dynasty 俗書刋誤四庫全書本卷嘗俗書刊誤. The character 双 bears superficial similarity to the early form of 友. However, the former is not a direct descendant of the latter.

反.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|又|厂|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=hand}}. The character originally depicted the action of turning the palm of the hand, and by extension, it came to mean "to return" or "to reverse."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
反.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 又 (hand) + phonetic 厂. The character originally depicted the action of turning the palm of the hand, and by extension, it came to mean "to return" or "to reverse."

叔.originText: Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 尗 (wooden stake) + semantic 又 (hand) – using a wooden stake to dig the ground. Later phonetically borrowed to mean "paternal uncle". The whole character is partly related to 建 since it represents a hand planting a wooden stake in the ground.

取.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 耳 (ear) + semantic 又 (hand) - to take the ear of fallen prey, a rite of hunters mentioned in the Rites of Zhou. 大獸公之小禽私之獲者取左耳 ' interprets it as taking the ear of an enemy instead. However, Wang (2022) points out that there is no evidence that this actually happened in war.

受.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Possibly a {{Han compound|爪|舟|又|t1=hand|t2=boat|t3=hand|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – to hand over.
受.originText: Possibly a Ideogrammic compound: semantic 爪 (hand) + semantic 舟 (boat) + semantic 又 (hand) – to hand over.

叙.originRaw: Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|敘|f=攴|t=又|nocap=y}} found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary {{w|Ganlu Zishu}} ({{lw|zh|干祿字書}}) and eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China. <!-- Note: Exact time period is unknown. Not found in 1956 《漢字簡化方案》 or 1964 《簡化字總表》 -->
叙.originText: Unorthodox variant 敘攴又 found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary (干祿字書) and eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China.

口.originText: resembles an open mouth. In the oracle bone script, radical 口 is used for characters having abstract meanings. Such a character can have a figurative meaning derived from the phonetic part, e.g. 右 = 又 + 口 and 𪪺 = 弓 + 口, or be an unrelated borrowing, e.g. 否 = 不 + 口.

古.originText: A shield (甲, contraction of 盾 and similar but unrelated to 中) and the radical of the mouth (口) both as a distinguishing mark and as a component that partly indicates pronunciation. Together, they indicate the concept of "strong, firm" (as strong as a shield); original form of 固 (Qiu Xigui, Ding Shan 丁山). Compare oracle bone forms with 干, 盾. Unrelated to 中 and hence to 史 and 使. finds evidence for the 十 component originally being a depiction of a piece of food and the character originally being a depiction of someone spitting out a piece of food due to his bad taste. Thus, Fang argues this character is the original form of 苦, "bitter".

句.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 丩 (to entangle) + phonetic 口, which may represent the tip of a big nail. The 丩 component, originally two entangled ropes, now resembles the unrelated 勹.

叫.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|丩|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mouth}}. According to Shuowen Jiezi, its original meaning was "to shout".
叫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 丩. According to Shuowen Jiezi, its original meaning was "to shout".

召.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 刀 + semantic 口 (mouth) – originally, to call out (with one’s mouth) or to serve wine for guests. Part of the second original meaning is preserved in 招. In the most ancient versions on some oracle bones, the character was totally different: it represented one or two hands over a wine vessel; the knife and mouth components were added later to this variant.

可.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|丂|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}} with a reference to exhaled air. Perhaps its original meaning was "to sing", then [[訶]] and [[哥]] (可 written twice).
可.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 丂 with a reference to exhaled air. Perhaps its original meaning was "to sing", then 訶 and 哥 (可 written twice).

台.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 㠯 + semantic 口 (mouth). An alternate variant of 㠯 (modern form: 以) in Chinese bronze inscriptions.

史.originText: 又 holding a stylized flag almost identical to 中 perhaps to indicate a representative or ambassador (see its variant 吏 used in 使 to mean "ambassador"). As an alternative, it holds either a pen or a hunting weapon resembling similar to 中. Hence, the inner component 中 is partly unclear. The whole character originally indicates the act of taking notes; today, it means "history". Compare 事.

右.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|又|口|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. Originally written as {{och-l|*又}} as a phonetic loan in the oracle bone script; in bronze inscriptions, a meaningless {{zh-l|*口}} component was added as a distinguishing mark.
右.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 又 + semantic 口. Originally written as 又 as a phonetic loan in the oracle bone script; in bronze inscriptions, a meaningless 口 component was added as a distinguishing mark.

号.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|口|丂|t1=mouth|t2=exhaled air; a tiger's cry}}. See {{och-l|*號}} for more details.
号.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + semantic 丂 (exhaled air; a tiger's cry). See 號 for more details.

司.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Inconclusive.
* Jì Xùshēng: {{liushu|ls=ic}} a mouth {{zh-l|*口}} giving orders and a scepter {{zh-l|*刁}} of authority. 
* Liú Xìnglóng interprets {{zh-l|*刁}} to be a hand instead. 
* Táng Lán: Originally the same character as {{zh-l|*后}}, which later diverged.
* ''{{w|Shuowen}}'': {{zh-l|*后}} flipped.

各.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|夂|口|ls=ic|t1=sole of foot}} – to come, to enter; original form of {{och-l|𢓜}} and {{och-l|格}}. The mouth could be referred to the entrance of a cavern or building (see [[高]], [[去]] and [[谷]]; however, this is not the case in [[向]]). Compare [[出]].
各.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 夂 (sole of foot) + semantic 口 – to come, to enter; original form of 𢓜 and 格. The mouth could be referred to the entrance of a cavern or building (see 高, 去 and 谷; however, this is not the case in 向). Compare 出.

合.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|亼|口|t2=mouth|ls=ic}} : Two mouths speaking together. See also [[會]].
合.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 亼 + semantic 口 (mouth) : Two mouths speaking together. See also 會.

吉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}} – originally {{zh-l|*圭}} and {{zh-l|*口}} in the oracle bone script. The top component mutated into {{zh-l|*士}} in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions.
吉.originText: originally 圭 and 口 in the oracle bone script. The top component mutated into 士 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions.

同.originText: a pipe — original form of 筒.

名.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 夕 (crescent moon) + semantic 口 (mouth) — to say one's own name to identify oneself in the dark. An alternative theory has been proposed based on Shang era texts. 口 was originally used to write both 口 and 名. 夕 standing for what later came to be written 明, was added as a phonetic indicator to disambiguate the two meanings.

后.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Multiple theories exist regarding its primary sense:

* One traditional view (e.g., ''{{w|Shuowen}}'') interprets it as a reversed form of {{och-l|司|to manage; to command}}, depicting a person issuing decrees from within (symbolized by {{och-l|口|mouth}}), with the original meaning of "sovereign; ruler" (such as the Xia dynasty rulers). However, this view is considered questionable in contemporary paleography.

* Another theory (e.g., [[w:Wang Guowei|Wang Guowei]]) posits a {{w|phonetic}} and {{w|semantic}} connection with {{och-l|毓|to give birth}}. Wang argued that the sense of "monarch" extended from the notion of {{lang|zh|繼嗣}} ("continuing the lineage"). Crucially, while the character {{och-l|毓}} graphically depicts a woman giving birth (a head-down delivery), the oracle bone form of {{lang|zh|后}} does not share this visual depiction; this connection is just phonological and etymological, rather than a direct graphic evolution.

* Recent epigraphic studies suggest that oracle bone forms of {{lang|zh|后}} and {{lang|zh|司}} were largely interchangeable, often functioning as {{lang|zh|司}} in sacrificial contexts rather than representing {{lang|zh|后}}. See also the ongoing debate regarding [[w:zh:后母戊鼎|{{lang|zh|后母戊鼎}}]].
后.originText: Multiple theories exist regarding its primary sense:

吏.originText: Alternative descendant of 叓, which is the ancient form of 事. Furthermore, both characters are related to 史, which was born as a variant without the horizontal stroke on top. The character should represent a hand holding a flag to mean "representative, ambassador"; see 使.

吐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 土.

向.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宀|口|t1=house|t2=mouth|ls=ic}}, echos in a place. The original form of {{och-l|響}}. It was borrowed to represent {{zh-l|*𠨍}} ({{zh-l|*嚮}}) later. The mouth does not represent an opening as in {{zh-l|*高}} and {{zh-l|*谷}}. Compare {{zh-l|*冋}}.
向.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 口 (mouth), echos in a place. The original form of 響. It was borrowed to represent 𠨍 (嚮) later. The mouth does not represent an opening as in 高 and 谷. Compare 冋.

君.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|尹|口|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. In the oracle bones and early Zhou bronze inscriptions, {{och-l|*君}} was often interchanged with {{och-l|*尹}}. ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' suggests that {{och-l|*口}} represents commands, but it may simply be decorative.
君.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尹 + semantic 口. In the oracle bones and early Zhou bronze inscriptions, 君 was often interchanged with 尹. ' suggests that 口 represents commands, but it may simply be decorative.

吟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 今.

否.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 不 (not) + semantic 口 (mouth). Similar to 咅.

含.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 今 + semantic 口 (mouth).

吸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|t1=mouth|及|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to inhale through the mouth. Note that 及 originally derives from “grab”, hence connotations of “grab through the mouth, inhale”.
吸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 及 – to inhale through the mouth. Note that 及 originally derives from “grab”, hence connotations of “grab through the mouth, inhale”.

吹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|口|欠|t1=mouth|t2=blow}} according to oracle bones and bronzes. An archaic variant of this character is [[龡]].
吹.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + semantic 欠 (blow) according to oracle bones and bronzes. An archaic variant of this character is 龡.

呂.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Ji Xusheng (2014): {{liushu|p}}: two blocks of metal. Original form of {{och-l|鋁|ingot}}. Later incorporated into {{och-l|*金|metal}} as a semantic component.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets it as a pictogram of two [[vertebrae]]. However, the two blocks were originally disconnected, and the connecting line was only added in the seal script.

The character has been {{Han phonetically borrowed}} to represent {{och-l|膂|spine}} and {{och-l|呂|music notes}}. The character was later also borrowed and stylized for {{och-l|予|I; give}}.
呂.originText: Ji Xusheng (2014): : two blocks of metal. Original form of 鋁. Later incorporated into 金 as a semantic component. ' interprets it as a pictogram of two vertebrae. However, the two blocks were originally disconnected, and the connecting line was only added in the seal script. The character has been to represent 膂 and 呂. The character was later also borrowed and stylized for 予.

呈.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|𡈼|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. The bottom component is not to be confused with {{l|zh|壬}} or {{l|zh|王}}.
呈.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 𡈼. The bottom component is not to be confused with 壬 or 王.

呉.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|吳}}.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
呉.originText: Variant of 吳. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

告.originRaw:
{{Han etym}} Unclear. Theories include: * Zhongshu Xu: {{liushu|p}}: tongue sticking out from the mouth.徐中舒 「怎様考釈古文字」 『古文字学論集』初編 香港中文大学、1983年、7-20頁。
張玉金 「論殷商時代的祰祭」 『中国文字』新30期 藝文印書館、2005年、1-30頁。 * Meilan Chen: {{Han compound|ls=ic|壴|口|abb1=y}}, hence a decorated drum and an open mouth.陳美蘭 「説“告”」 『中正漢学研究』2013年2期 中正大学中国文学系、2013年。 ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets it as 牛 + 口; however, {{w|Yu Xingwu}} points out that the top component is unrelated to [[牛]], as can be seen in the oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions.于省吾主編 『甲骨文字詁林』 中華書局、1996年、689頁。
告.originText: Unclear. Theories include: ' interprets it as 牛 + 口; however, points out that the top component is unrelated to 牛, as can be seen in the oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions.

周.originText: Oracle bone script: : a jade artifact with carved patterns. Original form of 彫. The character was later borrowed as a country name and 口 was added as a distinguishing mark. A semi-conservative version in which the carvings are visible is 𠕛. The top part of the character gradually became similar to 用 in the late Western Zhou period. See also 黃, which could have a reference to a jade artifact. Folk etymology interprets the seal script form as 口 + 用, indicating the idea of using words skillfully to express oneself, thereby implying the meaning of being meticulous or detailed.

呪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
A derivative ({{zh-l|*分化}}): variant form of {{och-l|祝}} — to pray<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref>.
呪.originText: A derivative (分化): variant form of 祝 — to pray.

味.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 未.

呼.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|t1=mouth|乎|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to exhale, call, or shout from the mouth.
呼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 乎 – to exhale, call, or shout from the mouth.

命.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 令. Doublet of 呤.

和.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|禾|口|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=mouth}} – harmony. The original version was [[龢]], with the radical of the flute [[𠎤]] (> [[龠]]) in its either archaic or contracted version perhaps to indicate the abstract concept of harmony through harmony in music.
和.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 禾 + semantic 口 (mouth) – harmony. The original version was 龢, with the radical of the flute 𠎤 (> 龠) in its either archaic or contracted version perhaps to indicate the abstract concept of harmony through harmony in music.

咲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|口|关|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mouth|t2=to laugh}}. It was the original form of [[笑]], meaning "to laugh." In Japan, it is used to represent the idea of flowers blooming.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
咲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 关 (to laugh). It was the original form of 笑, meaning "to laugh." In Japan, it is used to represent the idea of flowers blooming.

咽.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|t1=mouth|因|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – connected to the mouth, the throat.
咽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 因 – connected to the mouth, the throat.

哀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 衣 + semantic 口 (mouth).

品.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}: {{zh-etym-triple|口}}, representing various objects. Also occurs in {{zh-l|*區}}.
品.originText: tripled 口, representing various objects. Also occurs in 區.

員.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|〇|鼎|c1=p|c2=s|tr1={{och-retrieve-pron|圓}}|t1=circle|t2=[[ding]]}}.

The {{och-l|*〇}} is an ideogram of a circle. This character is an intermediate form of {{och-l|圓|circle}} which has been borrowed for the word {{och-l|員|many people|id=1}}.

The {{och-l|*鼎}} corrupted into {{och-l|*貝}} in the seal script. ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' misinterprets it as {{och-l|*口}} + {{och-l|*貝}}. See {{och-l|*則}} where a similar change has occurred.
員.originText: {{Han compound|ls=psc|〇|鼎|c1=p|c2=s|tr1=圓|t1=circle|t2=ding}}. The 〇 is an ideogram of a circle. This character is an intermediate form of 圓 which has been borrowed for the word 員. The 鼎 corrupted into 貝 in the seal script. ' misinterprets it as 口 + 貝. See 則 where a similar change has occurred.

哲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In [[bronze]] [[script]], written as {{zh-l|悊}} and other variants, with no evidence of the existence of {{zh-l|哲}} until [[small]] [[seal script]]. In ''{{zh-l|說文解字}}'', described as a {{Han compound|折|口|t2=mouth|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=1}} .
哲.originText: In bronze script, written as 悊 and other variants, with no evidence of the existence of 哲 until small seal script. In 說文解字, described as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 折 + semantic 口 (mouth).

哺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 甫.

唄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 貝.

唆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 夋.

唇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 辰 + semantic 口 (mouth).

唐.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|庚|口|c1=p|c2=s|t2=mouth|ls=psc|tr1=*lˤaŋ|tr=*kˤraŋ}}. {{zh-l|*口}} functions as a differentiating mark (cf. {{zh-l|*古}}/{{zh-l|*固}}), not as semantic "mouth." The graph abstracts some property — likely "hollowness" or "spatial openness" — from {{zh-l|*庚}}, a pictograph of a hollow percussion/ritual instrument. Used in oracle bones for Shang king {{w|Cheng Tang}}.
唐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 庚 + semantic 口 (mouth). 口 functions as a differentiating mark (cf. 古/固), not as semantic "mouth." The graph abstracts some property — likely "hollowness" or "spatial openness" — from 庚, a pictograph of a hollow percussion/ritual instrument. Used in oracle bones for Shang king.

唯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|口|隹|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mouth|ls=psc|tr2={{och-retrieve-pron|鷕}}}}. Original form of {{och-l|鷕|cry of a bird}}.<ref>布之道『[http://www.kaom.net/sgy_bzd.php 廣韻形聲考]』</ref> Phonetically borrowed for abstract meanings.
唯.originText: {{Han compound|口|隹|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mouth|ls=psc|tr2=鷕}}. Original form of 鷕. Phonetically borrowed for abstract meanings.

唱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 昌.

唾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 垂.

商.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

The formation is unclear. The base component is consistently {{zh-l|*丙}}; late-period variants add {{zh-l|*口}} below. The element placed atop {{zh-l|*丙}} varies:

# Inverted triangle with a horizontal bar.
# {{zh-l|*辛}}-like form: as type 1, but the tip extends a vertical stroke downward to {{zh-l|*丙}}, with the bar crossing this stroke.
# Bare inverted triangle (▽); possibly the original form of {{zh-l|*樴}}.
# Two instances of type 1 or 2, placed symmetrically left and right.
# Paired round or teardrop-shaped elements, each trailing a stroke down toward {{zh-l|*丙}}.
# {{zh-l|*辛}}-form with star-shaped marks in its quadrants (two or four); possibly a dedicated graph for the Shāng star.

In oracle bone and early Western Zhou bronze script, {{zh-l|*賞}} is written as {{zh-l|*商}} over {{zh-l|*貝}}; by mid-Western Zhou the upper part is replaced by {{zh-l|*尚}}.
商.originText: The formation is unclear. The base component is consistently 丙; late-period variants add 口 below. The element placed atop 丙 varies: # Inverted triangle with a horizontal bar. # 辛-like form: as type 1, but the tip extends a vertical stroke downward to 丙, with the bar crossing this stroke. # Bare inverted triangle (▽); possibly the original form of 樴. # Two instances of type 1 or 2, placed symmetrically left and right. # Paired round or teardrop-shaped elements, each trailing a stroke down toward 丙. # 辛-form with star-shaped marks in its quadrants (two or four); possibly a dedicated graph for the Shāng star. In oracle bone and early Western Zhou bronze script, 賞 is written as 商 over 貝; by mid-Western Zhou the upper part is replaced by 尚.

問.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 門 + semantic 口.

善.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally written {{zh-l|譱}} in {{w|bronze inscriptions}}, consisting of two {{och-l|言}} and one {{zh-l|*羊}}. The {{och-l|言}} might have served as the phonetic component, while {{zh-l|*羊}} represented the sense "good; beautiful" (see {{zh-l|*祥}}, {{zh-l|*義}}). The small seal script of {{lang|zh|善}} was simplified from the bronze inscription form, consisting of one {{zh-l|*言}} below one {{zh-l|*羊}}.

According to ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', the form
{{zh-l|譱}} is an {{Han compound|誩|羊|ls=ic|t1=to wrangle|t2=sheep|nocap=1}} – good; virtuous. This interpretation may be difficult to comprehend.
善.originText: Originally written 譱 in, consisting of two 言 and one 羊. The 言 might have served as the phonetic component, while 羊 represented the sense "good; beautiful" (see 祥, 義). The small seal script of 善 was simplified from the bronze inscription form, consisting of one 言 below one 羊. According to ', the form 譱 is an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 誩 (to wrangle) + semantic 羊 (sheep) – good; virtuous. This interpretation may be difficult to comprehend.

喉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 侯.

喚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 奐.

喜.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 壴 (drum) + semantic 口 (mouth). Duplicated character: 囍.

喝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 曷.

喩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 兪.

喪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{Han compound|桑|㗊|c1=p|c2=s|t1=mulberry tree|t2=many mouths|ls=psc|nocap=y}}. The number of mouths frequently varied. Sometimes {{zh-l|*走|run}} was included as a semantic component, and later {{och-l|亡|die}} was added as a phonetic (and also possibly semantic) component.

In the {{w|seal script}} became {{Han compound|哭|亡|c1=s|c2=p|t1=cry|t2=die|ls=psc|ls2=ic|nocap=y}}, from which the modern form derives.

Compare {{zh-l|*咢}} and {{zh-l|*噩}}, which may be derived from or originally the same character as 喪.
喪.originText: Originally Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 桑 (mulberry tree) + semantic 㗊 (many mouths). The number of mouths frequently varied. Sometimes 走 was included as a semantic component, and later 亡 was added as a phonetic (and also possibly semantic) component. In the became Phono-semantic compound: semantic 哭 (cry) + phonetic 亡 (die), from which the modern form derives. Compare 咢 and 噩, which may be derived from or originally the same character as 喪.

喫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 契.

嗅.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han simp|齅|f=鼻|t=口}}; in current form: {{Han compound|口|臭|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}.
嗅.originText: 齅鼻口; in current form: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 臭.

嗣.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|口|冊|司|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=s|c3=p|t1=mouth|t2=document}}. It originally referred to appointing the successor to the ruler through speech and documents, and by extension, expresses the idea of “succeeding.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
嗣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + semantic 冊 (document) + phonetic 司. It originally referred to appointing the successor to the ruler through speech and documents, and by extension, expresses the idea of “succeeding.”

嘆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|口|歎|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mouth}}. It expresses the idea of feeling down and letting out a sigh.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
嘆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 歎. It expresses the idea of feeling down and letting out a sigh.

嘲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 朝.

器.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Uncertain.
The classical interpretation is an {{liushu|ic|nocap=1}}: a {{zh-l|*犬|dog}} guarding four {{zh-l|*口|vessels}}. 

It might also be a phonetically borrowed character, originally meaning “to [[bark#Verb|bark]]” (Compare {{zh-l|*狺}}).

Another theory states the character is derived from {{zh-l|*喪|mourning}}. (Compare {{zh-l|*噩}}, {{zh-l|*哭}} , {{zh-l|*咢}}). Borrowed not for sound but as an {{liushu|i|nocap=1}} referring to a funerary urn.
器.originText: Uncertain. The classical interpretation is an : a 犬 guarding four 口. It might also be a phonetically borrowed character, originally meaning “to bark” (Compare 狺). Another theory states the character is derived from 喪. (Compare 噩, 哭, 咢). Borrowed not for sound but as an referring to a funerary urn.

噴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + phonetic 賁

嚇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 口 + phonetic 赫.

囚.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|囗|t1=box, enclosure|人|t2=person|ls=ic}} – an enclosed person: confinement, prisoner. Similar but unrelated to [[因]]. Unrelated to [[𥁕]].
囚.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 囗 (box, enclosure) + semantic 人 (person) – an enclosed person: confinement, prisoner. Similar but unrelated to 因. Unrelated to 𥁕.

四.originText: a nose exhaling. Original form of 呬. Later to represent 四. The word "four" was written as 亖 before and 四 appeared in late. This alternative form was used to prevent confusion of 亖 and 二 or 三 in vertical writing. It was standardized in.

因.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 囗 (sheet) + semantic 大 (person) – man on a mattress. Original form of 裀 or 茵. Alternatively, possibly an of a man wearing clothing.

困.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|囗|木|ls=ic|t1=surround|t2=wood}}. Probably the original form of {{och-l|梱|doorsill}} and {{och-l|閫|doorsill}}.
困.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 囗 (surround) + semantic 木 (wood). Probably the original form of 梱 and 閫.

囲.originRaw: Variant form.<ref>{{cite-book|en|author=Roar Bökset|url=https://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archivedate=2021-12-02|series=Stockholm East Asian Monographs|volume=11|year=2006|publisher=Stockholm University|title=Long Story of Short Forms: The Evolution of Simplified Chinese Characters|isbn=978-91-628-6832-1|page=36|pageurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01#page=40}}</ref> {{Han compound|囗|井|lang=ja|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|t1=surround|tr=i|tr2=i}}.
囲.originText: Variant form. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 囗 (surround) + phonetic 井.

固.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 囗 + phonetic 古.

国.originRaw: {{Han simp|國|f=或|t=玉}}. Also compare <big>{{zh-l|囯}}</big>, an unorthodox variant of {{l|mul|國}} that contains {{zh-l|王*|[[king]]}} instead of {{zh-l|玉*|[[jade]]}}.
国.originText: 國或玉. Also compare 囯, an unorthodox variant of 國 that contains 王* instead of 玉*.

圏.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{l|zh|圈}} with bottom component of {{l|zh|卷}} written {{l|zh|己}} instead of {{l|zh|㔾}}.
圏.originText: Unorthodox variant of 圈 with bottom component of 卷 written 己 instead of 㔾.

園.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 囗 (fence) + phonetic 袁.

土.originText: Pictogram 象形: a mound of earth. In oracle-bone inscriptions, it could also refer to the soil deity, serving as the original graph of 社. The mound later became narrowed or pointed at both ends, with the broad middle part developing into the horizontal stroke. Unrelated to the top component of 夌, 走, and 周; also unrelated to the central component of 金 and the overall character 圭.

在.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 才 + phonetic 士. In the oracle bone script and some of the bronze inscriptions, 才 is phonetically borrowed to represent this word; a phonetic 士 was added later. 士 eventually corrupted into 土.

地.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|土|也|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth|ls=psc}}. One of the first versions of this character is [[𡓬]] (> [[墬]]), in which a hill, a pig and a mound of earth are visible; visually, the upper part of the variant is [[䧘]].
地.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 也. One of the first versions of this character is 𡓬 (> 墬), in which a hill, a pig and a mound of earth are visible; visually, the upper part of the variant is 䧘.

坂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 + phonetic 反.

均.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 匀.

坊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 方.

坑.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In its current form, a {{Han compound|ls=psc|nocap=1|亢|土|c1=p|c2=s|t2=soil}}. Early forms appear to be {{lang|zh|阬}}.
坑.originText: In its current form, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亢 + semantic 土 (soil). Early forms appear to be 阬.

坪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 平.

垂.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Originally 𡍮. {{Han compound|ls=p|𠂹|土}}, flowers hanging from a plant.
垂.originText: Originally 𡍮. Pictogram: 𠂹 + 土, flowers hanging from a plant.

型.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|刑|土|t2=earth|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – an earthen mold, hence form, pattern.
型.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 刑 + semantic 土 (earth) – an earthen mold, hence form, pattern.

垣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 亘.

埋.originText: Originally written 薶, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (plant) + phonetic 貍. Later changed to 埋, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 里.

城.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|土|成|c1=s|c2=p|t1=soil|ls=psc}}, since city walls were originally made of stamped earth.
城.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (soil) + phonetic 成, since city walls were originally made of stamped earth.

域.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 + phonetic 或.

執.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|㚔|丮|t1=criminal / handcuffs|t2=hand|ls=ic}}: to [[arrest]]. In the present form, {{zh-l|㚔}} and {{zh-l|丮}} have been replaced by {{zh-l|幸}} and {{zh-l|丸}}, respectively.
執.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㚔 (criminal / handcuffs) + semantic 丮 (hand): to arrest. In the present form, 㚔 and 丮 have been replaced by 幸 and 丸, respectively.

培.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 咅.

基.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|其|土|t2=earth|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a foundation of earth.
基.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 其 + semantic 土 (earth) – a foundation of earth.

埼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 奇.

堀.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|土|屈|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth}}. It conveys the meaning of digging a hole in the ground.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
堀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 屈. It conveys the meaning of digging a hole in the ground.

堂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尚 + semantic 土.

堅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臤 + semantic 土.

堆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|土|隹|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth}}. The original form is {{zh-l|*𠂤}}.
堆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 隹. The original form is 𠂤.

堤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (soil) + phonetic 是.

堪.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|ls2=ic|土|甚|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth|t2=extreme, profound}} — originally meaning “heavy mountain/earthen protrusion”, it later came to signify the act of “enduring” that earth's weight.
堪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 甚 (extreme, profound) — originally meaning “heavy mountain/earthen protrusion”, it later came to signify the act of “enduring” that earth's weight.

報.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|㚔|𠬝|ls=ic|t1=handcuffs|t2=to subdue}} – to convict; to punish; to declare guilty.
報.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㚔 (handcuffs) + semantic 𠬝 (to subdue) – to convict; to punish; to declare guilty.

場.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 昜.

塊.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|土|鬼|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth; dust}} – clod of dirt.
塊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth; dust) + phonetic 鬼 – clod of dirt.

塑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朔 + semantic 土 (earth).

塔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 + phonetic 荅.

塗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 涂 + semantic 土 (earth; dirt).

塚.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|土|t1=earth|冢|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – an earthen mound, a tomb of earth.
塚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 冢 – an earthen mound, a tomb of earth.

塞.originText: Oracle bone script: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 工 (two items) + semantic 廾 (two hands) – stuffing the house with items. Hence, the original version is 𡨄, a character similar but unrelated to 共 but partly related to 展. ': Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𡨄 + semantic 土 (soil); the bottom component was added later.

塩.originRaw: Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|鹽|f=臣|t=土|f2=鹵|t2=口|nocap=y}}. In the 1946 {{w|Tōyō kanji}} list.
塩.originText: Japanese shinjitai 鹽臣土鹵口. In the 1946 list.

塾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 孰 + semantic 土 (soil).

境.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 竟.

墓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 莫 + semantic 土.

増.originRaw:
Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|增|f=曾|t=曽|nocap=1}}.

The current form is a {{Han compound|土|曽|lang=ja|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=earth|nocap=1}}.
増.originText: Japanese shinjitai 增曾曽. The current form is a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 曽.

墜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 隊 + semantic 土.

墨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 黑 + semantic 土 (soil).

墳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 + phonetic 賁.

墾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 貇 + 土 (earth/soil).

壁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|土|t1=earth|辟|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – an earthen wall.
壁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 辟 – an earthen wall.

壇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 土 + phonetic 亶.

士.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a war axe. Later, it took the meaning of "soldier" and eventually "officer, intellectual". Partly related to [[王]] since in at least two characters it should represent a ritual axe, perhaps made of jade: in fact, it is related to [[圭]] and [[金]] despite their appearance.
士.originText: a war axe. Later, it took the meaning of "soldier" and eventually "officer, intellectual". Partly related to 王 since in at least two characters it should represent a ritual axe, perhaps made of jade: in fact, it is related to 圭 and 金 despite their appearance.

壱.originRaw: Found in {{w|Zhongwen Da Cidian}} <big>《中文大辭典》</big>, a dictionary published in Taiwan from 1962 to 1968 that is based on the Japanese {{w|Dai Kan-Wa Jiten}}.
壱.originText: Found in 《中文大辭典》, a dictionary published in Taiwan from 1962 to 1968 that is based on the Japanese.

変.originText: Variant of 變. 變䜌亦

夏.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Some scholars identify an oracle bone character {{Han compound|日|頁|ls=ic|t1=sun|t2=head; man|nocap=1}} as this character – a man under the scorching sun; summer. However, it only appears as a diviner's name, making the identification uncertain.

In {{w|Spring and Autumn period}} bronze inscriptions, various variants appeared. {{zh-l|*止|foot}} was often added below the man, and in some forms {{zh-l|*日}} was removed while {{zh-l|*𦥑|two hands}} was added. The seal script inherits from the latter form, with {{zh-l|*止}} replaced by the related {{zh-l|*夊}}.

{{w|Warring States period}} forms also varied. The bamboo and silk script above shows a common form: {{Han compound|日|止|頁}}. The "ancient script" ({{zh-l|*古文}}) in ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' (labelled as large seal script) has deviated significantly, with {{zh-l|*止}} becoming {{zh-l|*足}} and the top part possibly a corruption of {{zh-l|*頁}}.

The current form derives from the seal script, with {{zh-l|*𦥑}} and the legs of {{zh-l|*頁}} removed. Unrelated to [[复]].
夏.originText: Some scholars identify an oracle bone character Ideogrammic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + semantic 頁 (head; man) as this character – a man under the scorching sun; summer. However, it only appears as a diviner's name, making the identification uncertain. In bronze inscriptions, various variants appeared. 止 was often added below the man, and in some forms 日 was removed while 𦥑 was added. The seal script inherits from the latter form, with 止 replaced by the related 夊. forms also varied. The bamboo and silk script above shows a common form: Compound: 日 + 止 + 頁. The "ancient script" (古文) in ' (labelled as large seal script) has deviated significantly, with 止 becoming 足 and the top part possibly a corruption of 頁. The current form derives from the seal script, with 𦥑 and the legs of 頁 removed. Unrelated to 复.

夕.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} — [[moon]] [[crescent]]. Compare to its ancient variant {{zh-l|*月}}.
夕.originText: moon crescent. Compare to its ancient variant 月.

外.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 卜 + phonetic 月. According to ja, it is also an; 月 originally represents a crescent moon (i.e. the moon with part “missing” to the observer). The character is thus interpreted as representing divination based on the partial phase of the moon, implying the remaining visible part of the moon is the moon's ‘outside’. In oracle bone script, 外 was written identical to 卜, but they were distinguished by the fact that 卜 has a horizontal bar extending to the inside of the tortoise shell, while 外 has a horizontal bar extending to the outside.

多.originText: two pieces of meat (肉). In the bronze script, 肉 was corrupted into 夕 due to visual similarity, making 多 into a doubled 夕 (nocap=y). The form with 夕 was inherited in later scripts. suggests that meat is scarce in ancient times, so two pieces of meat is a lot, citing a passage from ': 七十者可以食肉矣 Chang Ping-chuan suggests that it is the duplicative nature of the character that gives the meaning of "many", just like in 林, from 木.

夜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亦 + semantic 夕 (moon). 夕 may also serve as another phonetic component. In the modern form, the phonetic 亦 is distorted into Compound: 亠 + 亻 + ㇏, with the right-falling stroke ㇏ merging into the semantic 夕.

夢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the {{w|Oracle bone script}}, a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} or {{liushu|ic|nocap=y}} – a person ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|人}}) lying on a bed ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|爿}}), sometimes with restless hands (compare the oracle-bone character for {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|丮}}) and sometimes with the eye ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|目}}) emphasized.

In the {{w|Bronze inscriptions}}, the eye ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|目}}) has eyebrows above it (compare {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|眉}}), and the person's body is attached underneath, now written as two dots on either side. The bed is no longer present, and instead {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|夕|t=moon; night}} has been added.

In the modern form 夢, the eyebrows are written {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|卝}}, the eyes are written {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|罒}}, and the person's body has become {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|冖}}, while {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|夕}} remains on the bottom.

According to ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', it is a {{Han compound|瞢|夕|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=y}}.
夢.originText: In the, a or – a person (人) lying on a bed (爿), sometimes with restless hands (compare the oracle-bone character for 丮) and sometimes with the eye (目) emphasized. In the, the eye (目) has eyebrows above it (compare 眉), and the person's body is attached underneath, now written as two dots on either side. The bed is no longer present, and instead 夕 has been added. In the modern form 夢, the eyebrows are written 卝, the eyes are written 罒, and the person's body has become 冖, while 夕 remains on the bottom. According to ', it is a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 瞢 + semantic 夕.

大.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: a person facing forward. Original form of {{och-l|夫|man}}, phonetically borrowed for {{och-l|大|big}}. Compare {{och-l|*人}}, which represents the profile of a person.

Often explained as an ideogram of a person with outstretched arms; however, the ancient scripts do not show stretching.

Compare with {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|尢}}, which is a man with bent legs. Compare also {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|立}}, similar to {{lang|zh|大}}, and {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|交}}, in which the legs are crossed. Compare also {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|文}}, which is a man with arms outstretched and a crest or tattoo on his chest, and to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|夭}}, which is a man with arms outstretched and leaning to side (running or marching vigorously).

See the top component of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|泰}} in the original version ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𡙌}}), the top component of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|赤}} and the bottom component of [[奐]] (well visible in some fonts). Related to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|太}}.

Unrelated to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|买}}, in which the bottom component is the stylization of a cowrie.
大.originText: a person facing forward. Original form of 夫, phonetically borrowed for 大. Compare 人, which represents the profile of a person. Often explained as an ideogram of a person with outstretched arms; however, the ancient scripts do not show stretching. Compare with 尢, which is a man with bent legs. Compare also 立, similar to 大, and 交, in which the legs are crossed. Compare also 文, which is a man with arms outstretched and a crest or tattoo on his chest, and to 夭, which is a man with arms outstretched and leaning to side (running or marching vigorously). See the top component of 泰 in the original version (𡙌), the top component of 赤 and the bottom component of 奐 (well visible in some fonts). Related to 太. Unrelated to 买, in which the bottom component is the stylization of a cowrie.

天.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
