太.originText: a differentiated form of 大 with a 丶 added to represent 太. Compare 泰, which is also a differentiated form with 廾 and 水 added instead.

夫.originRaw:
{{Han etym}} {{liushu|p}}: a variant form of {{och-l|大}} preserving its original meaning of {{och-l|夫|man|id=1}}.裘錫圭 『文字学概要』 商務印書館、1988年、3、122頁。
張世超、孫凌安、金国泰、馬如森 『金文形義通解』 中文出版社、1996年、2502-2505頁。
黄徳寛主編 『古文字譜系疏証』 商務印書館、2007年、1638-1640頁。
林志強等評注 『《文源》評注』 中国社会科学出版社、2017年、2頁。
陳剣 「釈“瓜”」 『出土文献与古文字研究』第9輯 復旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心編、上海古籍出版社、2020年、95頁。 {{och-l|*大}} and {{och-l|*夫}} were originally used interchangeably before settling to their current meanings.羅振玉 『増訂殷虚書契考釈』 東方学会、1927年、巻下30頁。
于省吾主編 『甲骨文字詁林』 中華書局、1996年、215-217頁。 The character was later also phonetically borrowed as an instance of {{liushu|j|nocap=y}} for {{och-l|夫|id=2|that}}. ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' mistakes the added horizontal stroke for a hairpin. In ancient times, when men reached the age of 20, they bound their hair with a hairpin during the [[w:Guan Li|Guan Li ceremony]]. The hairpin would thus be interpreted as the sign of “a grownup man”.
夫.originText: a variant form of 大 preserving its original meaning of 夫. 大 and 夫 were originally used interchangeably before settling to their current meanings. The character was later also phonetically borrowed as an instance of for 夫. ' mistakes the added horizontal stroke for a hairpin. In ancient times, when men reached the age of 20, they bound their hair with a hairpin during the Guan Li ceremony. The hairpin would thus be interpreted as the sign of “a grownup man”.

央.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Unclear. Possibly a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a man with the neck in shackles — original form of {{och-l|鞅|tr=*ʔaŋʔ}}.<ref>張世超、孫凌安、金国泰、馬如森 『金文形義通解』 中文出版社、1996年、1358-1359頁。
季旭昇撰 『説文新証』 芸文印書館、2014年、451-452頁。
林志強等評注 『《文源》評注』 中国社会科学出版社、2017年、232-233頁。</ref> Later borrowed to represent {{och-l|央|center}} as an instance of {{liushu|j|nocap=y}}.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets it as a person inside a house.
央.originText: Unclear. Possibly a of a man with the neck in shackles — original form of 鞅. Later borrowed to represent 央 as an instance of. ' interprets it as a person inside a house.

失.originText: depicting a footprint of someone that has fallen surrounded by drops of blood . Alternatively, according to Shuowen, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 手 + semantic 乙 — something falling from a hand (手). However, the original form doesn't show any hand.

奇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 大 (big; great) + phonetic 可.

奉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{Han compound|丰|廾|c1=p|c2=s|t2=two hands|ls=psc|nocap=y}}， hence the original version is [[𠬻]]. {{zh-l|*手|hand}} was later added at the bottom, and the original character was corrupted into {{zh-l|*𡗗}}. Related to [[舉]].
奉.originText: Originally Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丰 + semantic 廾 (two hands)， hence the original version is 𠬻. 手 was later added at the bottom, and the original character was corrupted into 𡗗. Related to 舉.

奏.originText: two hands (廾) holding an object, perhaps a musical instrument used during a sacrifical ritual (the lower part of the object originally was similar to 夲). Otherwise, the whole character depicts two hands collecting resin (桼) dripping from a cut tree (drawn like 屮). The resin is visible at the bottom of the character.

契.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 㓞 (to engrave) + semantic 大 (person), hence a person making an agreement and/or carving something with a knife. Possibly a variant of 栔 or vice versa, given that the two characters were used interchangeably in ancient text.

奔.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 止 (foot).

奨.originRaw:
{{Han simp|獎|f=將|t=将|f2=犬|t2=大}} in Japanese shinjitai.

{{Han compound|大|将|lang=ja|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} in current form.
奨.originText: 獎將将犬大 in Japanese shinjitai. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 大 + phonetic 将 in current form.

奪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|衣|雀|又|t1=clothing|t2=bird|t3=hand|ls=ic}} – a hand seizing a bird from someone.
奪.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 衣 (clothing) + semantic 雀 (bird) + semantic 又 (hand) – a hand seizing a bird from someone.

奮.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|奞|田|t1=bird|t2=field|ls=ic}} – bird spreading its wings to fly.
奮.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 奞 (bird) + semantic 田 (field) – bird spreading its wings to fly.

女.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: a woman with folded arms kneeling or standing. In the modern form, the pictogram is reversed from the Oracle Bone script form, and is "facing" toward the ''right'' edge of the character: the enclosed area (bounded on the right side by the downward-curving second stroke of the modern form) is the remnant of the figure's right arm, while the figure's left arm has disappeared.

Graphically cognate to {{zh-l|母|mother}} and [[毋]], which has developed similarly, but also includes dots for distinction. Compare {{noncog|egy|𓁐}}.

Similar but unrelated to [[卩]], in which the person kneeling has unspecified gender.
女.originText: a woman with folded arms kneeling or standing. In the modern form, the pictogram is reversed from the Oracle Bone script form, and is "facing" toward the right edge of the character: the enclosed area (bounded on the right side by the downward-curving second stroke of the modern form) is the remnant of the figure's right arm, while the figure's left arm has disappeared. Graphically cognate to 母 and 毋, which has developed similarly, but also includes dots for distinction. Compare. Similar but unrelated to 卩, in which the person kneeling has unspecified gender.

奴.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + semantic 又 (hand) – a hand capturing and ordering a woman around. 女 may also be phonetic. Some oracle bone script forms (not depicted above) are, showing a person (probably a woman) with hands crossed at the back, as opposed to 女 which depicts a woman clasping her hands in front of the body.

好.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|女|子|t1=woman|t2=child|ls=ic}}.

The widely accepted meaning of this character is that the characters for {{m-g|female}} ({{l|zh|女}}) and {{m-g|child}} ({{l|zh|子}}) were put together to form a compound because it was good for a woman to have a child. Similarly, it has been proposed that the compound originally refers to the mutual affection between the mother and child, which then extended to mean {{m-g|good}}. These theories are supported by the smaller {{l|zh|子}} found in some oracle bones and bronze inscriptions. See also [[保]] and the original version of [[乳]].

However, broader interpretations of the second character {{l|zh|子}} could lead to other theories. {{l|zh|子}} could also mean {{m-g|son}}, so it may have meant two children, a boy and a girl next to each other, which is a good fortune to have a boy and a girl. {{l|zh|子}} could also mean {{m-g|man}}, so it may have referred to the love between a man and a woman, which is good. {{w|Duan Yucai}}, in his annotated version of ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', interpreted it as originally referring to the beauty of {{l|zh|女子|woman}}. Lastly, it could mean that the {{m-g|attitude}} of a girl was considered good.

如.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 女 (woman) + semantic 口 (mouth).

妃.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + semantic 卩 (a kneeling man).

妄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亡 + semantic 女 (woman).

妊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 壬.

妖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 + phonetic 夭.

妙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 少

妥.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 爪 (hand) + semantic 女 (woman) – to comfort, to placate. Original form of 綏. Compare 孚.

妨.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|女|方|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. 方 also once bore the now-obsolete meaning of "take up" (space), which can explain the meaning of this character as being "to obstruct someone from approaching a woman".
妨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 + phonetic 方. 方 also once bore the now-obsolete meaning of "take up" (space), which can explain the meaning of this character as being "to obstruct someone from approaching a woman".

妬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 + phonetic 石.

妹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (female, woman) + phonetic 未.

{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|肀|女|ls=ic|t1=hand grabbing hair|t2=woman}} ― a man grabbing a woman's hair to show ownership ({{w|marriage by capture}}).
妻.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 肀 (hand grabbing hair) + semantic 女 (woman) ― a man grabbing a woman's hair to show ownership .

姉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|女|市|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=female}}. The character conveys the meaning of "older sister."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
姉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (female) + phonetic 市. The character conveys the meaning of "older sister."

委.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 禾 + semantic 女 (in the oracle bones inscriptions, there was 𠃊 instead of a woman kneeling).

姫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 臣

姻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 因 – marriage of/to a woman.

威.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 戌 + semantic 女.

婿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 + phonetic 胥. Attested in Qin materials as ⿰士咠, which is of Compound: semantic 士 + phonetic 咠; the phonetic part is later conflated into 胥 .

媒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 某.

媛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 爰.

嫉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 + phonetic 疾.

嫌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 兼.

嫡.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|女|啇|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=woman}}. It conveys the idea of "direct bloodline."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
嫡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 女 (woman) + phonetic 啇. It conveys the idea of "direct bloodline."

子.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – an image of a baby, with a large head and spread arms. The legs are wrapped in a blanket. Compare with {{m-lite|zh|sc=Hani|了}}, where the arms are wrapped, and [[㜽]], in which a lock of hair is visible on top. Compare also [[棄]] and [[毓]], in which the image of the baby is reversed upside-down.

The big seal script form is much more elaborate, showing a baby with hair on a head ({{m-lite|zh|sc=Hani|囟}}) and arms on the two sides of the body, sitting on a stool ({{m-lite|zh|sc=Hani|几}}).

See also the right component of [[保]].
子.originText: an image of a baby, with a large head and spread arms. The legs are wrapped in a blanket. Compare with 了, where the arms are wrapped, and 㜽, in which a lock of hair is visible on top. Compare also 棄 and 毓, in which the image of the baby is reversed upside-down. The big seal script form is much more elaborate, showing a baby with hair on a head (囟) and arms on the two sides of the body, sitting on a stool (几). See also the right component of 保.

孔.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Bronze inscriptions: {{Han compound|丿|子|ls=ic|t1=opening|t2=child}} – opening in the skull of a newborn, i.e. [[fontanelle]].
孔.originText: Bronze inscriptions: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 丿 (opening) + semantic 子 (child) – opening in the skull of a newborn, i.e. fontanelle.

字.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 子 (child).

存.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 才 + semantic 子.

孝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|耂|t1=an old man with long hair, bent over|子|t2=a child|ls=ic}} – an old man and a child, filial piety between generations. Compare top component to {{och-l|老|old}}.
孝.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 耂 (an old man with long hair, bent over) + semantic 子 (a child) – an old man and a child, filial piety between generations. Compare top component to 老.

季.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 禾 + semantic 子.

孤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 子 (child) + phonetic 瓜.

孫.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 子 (son) + semantic 系 (continue).

宅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 乇.

宇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + phonetic 于

守.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宀|寸|t1=roof; building|t2=hand|ls=ic}}; to guard, keep, or defend a place (e.g., a building whose roof is visible on top of the character). It's possible that 寸 (original form of {{och-l|肘}}) is also a phonetic component. A more conservative version is [[㝊]], in which [[又]] is not a phonetic component.
守.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (roof; building) + semantic 寸 (hand); to guard, keep, or defend a place (e.g., a building whose roof is visible on top of the character). It's possible that 寸 (original form of 肘) is also a phonetic component. A more conservative version is 㝊, in which 又 is not a phonetic component.

components.sense: a seated person (女<sub>2</sub>), i.e. sitting with legs together and the buttocks resting on the heels

安.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|宀|女<sub>2</sub>|c1=s|c2=p|t2=a seated person (女<sub>2</sub>), i.e. sitting with legs together and the buttocks resting on the heels|tr2=*ʔˤan}}. The lower element is distinct from {{zh-l|女}} (女<sub>1</sub>); the added stroke(s) depict the other leg and are not decorative.<ref>陳劍：《說“安”字》</ref>
安.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 女2 (a seated person (女2), i.e. sitting with legs together and the buttocks resting on the heels). The lower element is distinct from 女 (女1); the added stroke(s) depict the other leg and are not decorative.

完.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 元.

宗.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 示 (spirit tablet) – temple; ancestral shrine.

官.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Compositionally related to {{zh-l|*宮}}, but approximately analysable as {{Han compound|宀|𠂤|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.
官.originText: Compositionally related to 宮, but approximately analysable as Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 + semantic 𠂤 – multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.

宙.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|宀|由|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=roof}}. It originally represented the farthest place accessible by boat or vehicle and, by extension, came to express the idea of spatial expansion or vastness.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
宙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 由. It originally represented the farthest place accessible by boat or vehicle and, by extension, came to express the idea of spatial expansion or vastness.

定.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 正

宛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 夗. Its original meaning was perhaps linked to "house"; in ancient times, it was read as "館".

宜.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} or {{Han compound|且|多|t1=sacrifical altar|t2=two pieces of meat|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – two pieces of sacrificial meat placed in a sacrifical altar.
宜.originText: Originally a or Ideogrammic compound: semantic 且 (sacrifical altar) + semantic 多 (two pieces of meat) – two pieces of sacrificial meat placed in a sacrifical altar.

宝.originRaw: {{Han simp|寶|f=⿱珤貝|t=玉}}. Officially adopted as the simplified form of {{zh-l|*寶}} in the ''Chinese Character Simplification Scheme'' ({{lw|zh|pref=《|s:漢字簡化方案|漢字簡化方案|suf=》}}) in 1956.
宝.originText: 寶珤貝玉. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 寶 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (漢字簡化方案漢字簡化方案) in 1956.

客.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 各 – a guest.

宣.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|宀|亘|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=roof}}. The character originally represented the main hall where the emperor resided. By extension, it came to be used to mean "clear" or "evident."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
宣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 亘. The character originally represented the main hall where the emperor resided. By extension, it came to be used to mean "clear" or "evident."

室.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 至. Its original meaning is "house, residence". The arrows also indicates that a residence is a place or spot which somebody stops by, marked by an arrow on the ground, hence the phonetic component also adds part of the meaning. Therefore, the character can also be understood as an ideogrammic compound – "a ⼧ roof over ⾄ this exact spot". According to Shuowen Jiezi, it is indeed so, as the meaning is "至所止 arrive at a specific place, symbolized by the roof.

宮.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 + semantic 呂.

宰.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 乂 (to govern) — house of government. 乂 originally appeared as similar to 䇂 in the oracle bone script; in the modern form of this character, it has corrupted into 辛.

害.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Multiple theories:
* He Linyi ({{lang|zh|何琳儀}}): {{liushu|i}}: a spear {{zh-l|*𫲸}} (now {{zh-l|*𥎆}}) + a distinguishing mark {{lang|zh|口}}.<ref name="說文新證">季旭昇，2004《說文新證》，台北：藝文印書館印行，2014年9月第二版。p.601-602</ref><ref name="漢多">[https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf/search.php?word=%E5%AE%B3 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 「害」]</ref>
* {{zh-ref|Li Xueqin (2012)}}: {{liushu|psc}}. The phonetic component is {{zh-l|𡩜|xiàn}}.<ref>李學勤，2012《字源》，天津：天津古籍出版社，2013年7月2次印刷。p.662</ref>
*  Guo Moruo ({{lang|zh|郭沫若}}),<ref name="說文新證"></ref> Dai Jiaxiang ({{lang|zh|戴家祥}})<ref name="漢多"></ref>: {{liushu|p}}, ancient form of {{zh-l|*蓋}} ("lid; cover"). 
* Gao Hongying ({{lang|zh|高鴻纓}}): {{liushu|j}}, original character of {{zh-l|*桷}}, borrowed for sound, which was a {{liushu|p|nocap=yes}} of a house's [[rafter#Etymology_1|rafters]] (see {{zh-l|*舍}}).<ref name="說文新證"></ref>
* Chen Bingxin ({{lang|zh|陳秉新}}): Original form of {{zh-l|*𠤳}}, written as  {{lang|zh|⿷𠥓⿴害五}} in bronze inscriptions, which itself is an ancient way of writing the {{zh-l|*胡}} in {{lang|zh|{{w|㝬簋|胡簋|lang=zh}}}}.<ref name="說文新證"></ref><ref name="漢多"></ref>
* {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}: {{Han compound|宀|口|丯|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=s|c3=p}}.

宴.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宀|妟|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a woman in peaceful background (a roof and the sun). However, the appearance of the character, its meaning and his ancient pronunciation could link this character to [[安]].
宴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 妟 – a woman in peaceful background (a roof and the sun). However, the appearance of the character, its meaning and his ancient pronunciation could link this character to 安.

宵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 肖.

家.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Oracle bone script: {{Han compound|宀|𢑓|c1=s|c2=p|t1=roof|t2=male pig|ls=psc}}.<ref name="殷墟甲骨文“■”、“■”兩字考辨">{{lang|zh|姚萱，2016, 殷墟甲骨文“■”、“■”兩字考辨}} in{{lang|zh|《中国文字研究》，上海：上海书店出版社，2016年8月第二十三辑。}}</ref> An archaic variant closer to the original drawing is {{zh-l|𡩀}}. See {{zh-l|𢑓}} for more. Similar to {{zh-l|冡*}}.

Later the phonetic component have been corrupted to {{lang|zh|豕}}, so {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} erroneously analyzed it as {{Han compound|宀|豭|abb2=y|c1=s|c2=p|t1=roof|t2=pig|ls=psc}}.

All etymologies based on the modern version of the phonetic component ({{lang|zh|豕}}) are folk etymologies since they miss the original component ({{lang|zh|𢑓}}).
<references/>
家.originText: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 𢑓 (male pig). An archaic variant closer to the original drawing is 𡩀. See 𢑓 for more. Similar to 冡*. Later the phonetic component have been corrupted to 豕, so erroneously analyzed it as Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 豭 (pig). All etymologies based on the modern version of the phonetic component (豕) are folk etymologies since they miss the original component (𢑓).

容.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 公 – to hold; to contain. 容 has also largely supplanted 頌 for the sense of “appearance”.

宿.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the {{w|oracle bone script}}, an {{Han compound|人|⿴囗⿱人仌|t1=person|t2=bamboo mat|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – a person resting on a mat. Sometimes a house ({{zh-l|*宀}}) was added.

Later the pictogram of the bamboo mat became {{zh-l|*㐁}} or {{zh-l|*𠀬}}, and eventually came to be written {{zh-l|*百}}.

Contrast {{zh-l|*寒}}.
宿.originText: In the, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic ⿴囗⿱人仌 (bamboo mat) – a person resting on a mat. Sometimes a house (宀) was added. Later the pictogram of the bamboo mat became 㐁 or 𠀬, and eventually came to be written 百. Contrast 寒.

寂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + phonetic 叔

寄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宀|奇|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=house}} ― living away from home.
寄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + phonetic 奇 ― living away from home.

密.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宓|山|t2=mountain|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – hidden in the mountains, secret, intimate. Note that the phonetic 宓 alone has also been used to express the same morpheme as 密.
密.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 宓 + semantic 山 (mountain) – hidden in the mountains, secret, intimate. Note that the phonetic 宓 alone has also been used to express the same morpheme as 密.

富.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 畐.

寒.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 人 (person) + semantic 茻 (grass) – a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold. In some bronze inscriptions, 二 is added at the bottom of the character; this may simply be decorative or may represent a mat. In the seal script, 二 is changed to 仌 to emphasize its meaning of coldness. Contrast 宿.

寛.originRaw:
Unorthodox form {{Han simp|寬|f=萈|t=莧|nocap=y}}. Elimination of {{l|zh|丶}} stroke and alteration of {{l|zh|𦫳|⻀}} <small>(ram's horn component)</small> → {{l|zh|艹}} <small>(grass radical)</small>.

Originally found in the historical {{w|Longkan Shoujian}} ({{lw|zh|龍龕手鑑}}) dictionary (997 AD).
寛.originText: Unorthodox form 寬萈莧. Elimination of 丶 stroke and alteration of 𦫳 (ram's horn component) → 艹 (grass radical). Originally found in the historical (龍龕手鑑) dictionary (997 AD).

察.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 祭.

寡.originText: In the from the, it was originally an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 頁 (head) — only one person in the house; alone. In the bronze script from the, two decorative strokes were added around 頁. The seal script found in ' adds two additional strokes, making the component under 宀 appear as 分 and 頁, leading Shuowen to erroneously interpret the character as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 頒 (to distribute).

寧.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[oracle bone script|Oracle bone script]]: {{Han compound|宀|皿|丂|ls=ic|t1=house|t2=food or wine vessel|t3=table (?)}} – contentment. The {{zh-l|*心|heart}} component was added in [[金文|bronze inscriptions]] to yield {{lang|zh|寧}}, and the {{lang|zh|丂}} component was sometimes omitted to yield {{zh-l|*寍}}.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'': {{Han compound|寍|丂|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=speech (?)}}.

Note that the simplified form {{zh-l|宁}} is also a traditional character on its own.
寧.originText: Oracle bone script: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (house) + semantic 皿 (food or wine vessel) + semantic 丂 (table (?)) – contentment. The 心 component was added in bronze inscriptions to yield 寧, and the 丂 component was sometimes omitted to yield 寍. ': Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 寍 + semantic 丂 (speech (?)). Note that the simplified form 宁 is also a traditional character on its own.

審.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|宀|釆|田|t1=roof|t2=to distinguish}}. There are two theories about the component {{lang|zh|田}}. One is that it was originally {{zh-l|*口|mouth}}, then corrupted into {{zh-l|*曰|say}}, then further into {{lang|zh|田}}. The other one is that its a remnant from a variant form {{lang|zh|⿱宷思}} with {{lang|zh|心}} omitted. The {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} describes {{lang|zh|審}} as the seal script variant of {{zh-l|*宷}}.
審.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + semantic 釆 (to distinguish) + semantic 田. There are two theories about the component 田. One is that it was originally 口, then corrupted into 曰, then further into 田. The other one is that its a remnant from a variant form ⿱宷思 with 心 omitted. The describes 審 as the seal script variant of 宷.

寮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 + phonetic 尞.

寸.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Two separate characters with this form exist:

* {{liushu|j}}: abbreviated form of {{och-l|尊}}, borrowed to refer to {{och-l|寸|a unit of measurement}}.<ref>李轶.先秦度量单位"尺""寸"用字考[J].云南师范大学学报(哲学社会科学版), 2010, 42(5).DOI:10.3969/j.issn.1000-5110.2010.05.017.)</ref>
* {{liushu|i}}: a line on the hand, emphasizing the elbow. Original form of {{och-l|肘|elbow}}.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' considered it to represent a position on the forearm where the pulse can be palpated by compressing the [[radial artery]]. It is called {{zh-l|寸口}} in modern Chinese, and the meaning of a unit of measurement is derived from the distance between the wrist and this position.

Compare {{zh-l|*又}}, {{zh-l|*手}}, {{zh-l|*九}}, {{zh-l|*爪}}.
寸.originText: Two separate characters with this form exist: ' considered it to represent a position on the forearm where the pulse can be palpated by compressing the radial artery. It is called 寸口 in modern Chinese, and the meaning of a unit of measurement is derived from the distance between the wrist and this position. Compare 又, 手, 九, 爪.

寺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 之 (to go) + semantic 又 (hand) – to grasp, to hold. Phonetic 𡳿 (之), which represents a footprint pointing up, became 土 or 士 in the clerical script from the late Western Han to the Eastern Han, and semantic 又 became 寸 in Small Seal Script. The derivative 持 refers to the original word. The character was often used in the place of a more specialized form. For example, in the (see table above) it clearly stood for 時.

封.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丰 + semantic 土 (earth) + semantic 寸 (hand). Compare 邦. Originally 丰, depicting a tree seedling. Variants that added any combination of 土, 又, 田, 丮 appeared from bronze inscriptions onwards.

専.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|專}}; {{Han simp|專|nocap=1}}. Compare [[恵]].

The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
専.originText: Variant of 專; 專. Compare 恵. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

射.originText: In the, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + semantic 矢 (arrow) – to shoot a bow. In the, a hand (又) drawing the bowstring was added. Hence, a conservative variant is 𢎤. Later the bow and arrow on the left became 身 before or during the period, and the hand came to be written 寸.

尉.originText: Possibly Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𡰥 + semantic 寸 (hand) + semantic 火 (fire).

尊.originText: Shuowen: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 酋 (wine) + semantic 寸 (hand) – a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋 to show respect and veneration. However, based on the small seal script, it may instead be a variant of 𢍜, which is Ideogrammic compound: semantic 酋 (wine) + semantic 廾 (two hands).

尋.originText: two hands (now 彐 and 寸 ) stretched out measuring a mat (now 工) – "a unit of measurement; arm span". The component 口 (“mouth, talk”) was likely added to emphasize the act of reading the measurement out loud. Forms with it have appeared as early as, but forms without it have also appeared as late as the. Appears as 𢒫 in the Shuowen Jiezi, which interprets the character as with 彡 as the sound component.

導.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 道 (path) + semantic 寸 (hand) – to lead someone.

小.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Two possible interpretations:
* {{liushu|i}} – three small dots > small.
* {{liushu|p}} – three granules of sand – original character of {{och-l|沙}} > small.

Starting from some bronze inscriptions, the dots have become elongated. Based on this form, ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' erroneously considers it to be an {{Han compound|八|丨|ls=ic|nocap=1|t1=to divide; to separate|t2=small object}}.

Compare with {{och-l|少}}, represented by four dots in its oracle bone script form. Unrelated to the bottom part of [[京]], [[示]], [[尞]], [[尗]], and [[原]].
小.originText: Two possible interpretations: Starting from some bronze inscriptions, the dots have become elongated. Based on this form, ' erroneously considers it to be an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 八 (to divide; to separate) + semantic 丨 (small object). Compare with 少, represented by four dots in its oracle bone script form. Unrelated to the bottom part of 京, 示, 尞, 尗, and 原.

少.originText: four dots, perhaps three grains of sand (see 沙), to indicate "a few, a little". Phonetically borrowed from 小, which is depicted by three dots. Unrelated to 步 (and hence 歲), in which the lower component is the stylization of a foot.

尚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 八 + phonetic 向. Similar to 冋.

就.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{zh-l|*𫢁}}, {{Han compound|享|京|ls=ic|nocap=yes}}, a temple and a tower – meaning "to sacrifice at a high place". During the {{w|Warring States}} period, {{lang|zh|享}} was omitted. In seal script, {{zh-l|*尤|especially; even more}} is added to the right, signifying "high; to go to a higher place".
就.originText: Originally 𫢁, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 享 + semantic 京, a temple and a tower – meaning "to sacrifice at a high place". During the period, 享 was omitted. In seal script, 尤 is added to the right, signifying "high; to go to a higher place".

尺.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Uncertain. Various explanations include:
* A man ({{zh-l|*人}}) with a mark ({{zh-l|*乙}}) on his leg to indicate 10 {{w|Cun (unit)|cun (寸)}} above the foot. ([[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#L|Lin Yiguang, 1920]])
* Differentiation of {{och-l|乇}}, {{och-l|宅}}, or {{och-l|斥}}. ([[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#H|He Linyi, 1998]], [[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#C|Ji Xusheng, 2014]])
* {{liushu|p}} of a hand, more specifically the thumb and the middle finger, stretched out to measure the length of 10 {{w|Cun (unit)|cun (寸)}}. (Shirakawa Shizuka, Lawrence J. Howell)

尻.originText: in the oracle bone script – a person with the buttocks highlighted. In the, it developed into a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 尸 (body) + phonetic 九.

尼.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|ic}}. The character does not appear as an independent character in the oracle bone script but appears as a component of {{zh-l|*𢓚}} and {{zh-l|*秜}}. The character shows a man ({{zh-l|*尸}}) sitting on or leaning on another man ({{zh-l|*匕}}), giving the original meaning of “to stop” or “close; intimate”; the derivative {{zh-l|*昵}} refers to the latter meaning.

Shuowen Jiezi considered it as a phono-semantic compound, but this is widely discredited by later scholars.

Compare [[化]], [[比]], [[北]], and [[卬]].
尼.originText: The character does not appear as an independent character in the oracle bone script but appears as a component of 𢓚 and 秜. The character shows a man (尸) sitting on or leaning on another man (匕), giving the original meaning of “to stop” or “close; intimate”; the derivative 昵 refers to the latter meaning. Shuowen Jiezi considered it as a phono-semantic compound, but this is widely discredited by later scholars. Compare 化, 比, 北, and 卬.

尾.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 尸 (person) + semantic 毛 (hair; feather).

尿.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} in the oracle bone script - a urinating man. In the seal script, it became an {{Han compound|尾|水|ls=ic|nocap=y|t1=tail|t2=water}}. {{zh-l|*尾}} later simplified into {{zh-l|*尸|body}}.
尿.originText: in the oracle bone script - a urinating man. In the seal script, it became an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 尾 (tail) + semantic 水 (water). 尾 later simplified into 尸.

局.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 尸 + phonetic 句. Folk etymology found in some dictionaries mistakes it for a representation of a deceased person's limbs being bent and buried.

居.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 尸 + phonetic 古.

屈.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Originally {{lang|zh|𡲶}}. {{Han compound|ls=psc|出|尾|c1=p|c2=s|t2=tail}}. {{lang|zh|尾}} became {{lang|zh|尸}} in clerical script.
屈.originText: Originally 𡲶. Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 出 + semantic 尾 (tail). 尾 became 尸 in clerical script.

屋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𡉉 + semantic 室 (room). The upper part has corrupted into the unrelated 尸. ' mistakes it for an ideogrammic compound.

展.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 尸 + phonetic 𧝑, which has a variant 𧝣; the original version is 㞡. The phonetic component is a reference to fine red silk clothes, one of the six garments worn by the queen in the Rites of Zhou, and it contains as well a reference to the concept of "opening, extending; watch carefully" in the component 㠭. Similar but unrelated to 昔 and 共.

層.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 尸 + phonetic 曾.

履.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the {{w|bronze inscriptions}}, an {{Han compound|眉|頁|止|舟|ls=ic|nocap=y|t2=person with prominent head|t3=foot|t4=shoe or (shoe-shaped) boat}}. Possibly {{och-l|履}} is also {{liushu|psc|nocap=1|adj=1}} with phonetic component {{och-l|眉}}.

According to ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', {{Han compound|尸|彳|夊|舟|ls=ic|nocap=y|t2=road|t3=foot|t4=(shoe-shaped) boat}}. Possibly {{liushu|psc|nocap=1|adj=1}}, with {{och-l|尸}} functioning as a phonetic component corrupted from {{och-l|眉}}. Comparing Qin bamboo slip script, ''Shuowen'' seal's {{zh-l|*舟}} was corrupted from {{zh-l|*自}}, and Qin's 自 was simplified from {{zh-l|*頁}}.

Modern form is a compound of {{Han compound|尸|復|t2=return}}.
履.originText: In the, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 眉 + semantic 頁 (person with prominent head) + semantic 止 (foot) + semantic 舟 (shoe or (shoe-shaped) boat). Possibly 履 is also with phonetic component 眉. According to ', Ideogrammic compound: semantic 尸 + semantic 彳 (road) + semantic 夊 (foot) + semantic 舟 ((shoe-shaped) boat). Possibly, with 尸 functioning as a phonetic component corrupted from 眉. Comparing Qin bamboo slip script, Shuowen seal's 舟 was corrupted from 自, and Qin's 自 was simplified from 頁. Modern form is a compound of Compound: 尸 + 復 (return).

屯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a swollen sprout or bud beginning to emerge; the original form of {{zh-l|*芚}}.
屯.originText: a swollen sprout or bud beginning to emerge; the original form of 芚.

山.originText: three mountain peaks. In the Oracle Bone Script, they were represented by triangles rather than vertical strokes. Compare 丘, particularly earlier forms. Unrelated to 出 and the top component of 岁 and 豐. Also unrelated to 屮 and 巾.

岐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 支

岡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 网 + semantic 山 (mountain).

岩.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 山 (hill) + semantic 石 (rock). Originally written as 巖 – Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (hill) + phonetic 嚴. The variant form 岩 first appeared in the clerical script in the Han dynasty era.

岬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 甲.

岳.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|羋|山|t1=sheep bleat|t2=mountain}}: rebus of {{zh-l|*羋}} for {{zh-l|*岳}}, with {{zh-l|*山}} added as semantic component.<ref>陈年福：《实用甲骨文字典》，四川辞书出版社2019年版，P.409</ref>
岳.originText: Compound: 羋 (sheep bleat) + 山 (mountain): rebus of 羋 for 岳, with 山 added as semantic component.

岸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|屵|t1=cliff|干|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – the edge of the land. Its proto-form was {{zh-l|*屵}}.
岸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 屵 (cliff) + phonetic 干 – the edge of the land. Its proto-form was 屵.

峰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 夆.

島.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 鳥 + semantic 山 (mountain).

崇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 宗.

崎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 奇.

崖.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|山|t1=mountain|厓|t2=cliff|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}.

Alternatively analyzed as {{Han compound|屵|t1=cliff|圭|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. In this case, its proto-form could be [[屵]].

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth ([[土]]) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade [[士]]. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character, [[厓]] and [[街]] either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
崖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 厓 (cliff). Alternatively analyzed as Phono-semantic compound: semantic 屵 (cliff) + phonetic 圭. In this case, its proto-form could be 屵. Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character, 厓 and 街 either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.

崩.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|山|朋|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=mountain}} – to collapse (of a mountain).
崩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 朋 – to collapse (of a mountain).

嵐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 (mountain) + phonetic 葻

川.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of flowing water – compare {{och-l|水}}, {{zh-l|*巛}}, and {{zh-l|*𡿧}}.
川.originText: of flowing water – compare 水, 巛, and 𡿧.

巡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 川.

巣.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{l|zh|巢}} found in a {{w|Movable type#Metal movable type in China|moveable type}} copy of ''{{w|Biographies of Exemplary Women}}'' 《{{lw|zh|列女傳}}》. First attested in 《{{lw|zh|宋元以來俗字譜}}》, a {{w|Variant Chinese character|variant forms}} dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms ({{l|zh|俗字}}) that have existed since the {{w|Song dynasty}}.
巣.originText: Unorthodox variant of 巢 found in a copy of ' 《列女傳》. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the.

工.originText: a bladed tool to plow the ground and to mark a border. As an alternative, a carpenter's square; according to the second interpretation, the character is related to the original meaning of 巨. Unrelated to 巠 > 𢀖 and 壬.

左.originText: Originally written 𠂇 and 䶹 in the oracle bone script: – a left hand. Compare 又. Late bronze inscription forms show an added 工 component, making the current form a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𠂇 (left hand) + semantic 工 (work), representing the original form of 佐.

巧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 工 + phonetic 丂

巨.originText: of 矩, borrowed for 巨. By the small seal script, the character was simplified and the man holding the carpenter's square was removed; however, the hand holding it appears to remain as the sc=Hani shape inside the 工. ' interprets it as a pictogram, however Chen (2021) points out that 矩 is the original shape.

差.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 來 (wheat) + semantic 𠂇 (left hand) – to hull wheat by rubbing grains inside hands. Original form of 搓. 工 or 口 was later added under 𠂇 to form 左, which is also this character's phonetic component.

己.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – silk rope for binding objects. Original form of {{och-l|紀}}. The character must not be confused with [[已]] and [[巳]]. See also [[丩]].
己.originText: silk rope for binding objects. Original form of 紀. The character must not be confused with 已 and 巳. See also 丩.

市.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: {{Han compound|兮|之|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bustling}}.
市.originText: Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 兮 (bustling) + phonetic 之.

布.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 父 + semantic 巾 (kerchief).

帆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 巾 (cloth) + phonetic 凡.

希.originText: Originally 𢁫, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 爻 + semantic 巾 (cloth).

帝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Oracle Bone Script Di Variants.jpg|thumb|280px|Various forms of {{lang|zh|帝}} in {{w|Oracle Bone Script}}.]]

{{liushu|p}}: Depicts a flower calyx — the structure joining blossom to stem; original form of {{och-l|蒂|calyx; peduncle|tr=*tˤes}}. In oracle bone inscriptions, it denotes the supreme deity governing celestial phenomena, harvests, warfare, and the Shang king's illnesses.

Alternative proposals: a bundle of sacrificial firewood or an altar (→ {{och-l|禘|great sacrifice|tr=*dˤeh}}); a circumpolar asterism centered on the north celestial pole ({{zh-ref|Pankenier, 2004}}).

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' erroneously analyzes the character as {{Han compound|丄|朿|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=up; above|nocap=1}}.
帝.originText: Depicts a flower calyx — the structure joining blossom to stem; original form of 蒂. In oracle bone inscriptions, it denotes the supreme deity governing celestial phenomena, harvests, warfare, and the Shang king's illnesses. Alternative proposals: a bundle of sacrificial firewood or an altar (→ 禘); a circumpolar asterism centered on the north celestial pole . ' erroneously analyzes the character as Phono-semantic compound: semantic 丄 (up; above) + phonetic 朿.

帥.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|寻|巾|t1=two hands|t2=scarf}} - to wear a scarf. {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} interprets it as {{Han compound|ls=psc|𠂤|巾|c1=p|c2=s|tr1=*C.tˤuj}}.
帥.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 寻 (two hands) + semantic 巾 (scarf) - to wear a scarf. interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𠂤 + semantic 巾.

師.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𠂤 + semantic 帀. 師 may be related to words denoting multitude, abundance, or movement to and fro, such as 詵, 駪, 甡, 莘, 侁, 瑟, 蝨 and 蟋.

席.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: a woven mat with ornament. Later, a phonetic {{och-l|石}} was added and the image of the mat corrupted into {{och-l|*巾|cloth}}. 

In the small seal script, {{och-l|*石}} had corrupted into {{lang|zh|sc=Hani|𲟁}}, leading ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' to interpret it as {{Han compound|庶|巾|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=y|abb1=yes}}. In the variant {{lang|zh|𠩛}}, the mat is better preserved and {{och-l|*石}} has corrupted into {{och-l|*厂}} instead.

Compare {{och-l|度}} and {{och-l|庶}}.
席.originText: a woven mat with ornament. Later, a phonetic 石 was added and the image of the mat corrupted into 巾. In the small seal script, 石 had corrupted into sc=Hani, leading ' to interpret it as Compound: phonetic 庶 + semantic 巾. In the variant 𠩛, the mat is better preserved and 石 has corrupted into 厂 instead. Compare 度 and 庶.

帰.originRaw: Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|歸|nocap=y}} (⿱{{l|zh|[[𠂤]][[止]]}} → ⿰{{l|zh|[[丨]][[丿]]}}) originally found in the {{w|Yuan dynasty}} orthographic dictionary <big>《字鑑》</big>.
帰.originText: Unorthodox variant 歸 (⿱𠂤止 → ⿰丨丿) originally found in the orthographic dictionary 《字鑑》.

帳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 巾 + phonetic 長.

常.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尚 + semantic 巾 (cloth). The character originally referred to a "lower garment" similar to a skirt, before being phonetically borrowed to mean "long-lasting; frequently". The original sense is now represented by the character 裳.

帽.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|巾|t1=cloth|冒|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. Originally written as {{och-l|*冃}}; later, {{och-l|*目}} and {{och-l|*巾}} were added.
帽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 巾 (cloth) + phonetic 冒. Originally written as 冃; later, 目 and 巾 were added.

幅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 巾 (clothing) + phonetic 畐.

幕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 莫 + semantic 巾 (cloth).

幣.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|敝|巾|c1=p|c2=s|t2=cloth|ls=psc}} – silk given as a gift or sacrificed.
幣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敝 + semantic 巾 (cloth) – silk given as a gift or sacrificed.

干.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of a shield with feather ornaments on top; in some versions in oracle bones, the central and flat part of the shield can be seen as [[回]].

As an alternative, it is possible {{och-l|*干}} and {{och-l|*單}} are variant forms of the same character in oracle bone script due to their similar shapes and its appearance in the original forms of [[敢]]. Hence, 干 would depict a bifurcated hunting weapon, not a shield. But 單 has two dots on top that depict two stones, while these two dots are absent in 干.

Also borrowed phonetically as a simplification of {{zh-l|*乾}} (dry) and {{zh-l|*幹}}. See also [[盾]] (the pictogram of another shield) and its possible differentiation [[古]].

The interpretation that links this pictogram to a pestle is folk etymology. Unrelated to [[午]], which however represents a pestle.
干.originText: of a shield with feather ornaments on top; in some versions in oracle bones, the central and flat part of the shield can be seen as 回. As an alternative, it is possible 干 and 單 are variant forms of the same character in oracle bone script due to their similar shapes and its appearance in the original forms of 敢. Hence, 干 would depict a bifurcated hunting weapon, not a shield. But 單 has two dots on top that depict two stones, while these two dots are absent in 干. Also borrowed phonetically as a simplification of 乾 (dry) and 幹. See also 盾 (the pictogram of another shield) and its possible differentiation 古. The interpretation that links this pictogram to a pestle is folk etymology. Unrelated to 午, which however represents a pestle.

平.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Uncertain. Various explanations include:
* According to the {{w|Shuowen}}, {{Han compound|八|亏|t1=division|t2=exhaled air}} — the smooth flow of speech.
* {{Han compound|ls=psc|釆|二|c1=p|c2=s|t2=two equal lines}} ([[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#L|Lin Yiguang, 1920]])
* A {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of [[waterweed]] spread flat on the surface of water. Original form of {{och-l|苹|duckweed}}. (Lawrence J. Howell)
* {{liushu|p}} of a balance scale. ({{w|Bernhard Karlgren|Karlgren}},  1973)

年.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (wheat; grain) + phonetic 人. Originally meaning "harvest", it later came to mean "year". In the oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, it was originally written like 秂. In bronze inscriptions after the period, a stroke was often added to 人 to give 千, which still acted as a phonetic component, thus getting (秊). The current form is inherited from the clerical script, where ' (隸變) has occurred.

幹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{zh-l|*榦}}, a {{Han compound|倝|木|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=tree|nocap=1|nocat=1}}. The semantic {{zh-l|*木}} was replaced with a phonetic {{och-l|干}}, making both components phonetic.
幹.originText: Originally 榦, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 倝 + semantic 木 (tree). The semantic 木 was replaced with a phonetic 干, making both components phonetic.

幻.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|j}}, but of what is unclear: 
* Variant of {{och-l|玄}} with an elongated stroke to distinguish (Ji Xusheng).
* Abbreviation of {{och-l|縣}} (He Linyi).

{{Shuowen}} mistakes it for an inversion of {{och-l|予}} based on its seal script form. This misinterpretation has produced the variant form {{och-l|*𠄔}} through ''{{w|liding}}'' ({{zh-l|*隸定}}). This variant is sometimes mistakenly presented as evidence of the character's origin in popular media.
幻.originText: , but of what is unclear: mistakes it for an inversion of 予 based on its seal script form. This misinterpretation has produced the variant form 𠄔 through ' (隸定). This variant is sometimes mistakenly presented as evidence of the character's origin in popular media.

幼.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|幺|力|ls=ic|t1=tiny|t2=strength}}. {{och-l|幺}} may also act as a phonetic component.
幼.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 幺 (tiny) + semantic 力 (strength). 幺 may also act as a phonetic component.

幽.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|𢆶|山|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc}} (originally [[火]] in oracle bone).
幽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𢆶 + semantic 山 (originally 火 in oracle bone).

幾.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𢆶 (silk threads; little things) + semantic 戍 (to guard against) – watching over the fine details. Note that the simplified form 几 is also a traditional character on its own.

広.originRaw: {{Han simp|廣|f=黃|t=厶}}; shinjitai. First attested in 1891 in Japan, influenced by 鑛 → 鉱.<ref>Mari {{smallcaps|Yamashita}}, [http://www.kanken.or.jp/project/data/investigation_incentive_award_2010_yamashita.pdf {{lang|ja|「広」の字体について―略字体の出現時期とその要因―}}], 2011</ref>　Perhaps also influenced by [[弘]], [[宏]], [[紘]], all of which have the ''on'' reading こう and ''kun'' readings ひろ(い), ひろ(し) in Japanese.
広.originText: 廣黃厶; shinjitai. First attested in 1891 in Japan, influenced by 鑛 → 鉱.　Perhaps also influenced by 弘, 宏, 紘, all of which have the on reading こう and kun readings ひろ(い), ひろ(し) in Japanese.

床.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally an unorthodox variant of {{zh-m|*牀}}. Now made up of {{Han compound|广|木|t1=house|t2=tree}}, an {{liushu|ic|nocap=1}} representing a wooden furniture item (a bed) in a house.
床.originText: Originally an unorthodox variant of 牀. Now made up of Compound: 广 (house) + 木 (tree), an representing a wooden furniture item (a bed) in a house.

序.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 + phonetic 予.

底.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|广|t1=building|氐|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – the bottom or base, foundation of a building. Note that 氐, according to one interpretation, is a figure bowing or the root of a tree, hence a connotation of "down"; if the interpretation is correct, the phonetic component also adds part of the meaning.
底.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (building) + phonetic 氐 – the bottom or base, foundation of a building. Note that 氐, according to one interpretation, is a figure bowing or the root of a tree, hence a connotation of "down"; if the interpretation is correct, the phonetic component also adds part of the meaning.

components.sense: house built to depend on a cliff

店.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|广|占|c1=s|c2=p|t1=house built to depend on a cliff}}
店.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (house built to depend on a cliff) + phonetic 占

府.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|广|t1=building|付|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a type of building.
府.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (building) + phonetic 付 – a type of building.

度.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|石|c1=p|t1=rock|又|c2=s|t2=hand|ls=psc}}. {{w|Duan Yucai}} argues that the presence of the hand component in this character is because the hand was used as a reference for measurement. {{lang|zh|石}} is then corrupted into {{lang|zh|sc=Hani|𲟁}}.

{{w|Shuowen}} considers it to be a {{Han compound|庶|c1=p|又|c2=s|ls=psc|nocap=y}}.

Compare {{och-l|庶}} and {{och-l|席}}.
度.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 石 (rock) + semantic 又 (hand). argues that the presence of the hand component in this character is because the hand was used as a reference for measurement. 石 is then corrupted into sc=Hani. considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 庶 + semantic 又. Compare 庶 and 席.

座.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (house on cliff) + phonetic 坐.

庫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (building) + phonetic 車. ' incorrectly interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.

庭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 + phonetic 廷.

庶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 石 (stone) + semantic 火 (fire). In the small seal script, 石 has corrupted into sc=Hani. ' interprets it as Compound: 广 (roof) + 炗 (light). Compare 度 and 席.

康.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 庚 (threshing tools) + semantic 米 (rice) – chaff. The clearest version is 𢊪, in which the two components can be identified well; in the semi-conservative variant 𥹺, the rice at the bottom is still well visible. The derivative 糠 refers to the original word. Unrelated to 隶, in which the bottom part is a reference to a tail (毛); also unrelated to 水.

庸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 庚 + phonetic 同. Probably the original graph of 鏞 (“large bell”), formed from 庚 plus 同 / 用.

廉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 + phonetic 兼.

廊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 + phonetic 郎. 良 may be the original form of this character, see there for more.

延.originText: Originally 㢟, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 彳 (walking) + semantic 止 (foot) – "to travel far". The stroke at the top started being added as a distinguishing mark at the end of the, as a way to distinguish its usage from 㢟 as an adverb to mean "prolonged", making it an. interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丿 + semantic 㢟.

廷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 廴 + phonetic 𡈼.

建.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 廴 + semantic 聿. Originally, a — a hand (又) planting a pole (𰀁) into a base . The left component was originally written as ∟. The right component is stylized as 聿; while the hand is still recognizable, the bottom part is unrelated to a writing brush. The whole character is mostly similar to 叔.

弁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|厶|廾}}: hands (廾) placing a hat (厶) on someone’s head.
弁.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 厶 + semantic 廾: hands (廾) placing a hat (厶) on someone’s head.

弄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|玉|廾|ls=ic|t1=jade|t2=hands}} – to touch jade with one's hands.
弄.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + semantic 廾 (hands) – to touch jade with one's hands.

弊.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|敝|廾|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc|ls2=ic|t1=destroy, tatters|t2=both hands}}: emphatic form of {{zh-m|敝|tr=-}} — destroying something with both hands.
弊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敝 (destroy, tatters) + semantic 廾 (both hands): emphatic form of 敝 — destroying something with both hands.

式.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 弋 + semantic 工 (work).

弓.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a bow. See also the original version of [[射]]. Unrelated to [[弗]]. See also [[夷]].
弓.originText: a bow. See also the original version of 射. Unrelated to 弗. See also 夷.

弔.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the oracle bone script, a person with a corded arrow wound around the body; an ideogram of {{zh-m|*約||to bind; to tie}}.<ref>鄔可晶《甲骨文“弔”字補釋》</ref>
弔.originText: In the oracle bone script, a person with a corded arrow wound around the body; an ideogram of 約.

引.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + semantic 丿 (indicatory stroke) Oracle-bone and bronze forms depict a (often slack) bow with a short slant stroke added as an indicatory mark; it most likely marks the place/line of drawing the bow (i.e. pulling the string), hence the basic meaning “to pull; to draw (a bow)”. A newer view takes the stroke as pointing to the bow’s curved section (弓淵) and derives “to draw” secondarily, but this remains less certain.

弟.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap. The wrapping signified order or sequence, which extended to "younger brother".
弟.originText: of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap. The wrapping signified order or sequence, which extended to "younger brother".

弥.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + phonetic 尔 Usage recorded as early the 6th century, found in the Yupian玉篇四庫全書本卷玉篇, which was used interchangeably with 彌.

弦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + phonetic 玄.

弧.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|弓|瓜|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bow}}. It refers to a bow made of wood, and by extension, expresses the idea of bending like a bow.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
弧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + phonetic 瓜. It refers to a bow made of wood, and by extension, expresses the idea of bending like a bow.

弱.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + semantic 彡 (hair, meaning "decoration" in this case)—a decorative bow that is functionally inferior. Or it might be indicating that the bow is shaking, which implies a worn-out bow. An alternate etymology is 𢎥 + 𢎥, 𢎥 being a variant of 卷.

張.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 弓 (bow) + phonetic 長.

強.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{zh-ref|Zhengzhang (2003)}}: {{Han compound|彊|虫|c1=p|c2=s|t2=insect|ls=psc}}. {{zh-ref|Ji Xusheng (2014)}} gives {{och-l|𪪺}} as the phonetic component instead. Original form of {{och-l|𧖑|[[rice weevil]]}}. Later borrowed to represent {{och-l|彊|strong}}.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'': {{Han compound|弘|虫|c1=p|c2=s|t2=insect|ls=psc}}.

The character {{lang|zh|強}} likely originally referred to the [[rice weevil]], an [[insect]] that attacks [[rice]] and several other crops, before being phonetically borrowed to represent the sense of "strong; powerful", which was previously represented by the character {{och-l|彊}}.
強.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 彊 + semantic 虫 (insect). gives 𪪺 as the phonetic component instead. Original form of 𧖑. Later borrowed to represent 彊. ': Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 弘 + semantic 虫 (insect). The character 強 likely originally referred to the rice weevil, an insect that attacks rice and several other crops, before being phonetically borrowed to represent the sense of "strong; powerful", which was previously represented by the character 彊.

当.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{l|zh|當}}. From {{w|cursive script (East Asia)|cursive script}}.

彙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 㣇 + phonetic 胃.

形.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 井 + semantic 彡. Originally written as 刑 in ancient texts. Based on the corrupted form of 井, ' mistakes 幵 to be the phonetic component. The variant form 𢒈, which preserves the original phonetic component, is found in tombstones from the and times.

彩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 采 + semantic 彡.

彫.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|彡|周|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=representing patterns or ornamentation}}. It represents the act of carving patterns, and by extension, conveys the meaning "to engrave" or "to carve."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
彫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彡 (representing patterns or ornamentation) + phonetic 周. It represents the act of carving patterns, and by extension, conveys the meaning "to engrave" or "to carve."

彰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 章 (emblem) + semantic 彡 (colorful patterns) – conspicuous.

影.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|景|彡|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. The original meaning is "shadow". The phonetic component also indicates the concept of image.
影.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 景 + semantic 彡. The original meaning is "shadow". The phonetic component also indicates the concept of image.

役.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|彳|殳|t1=movement; action|t2=a weapon, like a spear|ls=ic|c1=s|c2=s}}. The character originally depicted guarding a border with a weapon in hand, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of performing a duty or task.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
役.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 彳 (movement; action) + semantic 殳 (a weapon, like a spear). The character originally depicted guarding a border with a weapon in hand, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of performing a duty or task.

彼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 + phonetic 皮.

往.originText: Originally 㞷𫭠, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 止 (foot) + phonetic 王; see also the top component of 出. Later 彳 was added to form 𢓸, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 (to step) + semantic 止 (foot) + phonetic 王. Eventually, the right component was stylized into the unrelated 主. The footprint 屮 pointing upwards on top became a point as in the character 之. See also 迋.

征.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 + phonetic 正 (straight). Also. 徵正 as well as existing already as a traditional character.

径.originRaw: {{Han simp|徑|f=巠|t=𢀖}} based on the table of 54 simplified radical components listed in the 1956 {{w|Chinese Character Simplification Scheme}} by the People's Republic of China. <!-- Refer https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/漢字簡化方案#漢字偏旁簡化表 -->
径.originText: 徑巠𢀖 based on the table of 54 simplified radical components listed in the 1956 by the People's Republic of China.

待.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 + phonetic 寺.

律.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 + phonetic 聿.

後.originText: In oracle bone script, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 幺 (thread) + semantic 夊 (foot) – a foot bound by a rope, thus lagging behind. The component 彳 was added afterwards to emphasize this action. Note that the simplified form 后 is also a traditional character on its own, with a different meaning.

徐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 (walk slowly) + phonetic 余

徒.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Small seal script: {{Han compound|辵|土|c1=s|c2=p|t1=walk|ls=psc}}. Later corrupted into {{Han compound|彳|走}}.
徒.originText: Small seal script: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 土. Later corrupted into Compound: 彳 + 走.

従.originRaw: Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|從|f=从|t=䒑|nocap=y}} found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary {{w|Ganlu Zishu}} ({{lw|zh|干祿字書}}).
従.originText: Unorthodox variant 從从䒑 found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary (干祿字書).

得.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}. The ancient form of {{lang|zh|得}} is {{zh-l|*㝵}}, composed of {{zh-l|*貝|cowry}} + {{zh-l|*又|hand}} — to pick up a cowry > to obtain valuables. A component {{zh-l|*彳}} was sometimes added to show that the cowry was picked up on the road.

In the Qin Bamboo and Slip script:
* a horizontal line was added to the {{zh-l|*又}}, which means it is replaced with the related {{zh-l|*寸}}. This is a feature of Qin script, and many characters that used to compound with {{zh-l|*又}} now compound with {{zh-l|*寸}}.

In the ''Shuowen'' seal script:
* the {{zh-l|*貝}} corrupts into something resembling {{zh-l|*見}}. However, this should be an error of ''Shuowen'' because it can only be only found in ''Shuowen'' and not in historical Qin Seal script, Qin Bamboo, and Slip script.

In the clerical script:
* the {{zh-l|*貝}} is simplified as {{zh-l|*目|eye}}; such simplification can be seen in its early form in Spring and Autumn and Warring States bronze inscriptions, Chu Bamboo, and Silk script, as well as other characters such as {{zh-l|*具}}. Then it corrupts into {{zh-l|*旦|dawn}} in later clerical script, and Regular script inherited it.
得.originText: The ancient form of 得 is 㝵, composed of 貝 + 又 — to pick up a cowry > to obtain valuables. A component 彳 was sometimes added to show that the cowry was picked up on the road. In the Qin Bamboo and Slip script: In the Shuowen seal script: In the clerical script:

御.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Oracle bone script: {{Han compound|ls=psc|午|卩|c1=p|c2=s|t2=kneeling person}} – govern. Bronze inscriptions added {{och-l|*彳}} and {{och-l|*止}} to emphasize action.
御.originText: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 午 + semantic 卩 (kneeling person) – govern. Bronze inscriptions added 彳 and 止 to emphasize action.

復.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 (walk) + phonetic 复 (repeat). Walk back and forth.

循.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 彳 (movement) + phonetic 盾 – to follow (movement).

微.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

In oracle bone script, it may be written as {{och-l|𡵂}} or {{och-l|𢼸}}. 

The former is a variant of {{och-l|美}}, borrowed for sound, {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a person with long hair. 

The latter an {{Han compound|nocap=y|美|alt1=𡵂|攴|alt2=攵|ls=ic|ls2=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=hand with tool}} – splitting or combing hairs; minute. Possibly the original form of {{och-l|媺}}. 

{{och-l|彳}} was added to emphasize action to create the modern form.
微.originText: In oracle bone script, it may be written as 𡵂 or 𢼸. The former is a variant of 美, borrowed for sound, of a person with long hair. The latter an Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 美 + semantic 攴 (hand with tool) – splitting or combing hairs; minute. Possibly the original form of 媺. 彳 was added to emphasize action to create the modern form.

徳.originRaw: {{m|zh|徳|tr=-}} evolved naturally from earlier forms of the Chinese script; {{m|zh|德|tr=-}} was reintroduced via knowledge that {{m|zh|徳|tr=-}}/{{m|zh|德|tr=-}} etymologically contains {{m|zh|直|tr=-}} as a component.
徳.originText: 徳 evolved naturally from earlier forms of the Chinese script; 德 was reintroduced via knowledge that 徳/德 etymologically contains 直 as a component.

徹.originText: Oracle bone inscriptions: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 鬲 (pot) + semantic 又 (hand) – a hand removing utensils after eating. Bronze inscriptions replaced 又 with 攵 to emphasize action. In seal script 彳 was added to further emphasize action, and what was originally a pot had corrupted into the unrelated 育.

心.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a heart, now highly stylized.

必.originText: Likely a – the handle (⿻⿺㇂丶丿) found on the right hand side of weapons such as 戊 or 戈 or 戉 written stand-alone. Two decorative strokes were then added to the sides. 柲 Unrelated to 心, as bronze script makes clear, but in current form very similar.

忌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 己 + semantic 心 (heart).

忍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 刃 (blade) + semantic 心 (heart).

志.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 之 + semantic 心. Note that the top has been simplified and is now graphically 士.

忘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亡 + semantic 心 (heart). of 忙.

忙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 亡. of 忘.

忠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 中 + semantic 心 (heart).

快.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 夬.

念.originText: Zhang (2021): Ideogrammic compound: semantic 今 (upside-down mouth) + semantic 心 (heart): to listen to one's heart. Original character for 念. ' interprets 今 to be a phonetic component, but the Old Chinese phonetics do not match.

怒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 奴 (slave) – angry.

怖.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|心|alt1=忄|布|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=heart}}. It conveys the meaning of "to fear" or "to be afraid."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
怖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 布. It conveys the meaning of "to fear" or "to be afraid."

思.originText: Original form was 恖, considered by ' to be a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 囟 + semantic 心 (heart). It may also be a Ideogrammic compound: semantic 囟 (fontanel) + semantic 心 (heart). 囟 started to corrupt into the unrelated 田 as early as the silk script.

怠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 台 + semantic 心 (heart).

急.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 及 + semantic 心 (heart).

性.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|心|alt1=忄|t1=heart|生|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – nature, personal quality, hence of the heart.
性.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 生 – nature, personal quality, hence of the heart.

怨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 夗 + semantic 心 (heart).

怪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 圣.

恐.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the Shuowen Jiezi appears as {{Han compound|ls=psc|𢀜|心|c1=p|c2=s|t2=heart|nocap=yes}}. The modern form can be interpreted as {{Han compound|ls=psc|巩|心|c1=p|c2=s|t2=heart|nocap=yes}}
恐.originText: In the Shuowen Jiezi appears as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𢀜 + semantic 心 (heart). The modern form can be interpreted as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 巩 + semantic 心 (heart)

恥.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 耳 + semantic 心 (heart)

恩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 因 + semantic 心 (heart).

恭.originText: ': Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 共 + semantic 心 (heart)

息.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|自|t1=nose|心|t2=heart|ls=ic}} – to breathe (life) through one’s nose. Note that {{lang|zh|自}} originally meant “nose” and was later borrowed for “self”.
息.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 自 (nose) + semantic 心 (heart) – to breathe (life) through one’s nose. Note that 自 originally meant “nose” and was later borrowed for “self”.

悔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 每.

悟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 吾.

悠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 攸 + semantic 心 (heart; mind)

患.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 串 + semantic 心 (heart). Since ' does not have the character 串, it interprets the character as Compound: phonetic 吅 + semantic 丨 + semantic 心 (heart) – to pierce through something from the heart. claims in his commentary that older copies of Shuowen actually have Compound: phonetic 毌 (to pierce through) + semantic 心 (heart) instead.

悲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 非 + semantic 心 (heart; thought; emotion).

悼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 卓.

惜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 昔 – a feeling (of the heart). Note that 昔 has meaning of “past, ending”, hence connotations of “feelings for the past, feeling about an ending – regret, rue”.

惧.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|心|alt1=忄|具|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=heart}}. Originally, it was a popular variant of [[懼]].<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
惧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 具. Originally, it was a popular variant of 懼.

惰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart; mind) + phonetic 隋.

想.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 相 (to look at) + semantic 心 (heart, mind) – to think, to consider.

愁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 秋 + semantic 心 (heart)

愉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 俞.

意.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Modern form is a compound of {{zh-l|*音}} and {{zh-l|*心|heart}}. However, the top component is etymologically unrelated to {{zh-l|*音}}. According to {{zh-ref|Lin (1920)}}, {{zh-l|𠶷}} (a compound of {{zh-l|言*}} and {{zh-l|中*}}) found in bronze inscriptions is the same character as {{zh-l|意}}.
意.originText: Modern form is a compound of 音 and 心. However, the top component is etymologically unrelated to 音. According to, 𠶷 (a compound of 言* and 中*) found in bronze inscriptions is the same character as 意.

愚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 禺 + semantic 心 (heart) – stupid.

愛.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Originally written as {{och-l|*㤅}}. {{Han compound|旡|心|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=[[heart]]|tr=*ʔˤəs|tr1=*kəs}}.

As early as the {{w|Qin dynasty}}, a redundant component {{och-l|*夊|[[foot]]}} was added to the bottom of the character, as with some other characters depicting people. Compare {{och-l|*憂}} (from {{och-l|*㥑}}). Hence, the character changed into {{och-l|*𢙴}}.

Further corruption of the top component of {{och-l|*𢙴}} turned the original phonetic {{och-l|*旡}} into {{lang|zh|⿱爫冖}}.
愛.originText: Originally written as 㤅. Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 旡 + semantic 心 (heart). As early as the, a redundant component 夊 was added to the bottom of the character, as with some other characters depicting people. Compare 憂 (from 㥑). Hence, the character changed into 𢙴. Further corruption of the top component of 𢙴 turned the original phonetic 旡 into ⿱爫冖.

感.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 咸 + semantic 心 (heart).

態.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 能 + semantic 心 (heart) – one’s heart-felt attitude.

慢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 曼 – a character trait or behavior (of the heart), sluggish. Note that 曼 also means “long, extended”, so connotations of “take a long time, leisurely, sluggish”.

{{Han compound|心|alt1=忄|t1=heart|貫|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – habit is what one does by heart.
慣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 貫 – habit is what one does by heart.

慶.originText: In Ideogrammic compound: semantic 廌 (antelope) + semantic 心. The component 心 signified goodness, blessings and auspiciousness. In 心 is often also written as 文. During the Warring states period, the tail of 廌 corrupted into 个, then further into 夂 during the Qin dynasty. Based on the overlap between the many ancient variants of the character suggests that 麕, 廌, 麐, 鹿 all refer to kinds of deer – beautiful and therefore worth celebrating when obtained. He also concludes that there is enough evidence that 慶 and 麐 were once the same character. Since 麐 was the most precious among deer, its character was used to express celebration.

憂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 㥑 + semantic 夊.

憎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 曾.

憤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 賁.

憩.originRaw: {{Han compound|恬|息|ls=ic|t1=tranquil|t2=rest|abb1=yes}}. There is also the possibility that {{lang|zh|憩}} is {{liushu|psc|adj=yse|nocap=yes|pron={{och-retrieve-pron}}}}, with {{och-l|𠯑}} as the phonetic component.
憩.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 恬 (tranquil) + semantic 息 (rest). There is also the possibility that 憩 is {{liushu|psc|adj=yse|nocap=yes|pron=}}, with 𠯑 as the phonetic component.

憬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 景.

憲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 (heart) + phonetic 𡩜 (a form of punishment involving tattooing the eyes). The character conveys the meaning of "law" or "rule."

憾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 心 + phonetic 感.

{{Han compound|縣|心|t2=heart|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. {{och-l|*縣}} originally referred to this word; {{och-l|*心}} was added later for distinguishment.
懸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 縣 + semantic 心 (heart). 縣 originally referred to this word; 心 was added later for distinguishment.

成.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|戊|丁|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. The phonetic component is not [[囗]] or [[口]], as folk etymology states. According to Ji Xusheng 季旭昇, its original meaning was "city walls", with a reference to something protected conveyed by the weapon. Its original meaning is preserved in [[城]].
成.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 戊 + phonetic 丁. The phonetic component is not 囗 or 口, as folk etymology states. According to Ji Xusheng 季旭昇, its original meaning was "city walls", with a reference to something protected conveyed by the weapon. Its original meaning is preserved in 城.

我.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

A {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a [[trident]]-like weapon or tool (note the oracle bone script form {{och-l|*𢦐}}). {{zh-ref|Jao & Zeng (1985, pp. 289–290)}} conjecture about its similarity to a kind of three-bladed polearm found at archaeological sites. Cf. {{och-l|*戈|polearm}}, which is the same weapon but with a single blade instead of three. It was already borrowed for sound as an instance of {{liushu|j|nocap=y}} for the pronoun {{och-l|我|I}} since the oracle bone script.

{{w|Guo Moruo}} considers it to be the original character for {{och-l|錡|id=1|gloss=a kind of war [[axe]] with three blades or teeth}}.

{{glossary|folk etymology|Folk etymology}} considers it to be an ideograph of a [[hand]] ({{och-l|*手}}) holding a [[weapon]] ({{och-l|*戈}}) to protect [[oneself]].
我.originText: A of a trident-like weapon or tool (note the oracle bone script form 𢦐). conjecture about its similarity to a kind of three-bladed polearm found at archaeological sites. Cf. 戈, which is the same weapon but with a single blade instead of three. It was already borrowed for sound as an instance of for the pronoun 我 since the oracle bone script. considers it to be the original character for 錡. considers it to be an ideograph of a hand (手) holding a weapon (戈) to protect oneself.

戒.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|戈|t1=halberd|廾|t2=hands|ls=ic}} – to hold up a weapon as warning.
戒.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 戈 (halberd) + semantic 廾 (hands) – to hold up a weapon as warning.

戚.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|戊|t1=scythe|尗|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – in early sense, a battle-axe, a kind of cutting weapon. Later borrowed to mean "relative".
戚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 戊 (scythe) + phonetic 尗 – in early sense, a battle-axe, a kind of cutting weapon. Later borrowed to mean "relative".

戴.originText: In the, a of a person holding something on their head with both hands. Possibly originally the same character as 異 (“person wearing a mask” or “person carrying something on their head”), see there for more. Later, a, with 異 serving as the semantic (and also possibly phonetic) component, and either 弋, 𢦏, or 之 acting as a phonetic component.

戻.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han simp|戾}}. {{Han compound|戶|犬|ls=ic|c1=s|c2=s|t1=door|t2=dog}}. It depicts a dog twisting its body to slip under a door, which came to convey the meanings “to return” or “to reach/arrive.” The modern commonly used character is a simplified form.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
戻.originText: 戾. Ideogrammic compound: semantic 戶 (door) + semantic 犬 (dog). It depicts a dog twisting its body to slip under a door, which came to convey the meanings “to return” or “to reach/arrive.” The modern commonly used character is a simplified form.

房.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 戶 (door) + phonetic 方. The meaning of 方 'side' can also play a role, if the character originally referred to one of the two rooms beside the central room (side room).

所.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|戶|斤|c1=p|c2=s|t2=[[axe]]|ls=psc}} – the sound of [[logging]] (the definition given in ''{{w|Shuowen}}'').
所.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 戶 + semantic 斤 (axe) – the sound of logging (the definition given in ').

扇.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 戶 (door) + semantic 羽 (feather).

扉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 戶 + phonetic 非.

手.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – hand and fingers. The top stroke is the bent over middle finger, while the horizontal strokes are each two fingers. Compare {{zh-m|*爪}}, {{zh-m|*寸}}, {{zh-m|*九}}, {{zh-m|*又}}, and {{zh-m|*彐}} as a stylized hand. Compare {{zh-m|*丑}} as an animal claw. See also the bottom part of {{zh-m|*舉}} and {{zh-m|*奉}}.

Note that unlike the other hand/claw characters, {{lang|zh|手}} has consistently had five fingers: a mammalian/human hand, as opposed to the three digits often found in the others.

Compare also {{zh-m|*止|foot}}, derived from a footprint pointing upward, originally composed of 3 toes and a sole.
手.originText: hand and fingers. The top stroke is the bent over middle finger, while the horizontal strokes are each two fingers. Compare 爪, 寸, 九, 又, and 彐 as a stylized hand. Compare 丑 as an animal claw. See also the bottom part of 舉 and 奉. Note that unlike the other hand/claw characters, 手 has consistently had five fingers: a mammalian/human hand, as opposed to the three digits often found in the others. Compare also 止, derived from a footprint pointing upward, originally composed of 3 toes and a sole.

才.originText: a sharp peg. Same as 弋 and 尗. The sense "talent" is via an early phonetic loan. See also the top component of 𢦏. erroneously analyzed this character as a sprout growing from the ground.

打.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 丁.

扱.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|手|alt1=⺘|及|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=hand}}. It conveys the meaning of taking in by hand. In Japan, it is used to mean "to handle" or "to deal with."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
扱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 及. It conveys the meaning of taking in by hand. In Japan, it is used to mean "to handle" or "to deal with."
