承.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 卩 (kneeling person) + semantic 廾 (both hands) – to hold; to carry. Compare 丞. In the seal script, an additional hand 手 was added.

抑.originText: A hand suppressing a kneeling person. For contrast, see 印.

捗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 步.

捨.originRaw:

{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|t1=hand|舍|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to discard with the hand.
捨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 舍 – to discard with the hand.

据.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 居.

捻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 念.

掃.originText: a 手 with a 帚.

授.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 受. There are actually three “hands” in this character, as 爫 also means “hand”, as does 又 graphically.

掌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尚 + semantic 手.

排.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 非 – to place in line.

掘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand; action) + phonetic 屈.

掛.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|手|alt1=⺘|卦|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=hand}}. It expresses the idea of hooking or hanging something with the hand. Originally, it was a popular form of the character [[挂]].<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
掛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 卦. It expresses the idea of hooking or hanging something with the hand. Originally, it was a popular form of the character 挂.

採.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|采|ls=psc|c1=s|t1=hand|t2=to pick|c2=p}}. Originally written {{zh-l|*采}}.
採.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 采 (to pick). Originally written 采.

探.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 𥥍.

接.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|妾|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}} – to receive (in the hand).
接.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 + phonetic 妾 – to receive (in the hand).

控.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 + phonetic 空.

推.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|t1=hand|隹|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – push with the hand.
推.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 隹 – push with the hand.

措.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 昔.

描.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 苗.

提.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 是.

揚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 昜.

換.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 奐.

握.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 屋.

揮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 軍.

援.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 爰. Possibly 爰 was the original form of this character, making it also an, see 爰 for more.

損.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 員

搬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 般.

搭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 荅.

携.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

The original character is [[攜]]. {{Han compound|手|alt1=⺘|雟|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=hand}}. It expresses the idea of carrying something hanging from the hand. The commonly used modern character is based on a popular simplified form.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
携.originText: The original character is 攜. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 雟. It expresses the idea of carrying something hanging from the hand. The commonly used modern character is based on a popular simplified form.

搾.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|手|alt1=⺘|窄|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=hand}}. It expresses the meaning of squeezing or wringing with the hand.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
搾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 窄. It expresses the meaning of squeezing or wringing with the hand.

摘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 啇.

摩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 麻 + semantic 手 (hand).

摯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 執 + semantic 手 (hand).

撤.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|t1=hand|徹|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|abb2=y}} – to remove by hand.
撤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 徹 – to remove by hand.

撮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 + phonetic 最.

撲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 菐.

擁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 雍.

操.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 喿.

擦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|alt1=扌|t1=hand|察|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – wipe, scrub by hand.
擦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 察 – wipe, scrub by hand.

擬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + phonetic 疑.

支.originText: 又竹十竹 – a branch. Similar but unrelated to 攴, 丈, 尹 and 父.

改.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:改-clerical-han-variant.svg|128px|thumb|{{m-self|zh|改}} (in the form of 攺) from a Western-Han manuscript of the ''{{w|Etiquette and Ceremonial|Yili}}'' in the clerical script.]]

In the oracle bone script, a {{Han compound|巳|攴|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=1}}.

The interpretation linked to a child beaten or threatened by a stick in hand to indicate "correct, amend" referred to educating a child is probably folk etymology.

Since the small seal script, the phonetic component has been changed to {{och-l|己}}.
改.originText: In the oracle bone script, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 巳 + semantic 攴. The interpretation linked to a child beaten or threatened by a stick in hand to indicate "correct, amend" referred to educating a child is probably folk etymology. Since the small seal script, the phonetic component has been changed to 己.

components.sense: hand holding a tool or weapon

攻.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|工|攴|alt2=攵|c1=p|c2=s|t1=work|t2=hand holding a tool or weapon|ls=psc}}.
攻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 工 (work) + semantic 攴 (hand holding a tool or weapon).

放.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|方|攴|alt2=攵|t2=hand, action|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – an action, release.
放.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 方 + semantic 攴 (hand, action) – an action, release.

政.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 正 + semantic 攴 (action).

故.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|古|攴|alt2=攵|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc}}.<!--The gloss should actually say what the actual semantic meaning is (not just a listing of the character with no further explanation), otherwise the etymology is incomplete and our users are left wondering.-->
故.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 古 + semantic 攴.

敏.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|每|攴|c1=p|c2=s|t2=hand; action|ls=psc}}. The {{lang|zh|攴}} component was sometimes written as {{zh-m|*又|gloss=hand}} in early writing.
敏.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 每 + semantic 攴 (hand; action). The 攴 component was sometimes written as 又 in early writing.

救.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 求 + semantic 攴.

敗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 貝 + semantic 攴 (strike).

components.sense: teaching cane; stick that represents authority

教.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 爻 + semantic 子 (child) + semantic 攴 (teaching cane; stick that represents authority) – teaching a child. See also 學 and 算.

敢.originText: a hand (又) using a capturing tool (𰅱) to hunt a wild boar (豕). Later, 𰅱 was omitted and a redundant component 口 or 甘 was added (Chen Jian, 2020; Xie Mingwen, 2020). The components eventually corrupted into the modern form.

散.originText: The original version visible on oracle bone script is 㪔, hence Ideogrammic compound: semantic 林 (trees, forest) + semantic 攴 (to knock, to tap), also written with hemp stalks 𣏟 (> 𢽳) or bamboo 竹 instead of two trees. The original meanings are "to clear a place from vegetation; to kill". The character later started meaning "to dissipate, to disperse" since bamboo in particular breaks easily into pieces; eventually, the meaning shifted to "to walk around, to stroll". ': Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 𢽳, written as 𣀙, in which 林 is well visible on top.

敬.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Possibly {{Han compound|茍|攴|t1=kneeling person or sitting dog|t2=hand holding a stick, authority|ls=ic|nocap=y}}.
敬.originText: Possibly Ideogrammic compound: semantic 茍 (kneeling person or sitting dog) + semantic 攴 (hand holding a stick, authority).

数.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{zh-l|數*}}, attested since [[w:Ming dynasty|Ming dynasty]]. {{Han simp|數|f=婁|t=娄}}.
数.originText: Unorthodox variant of 數*, attested since Ming dynasty. 數婁娄.

整.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 敕 + phonetic 正

敵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|啻|攴|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=to tap; to hit}}.
敵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 啻 + semantic 攴 (to tap; to hit).

敷.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Variant form of {{och-l|*𢾭}}. {{Han compound|ls=psc|ls2=ic|尃|攴|alt2=攵|c1=p|c2=s|t1=distribute|t2=hand with whip; action}}. The bottom left {{zh-l|*寸}} has been replaced with {{zh-l|*方}}.
敷.originText: Variant form of 𢾭. Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 尃 (distribute) + semantic 攴 (hand with whip; action). The bottom left 寸 has been replaced with 方.

文.originText: a man with a painted or tattooed chest – original form of 紋. The tattoo was usually a cross, a V shape or a stylized heart. In current form, tattoo has vanished, so simply an outline of a man (head, outstretched arms, legs, chest) similar to 立. Compare 大, which has no chest. Unrelated to the Kangxi radicals 齐 and 攵.

斉.originRaw:
Variant of {{m|mul|齊}}.

Unrelated to {{m|mul|文}}, but currently classified under that radical.
斉.originText: Variant of 齊. Unrelated to 文, but currently classified under that radical.

斑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 文 (pattern) + phonetic 班.

斗.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} (''{{w|Shuowen}}''), indicating a ladle-shaped dipper or cup used to measure grain (see below) held by hand. See also [[升]].
斗.originText: ('), indicating a ladle-shaped dipper or cup used to measure grain (see below) held by hand. See also 升.

料.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|米|斗|ls=ic|t1=rice|t2=dipper}} – to measure; to gauge.
料.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + semantic 斗 (dipper) – to measure; to gauge.

斜.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|斗|余|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=ladle/dipper}}. The character expresses the idea of scooping or drawing out. By extension, it is also used to mean "slant" or "diagonal."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
斜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 斗 (ladle/dipper) + phonetic 余. The character expresses the idea of scooping or drawing out. By extension, it is also used to mean "slant" or "diagonal."

斥.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally written {{zh-l|*㡿}}, a {{Han compound|广|屰|c1=s|c2=p|t1=building|t2=|ls=psc|nocap=y}}.

The {{zh-l|*屰}} later came to be written {{zh-l|*干}}, and the {{zh-l|*广}} was sometimes written as {{zh-l|*厂}}, eventually leading to the modern form of the character.

Alternatively, may be derived from {{zh-l|*宅}}.
斥.originText: Originally written 㡿, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 广 (building) + phonetic 屰. The 屰 later came to be written 干, and the 广 was sometimes written as 厂, eventually leading to the modern form of the character. Alternatively, may be derived from 宅.

斬.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|斤|車|ls=ic|c1=s|c2=s|t1=axe|t2=cart; vehicle}}. It refers to an ancient punishment in which a body was torn apart using carts, and by extension, conveys the meaning “to cut.” Another theory expresses the idea of cutting wood to make a vehicle.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
斬.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 斤 (axe) + semantic 車 (cart; vehicle). It refers to an ancient punishment in which a body was torn apart using carts, and by extension, conveys the meaning “to cut.” Another theory expresses the idea of cutting wood to make a vehicle.

新.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辛|斤|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc}} — to chop wood. Original form of {{och-l|薪|gloss=firewood}}. The character was later borrowed to represent {{och-l|新|new}} as an instance of {{liushu|j|nocap=y}}.

A semantic {{och-l|*木}} was later added in the bronze inscriptions which merged with the {{och-l|*辛}}.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' misinterprets the character as {{och-l|*𣓀}} + {{och-l|*斤}}.
新.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 辛 + semantic 斤 — to chop wood. Original form of 薪. The character was later borrowed to represent 新 as an instance of. A semantic 木 was later added in the bronze inscriptions which merged with the 辛. ' misinterprets the character as 𣓀 + 斤.

方.originText: Possibly the original character of 旁, with its form related to 巫. 巫 depicts four extremities with indicator symbols, being the original character of 荒 in 四荒. Compared to 巫, one end of this character lacks the indicator symbol and is elongated to denote "side" 旁. 方 in 四方 and 荒 in 四荒 may be cognates. It is unrelated to 㫃, from which characters like 旗 and 旅 are derived.

施.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 㫃 + phonetic 也.

旅.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㫃 (flag) + semantic 从 (two people) – brigade.

旋.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|㫃|止|〇|t1=flag|t2=foot|t3=circle|ls=ic}}. {{och-l|*〇}} is the original form of {{och-l|圓}} and also serves as a phonetic component. It has since merged with the {{och-l|*止}} into the unrelated {{och-l|*疋}}.<ref>[https://www.fdgwz.org.cn/Web/Show/11262 Gan Mu (2025), "說字（九則）"]</ref>
旋.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㫃 (flag) + semantic 止 (foot) + semantic 〇 (circle). 〇 is the original form of 圓 and also serves as a phonetic component. It has since merged with the 止 into the unrelated 疋.

族.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㫃 (flag) + semantic 矢 (arrow).

旗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 㫃 (flag) + phonetic 其.

既.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 皀 (bowl of rice) + semantic 旡 (kneeling figure) – person kneeling at bowl of rice – sitting down to eat (rice already finished cooking), turning away (already finished eating) or abstaining from eating or consuming. Note the stroke order in the right component 旡, which may not be clear in the compressed form of this character: the left vertical and second horizontal are one stroke with a corner, while the upper right vertical continues in a diagonal stroke to lower left.

日.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. {{l|zh|口}}. Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun ([[☉]]) and the Egyptian hieroglyph {{m|egy|𓇳}}.
日.originText: the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口. Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun (☉) and the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓇳.

旦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|日|丁|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}.

According to Shuowen Jiezi, the sun ({{lang|zh|日}}) appearing over the horizon ({{lang|zh|一}}). However, this version is not the original one and this interpretation belongs to folk etymology. This simplification is the same that appears in [[正]].

Unrelated to the top component of [[得]]. Also unrelated to [[查]].
旦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 + phonetic 丁. According to Shuowen Jiezi, the sun (日) appearing over the horizon (一). However, this version is not the original one and this interpretation belongs to folk etymology. This simplification is the same that appears in 正. Unrelated to the top component of 得. Also unrelated to 查.

旧.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|臼}}.

The reformative usage in simplified Chinese and Japanese that replaced {{l|mul|舊}} can be analysed either as from an elimination of {{l|mul|雈}} with glyphic alteration from {{l|mul|臼}} to {{l|mul|旧}} or as using a homophonic character.
旧.originText: Variant of 臼. The reformative usage in simplified Chinese and Japanese that replaced 舊 can be analysed either as from an elimination of 雈 with glyphic alteration from 臼 to 旧 or as using a homophonic character.

旨.originText: 匕 a spoon (匙) to eat or drink something delicious. The original version is 𠤔. See 嘗. Similar but unrelated to 皀. According to the Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 匕 + semantic 甘 (delicious).

早.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Early bronze inscriptions: {{liushu|p}} – acorn. Original form of {{och-l|皂}} through an intermediate variant [[皁]] (once also written as {{l|zh|草}}). Borrowed phonetically for "morning" sense.

Late bronze inscriptions: {{Han compound|日|棗|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=sun}}, with {{zh-l|*棗}} sometimes simplified as {{zh-l|*朿}}.

Small seal script: {{Han compound|日|甲|ls=ic|t1=sun|t2=first}} – when the sun first rises. However, Xu Shen's interpretation is not based on oracle bones and bronzes inscriptions.

In some ancient texts, {{och-l|蚤}} was often used instead.

Unrelated to the ancient version of [[是]]: in this character, it doesn't represent an acorn but a spoon.
早.originText: Early bronze inscriptions: – acorn. Original form of 皂 through an intermediate variant 皁 (once also written as 草). Borrowed phonetically for "morning" sense. Late bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 棗, with 棗 sometimes simplified as 朿. Small seal script: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + semantic 甲 (first) – when the sun first rises. However, Xu Shen's interpretation is not based on oracle bones and bronzes inscriptions. In some ancient texts, 蚤 was often used instead. Unrelated to the ancient version of 是: in this character, it doesn't represent an acorn but a spoon.

旬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 螾 + semantic 日 (sun; day). The pictographic protoform of 螾 was borrowed to represent "period of days" in oracle bone script. In bronze inscriptions, the semantic component 日 was added to this character. In the Warring States period, the phonetic component was mistaken as 勹, hence the incorrect analysis in ' of this character as Compound: 勹 + 日.

旺.originText: Simplified form of the original 暀, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 往. The current form is reanalyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 王.

昆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – the body and legs of an insect.
昆.originText: the body and legs of an insect.

昇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 升.

明.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}

{{Han compound|日|月|ls=ic|t1=sun|t2=moon}} – the sun just rising and the moon not yet set – dawn ({{l|zh|天明}}). Alternatively, it may be interpreted as two bright celestial bodies – bright. This form was already found in the oracle bone script and was prevalent throughout the eras.

Three other forms were found in the oracle bone script:
* {{l|zh|朙}} < {{Han compound|囧|月|t1=window}} – the moon shining through a window – moonlight. This form was also prevalent in the ancient scripts and was considered to be the standard form in ''{{w|Shuowen}}''. See this form's entry for its historical forms.
* {{l|zh|眀}} < {{Han compound|目|月|t1=eye}} – bright eyes. This form was rarely attested, so it is still uncertain whether this form is actually equivalent to {{lang|zh|明}}. It reappeared in the bamboo script of the {{w|Qin dynasty}}, but this was probably a corruption of {{l|zh|朙}}.
* {{l|zh|𤰾}} < {{Han compound|田|月}} – probably a corruption of the above forms.
明.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + semantic 月 (moon) – the sun just rising and the moon not yet set – dawn (天明). Alternatively, it may be interpreted as two bright celestial bodies – bright. This form was already found in the oracle bone script and was prevalent throughout the eras. Three other forms were found in the oracle bone script:

易.originText: and s: a of a filled container, the original form of 賜. Possibly specialised from 益. Perhaps borrowed phonetically to mean "easy". The character is not the pictogram of a chameleon, as folk etymology says. Unrelated to 陽 since it doesn't represent the sun.

昔.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|龷|日|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=sun; day|tr=*sak}}. 

The semantic {{zh-l|*日}} indicates "past days". The phonetic top component originally depicted "rough/wrinkled" or "intertwined" textures; it was an independent character and the original ideogram for {{och-l|*腊|tr=*sak}} and {{och-l|*皵|tr=*sak}}.<ref>陳劍「說「昔」字並論「𡿧」形的真正來源」『饒宗頤國學院院刊』第八期 香港浸會大學饒宗頤國學院、2021年、1–46頁。</ref>

{{w|Shuowen}}: {{Han compound|仌|日|ls=ic}} – two pieces of flesh ({{zh-l|*仌}}) dried in the sun ({{zh-l|*日}}). Original form of {{zh-l|*腊}} (dried meat).

Similar but unrelated to [[展]], [[共]], and [[散]].
昔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 龷 + semantic 日 (sun; day). The semantic 日 indicates "past days". The phonetic top component originally depicted "rough/wrinkled" or "intertwined" textures; it was an independent character and the original ideogram for 腊 and 皵. Ideogrammic compound: semantic 仌 + semantic 日 – two pieces of flesh (仌) dried in the sun (日). Original form of 腊 (dried meat). Similar but unrelated to 展, 共, and 散.

星.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|晶|生|c1=p|c2=p|t1=twinkling stars}}. {{och-l|*晶}} originally referred to this word; a phonetic {{och-l|*生}} was added later ([[Wiktionary:About Chinese/references#J|Ji Xusheng, 2004]]). {{och-l|*晶}} was later simplified into {{och-l|*日}}.
星.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 晶 (twinkling stars) + phonetic 生. 晶 originally referred to this word; a phonetic 生 was added later (Ji Xusheng, 2004). 晶 was later simplified into 日.

映.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 央.

春.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 屯 (swollen sprout) + semantic 日 (sun). Some oracle-bone and bronze forms contain only two components, either 艸/屮 with 屯, or 日 with 屯. The form 萅 preserves the older arrangement with 艸. In the regular script, the 艸 and 屯 have merged into 𡗗.

昧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun; day) + phonetic 未.

昨.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|日|乍|c1=s|c2=p|t1=sun|ls=psc}}. However, the phonetic component could add part of the meaning since it was borrowed phonetically to mean "at first".
昨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 乍. However, the phonetic component could add part of the meaning since it was borrowed phonetically to mean "at first".

昭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 召.

是.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Unclear. Possibly taken from an oracle-bone form of {{och-l|智|tr=*treh}}, composed of {{zh-l|*子}}, {{zh-l|*止}} and {{zh-l|*冊}}.<ref>陳劍：《古文字基礎形體研究》，南京大學文學院暑期班課程，2022年。</ref><ref>詹鄞鑫：《釋甲骨文“知”字——兼説商代的舊禮與新禮》，《華夏考：詹鄞鑫文字訓詁論集》，北京：中華書局，2006年，第369～375頁。</ref><ref>李艾希：《考釋商周古文所見“智”字構形之三個問題》，《中國文字》2022年冬季號（總第8期）</ref>
是.originText: Unclear. Possibly taken from an oracle-bone form of 智, composed of 子, 止 and 冊.

時.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun; day) + phonetic 之 (to go) — the passing of time. In ancient scripts, it had the form 旹. The phonetic component later changed to 寺.

普.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 並 (side by side) + semantic 日 (sun).

景.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|日|京|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=sun}}. Originally, it meant "sunlight". Compare [[昜]].
景.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 京. Originally, it meant "sunlight". Compare 昜.

晴.originText: Written as 夝 in ' and as 星 in the '. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 青.

暇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 叚

暑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 + phonetic 者.

暖.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|日|爰|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=sun}}. Later also used as a variant of {{zh-l|煖}} which is used as another word with different pronunciation.
暖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 爰. Later also used as a variant of 煖 which is used as another word with different pronunciation.

暗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 音.

暫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 斬 + semantic 日.

暮.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|莫|日|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t1=sunset}}. {{och-l|*莫}} is the original pictogram for this word; an additional {{och-l|*日}} was added to distinguish.
暮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 莫 (sunset) + semantic 日. 莫 is the original pictogram for this word; an additional 日 was added to distinguish.

暴.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Its original form is {{och-l|*𫻺}} and can be seen on oracle bone script; {{Han compound|ls=ic|虎|戈|t1=tiger|t2=weapon|nocap=y}} – violence. The character also means "to expose to the sun", but its most archaic form does not convey this particular meaning.

However, by the time of bamboo slip script, usage of {{lang|zh|𫻺}} had been replaced entirely by phonetically borrowing {{lang|zh|㬥}}. This new character originates from the proto-form 𮲡, an {{Han compound|ls=ic|nocap=y|日|共|t1=sun|t2=hands lifting an object}}; in this precise case, the hands are lifting a plant graphically similar to [[丰]] or [[出]]. {{zh-l|*米|rice}} was later added to emphasize the meaning of drying things out in the sun since rice and similar plants can be dried out in the sun. Eventually, the bottom component was stylized as the unrelated [[水]] and the whole character was stylized into {{lang|zh|暴}}: the plant is no more visible in the new version.

The meaning "to expose to the sun" is preserved in {{lang|zh|𣌑}} > {{och-l|*曝}}.
暴.originText: Its original form is 𫻺 and can be seen on oracle bone script; Ideogrammic compound: semantic 虎 (tiger) + semantic 戈 (weapon) – violence. The character also means "to expose to the sun", but its most archaic form does not convey this particular meaning. However, by the time of bamboo slip script, usage of 𫻺 had been replaced entirely by phonetically borrowing 㬥. This new character originates from the proto-form 𮲡, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + semantic 共 (hands lifting an object); in this precise case, the hands are lifting a plant graphically similar to 丰 or 出. 米 was later added to emphasize the meaning of drying things out in the sun since rice and similar plants can be dried out in the sun. Eventually, the bottom component was stylized as the unrelated 水 and the whole character was stylized into 暴: the plant is no more visible in the new version. The meaning "to expose to the sun" is preserved in 𣌑 > 曝.

曇.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|日|雲|ls=ic}}, presumably “sun behind clouds”.
曇.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 日 + semantic 雲, presumably “sun behind clouds”.

曖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 愛.

曜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 (sun) + phonetic 翟.

曲.originText: a bent object. Also 麴 via the variant character 麯. Unrelated to 曹 and 典.

更.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally an {{liushu|3|nocap=yes}}, showing two chariots ({{lang|zh|丙}}). Later {{lang|zh|攴}} was added and a {{lang|zh|丙}} omitted to create the form seen in the Shuowen Jiezi ({{lang|zh|㪅}}), a {{Han compound|ls=psc|𰀒|攴|c1=p|c2=s|t1=two chariots|t2=hand holding a whip; action|abb1=yes|nocap=yes}}. The remaining {{lang|zh|丙}} eventually corrupted into a shape similar to {{lang|zh|雨}}.
更.originText: Originally an, showing two chariots (丙). Later 攴 was added and a 丙 omitted to create the form seen in the Shuowen Jiezi (㪅), a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𰀒 (two chariots) + semantic 攴 (hand holding a whip; action). The remaining 丙 eventually corrupted into a shape similar to 雨.

書.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 聿 (writing brush) + phonetic 者.

曹.originText: Originally 㯥, an : two bundles 東. The original meaning is "pair; peer, same kind". Later, 囗 was added as a distinguishing mark, which corrupted into 甘 in bronze inscriptions and 曰 in Seal Script, thus arriving at the intermediate character form 𣍘. The top two 東 have merged and now resemble 曲 with an extra stroke. Unrelated to 曲 and 典.

曽.originRaw: Original form of 曾,<ref>{{cite-book|en|author=Roar Bökset|url=https://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archivedate=2021-12-02|series=Stockholm East Asian Monographs|volume=11|year=2006|publisher=Stockholm University|title=Long Story of Short Forms: The Evolution of Simplified Chinese Characters|isbn=978-91-628-6832-1|page=72|pageurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01#page=76}}</ref> used in compound characters such as {{lang|ja|[[増]]}} (from {{lang|und|sc=Hani|増}}).
曽.originText: Original form of 曾, used in compound characters such as 増 (from sc=Hani).

替.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|竝|曰|ls=ic}} – two figures ({{lang|zh|竝}}) changing places. Two top components have been simplified from {{zh-l|*立}} to {{zh-l|*夫}}.
替.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 竝 + semantic 曰 – two figures (竝) changing places. Two top components have been simplified from 立 to 夫.

最.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{och-l|㝡}}, {{Han compound|ls=psc|宀|取|c1=s|c2=p|t1=roof|nocap=1}} – "to gather". Later {{och-l|*二}} was added as distinguishing marks to disambiguate the character for the meaning "the most". The top components have corrupted into {{och-l|*冃}} in the traditional form. These components were further corrupted into {{och-l|*曰}} in the simplified version.
最.originText: Originally 㝡, Phono-semantic compound: semantic 宀 (roof) + phonetic 取 – "to gather". Later 二 was added as distinguishing marks to disambiguate the character for the meaning "the most". The top components have corrupted into 冃 in the traditional form. These components were further corrupted into 曰 in the simplified version.

月.originText: pictographic representation of a crescent moon. Related to 夕 and interchangeable in the past, but both are unrelated to 多, in which it represents two pieces of meat stylized as 夕. Unrelated to:

有.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|又|肉|t2=meat|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. The hand shape has been abstracted to {{och-l|*𠂇}}; compare {{och-l|*右}}, where {{och-l|*又}} has also taken this shape. The {{och-l|*肉}} in turn has taken the form of {{och-l|*⺼}}.

The character may have been the original form of {{och-l|侑|to urge to eat}}. Alternatively, it may be the original form of  {{och-l|醢|gloss=minced pickled meat}}, which also has the {{och-l|又}} element as phonetic.

Folk etymology traditionally explains it as a hand holding meat, hence “in possession of”. However, the oracle bone script shows no meat.

''{{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}'' and other ancient sources have erroneously analyzed the character as a {{Han compound|又|c1=p|月|c2=s|t2=moon|ls=psc|nocap=1}}. ''Shuowen Jiezi'' defines {{lang|zh|有}} as "{{lang|zh|不宜有也}}" ("[to have something that] not should be had"), citing the ''{{w|Spring and Autumn Annals}}'' ({{lang|zh|春秋傳}}): "{{lang|zh|日月有食之}}" ("There are solar and lunar eclipses"). As eclipses were not auspicious to the Chinese, they were "something that should not be happening". The {{lang|zh|月}} component alludes to the inauspicious lunar eclipse.
有.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 又 + semantic 肉 (meat). The hand shape has been abstracted to 𠂇; compare 右, where 又 has also taken this shape. The 肉 in turn has taken the form of ⺼. The character may have been the original form of 侑. Alternatively, it may be the original form of 醢, which also has the 又 element as phonetic. Folk etymology traditionally explains it as a hand holding meat, hence “in possession of”. However, the oracle bone script shows no meat. ' and other ancient sources have erroneously analyzed the character as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 又 + semantic 月 (moon). Shuowen Jiezi defines 有 as "不宜有也" ("[to have something that] not should be had"), citing the ' (春秋傳): "日月有食之" ("There are solar and lunar eclipses"). As eclipses were not auspicious to the Chinese, they were "something that should not be happening". The 月 component alludes to the inauspicious lunar eclipse.

服.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 凡 (tray) + phonetic 𠬝 (to subdue) – to serve. 𠬝 is the original pictogram for this character; 凡 was added later. 凡 here has been corrupted into 舟 and subsequently 月.

朕.originText: 𦩎舟月 Oracle-bone forms depict a 舟 (“boat”) beside two hands holding a rod-like object. In 合集 20610, a variant shows one hand holding the object, which overlaps with the prow of the boat. The graph may be transcribed as ⿰舟尹, and has been identified with 朕. The graph may be interpreted as an ideograph for 乘 (“to mount; to ascend; to board”). In Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, 朕 is used as a first-person genitive pronoun of deference, commonly before terms for ancestors, parents, or rulers; it is also used as a loan for 媵 in the sense “to send; to escort; to accompany; to transfer”. The traditional sense “sign; trace; evidence”, also written 眹, may be related to 證, 徵 and 應.

朗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 良 + semantic 月 (moon)

望.originText: Originally written 𦣠, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 臣 (eye) + semantic 𡈼 (person standing on the ground) – a person standing up and looking off into the distance. Later 月 was added to produce 朢. The 臣 component is now written 亡, making the current form a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亡 + semantic 月 + semantic 𡈼.

朝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

In the oracle bone script, it was an {{liushu|ic|nocap=1}}: 2 or 4 {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|屮||grass}} or even {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|木||tree}} + {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|日||sun}} + {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|月||moon}} – the sun rising above the ground while the waning moon is still in the sky – the morning.

In the bronze script, it was a compound of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𠦝}} and a pictograph of a river ({{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|川}} or {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|水}}) – this was possibly an original form for {{och-l|潮|gloss=tide}}. The river glyph may be a corruption of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|月}} due to association with tides or diurnal events. {{zh-ref|Chi (2010)}} considers such forms to be {{liushu|psc|nocap=1|adj=1}}, where {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𠦝}} is the abbreviated form of the phonetic {{och-l|朝}}. In the some late Western Zhou forms, {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𠦝}} was corrupted into a form resembling {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|車}}.

According to {{w|Guo Moruo}}, in the stone drum inscriptions ({{lw|zh|石鼓文}}, likely from the {{w|Spring and Autumn period}}) {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|㫃}} was added (attached to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|車}}), and the river glyph was replaced with {{och-l|舟}}, which was interpreted as the phonetic component; the small seal script might have inherited from this form. ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interpreted the fused components of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𠦝}} and {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|㫃}} as a semantic component {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|倝||dawn}}. However, the accuracy of identification has been questioned; the character was a heavily weathered one in which the {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|㫃}} identification was probably spurious and likely influenced by the ''{{w|Shuowen}}''. Meanwhile, the {{lang|zh|舟}} component on the right remained somewhat legible.<ref>{{cite-journal|zh|title=zh:郭沫若《石鼓文研究》摹本及释文辨正|author=zh:徐宝贵|journal={{lang|zh|考古学报}}|date=2007-07-15|issue=2007-03|pages=313–338}}</ref>

The {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|舟}} component remained in the {{w|bamboo and wooden slips}} of the {{w|Warring States period}} (see the table). In the clerical script since the {{w|Han dynasty}}, {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|舟}} had been reverted to {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|月}}; it is unclear whether this was a remnant from {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|月}} in the oracle bone script or a corruption of {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|舟}} (as in {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|朕}} < {{l-lite|zh|sc=Hani|𦩎}} and many other characters). The current form is essentially inherited from the clerical script.
朝.originText: In the oracle bone script, it was an : 2 or 4 屮 or even 木 + 日 + 月 – the sun rising above the ground while the waning moon is still in the sky – the morning. In the bronze script, it was a compound of 𠦝 and a pictograph of a river (川 or 水) – this was possibly an original form for 潮. The river glyph may be a corruption of 月 due to association with tides or diurnal events. considers such forms to be, where 𠦝 is the abbreviated form of the phonetic 朝. In the some late Western Zhou forms, 𠦝 was corrupted into a form resembling 車. According to, in the stone drum inscriptions (石鼓文, likely from the ) 㫃 was added (attached to 車), and the river glyph was replaced with 舟, which was interpreted as the phonetic component; the small seal script might have inherited from this form. ' interpreted the fused components of 𠦝 and 㫃 as a semantic component 倝. However, the accuracy of identification has been questioned; the character was a heavily weathered one in which the 㫃 identification was probably spurious and likely influenced by the '. Meanwhile, the 舟 component on the right remained somewhat legible. The 舟 component remained in the of the (see the table). In the clerical script since the, 舟 had been reverted to 月; it is unclear whether this was a remnant from 月 in the oracle bone script or a corruption of 舟 (as in 朕 < 𦩎 and many other characters). The current form is essentially inherited from the clerical script.

期.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 其 + semantic 日. The original composition with the semantic 日 is preserved in the variant forms 㫷 and 𣇳. The sun then changed to 月 to produce 朞, from which the character then evolved to the current form.

木.originText: a tree: branches on top, roots on the bottom (more visible in earlier forms). See also 本, 未, and 末.

未.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: a tree ({{zh-l|*木}}) with superposed or lush branches. Likely the original form of {{och-l|枚|stem; branch}}.
未.originText: a tree (木) with superposed or lush branches. Likely the original form of 枚.

末.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: a tree ({{zh-l|*木}}) with its top highlighted with an extra stroke, implying the meaning of “apex”; contrast {{zh-l|*本|}}, {{zh-l|*朱}}.
末.originText: a tree (木) with its top highlighted with an extra stroke, implying the meaning of “apex”; contrast 本, 朱.

本.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: a tree ({{l|zh|木}}) with its bottom highlighted with an extra stroke, accentuating the roots; contrast {{l|zh|末|}}, {{l|zh|朱}}.
本.originText: a tree (木) with its bottom highlighted with an extra stroke, accentuating the roots; contrast 末, 朱.

札.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|木|乙|alt2=乚|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=wood}}. It represents a thinly shaved wooden tag and, by extension, a tag or document on which characters are written.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
札.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 乙. It represents a thinly shaved wooden tag and, by extension, a tag or document on which characters are written.

朱.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}}: a tree ({{zh-l|*木}}) with its center highlighted with an extra dot-like stroke, accentuating the tree's core; contrast {{zh-l|*本|}}, {{zh-l|*末}}.
朱.originText: a tree (木) with its center highlighted with an extra dot-like stroke, accentuating the tree's core; contrast 本, 末.

朴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 卜. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 樸 (etymology 6) in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (漢字簡化方案漢字簡化方案) in 1956.

机.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree; wood) + phonetic 几.

朽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 丂.

杉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 彡.

材.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 才.

村.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 寸. Origin unclear. Seems a late graph, not in Shuowen dictionary of ca.100AD. Ogawa treats it as variant of CO graph 杶* "lacquer tree" which was used phonetically in the sense of "village" in place of another graph for "village", 邨*, which may be taken provisionally as 阝* "settlement, village", and 屯* "accumulate, stay" as semantic and phonetic.

束.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}} – bag tied at both ends (earlier forms were often vertically symmetric). See also {{zh-l|*東}} and {{zh-l|*柬}}.
束.originText: bag tied at both ends (earlier forms were often vertically symmetric). See also 東 and 柬.

杯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|不|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. According to a variant, the phonetic component is [[否]], which also had the ancient meaning of "to block", perhaps referred to liquids in a glass.
杯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 不. According to a variant, the phonetic component is 否, which also had the ancient meaning of "to block", perhaps referred to liquids in a glass.

東.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: a pictogram of a full {{och-l|橐|tr=*tʰˤak|t=bag}} tied at both ends. It is the original form of {{zh-l|*重}}: forms with a human figure gave rise to {{och-l|重|tr=*droŋ;droŋʔ;droŋh}}, while forms without it gave rise to {{och-l|東|tr=*tˤoŋ}}.<ref>張富海《說字二則》</ref><ref>施瑞峰《“束”的上古聲母及相關古文字問題補說》</ref>

Interpreted in the {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}} as an {{liushu|ic|nocap=yes}} the sun ({{zh-l|*日}}) rising behind a tree ({{zh-l|*木}}). According to {{zh-ref|Allan (1991)}} p. 47-50, the character represents the {{w|Fu Sang}} tree. However, the original form is rather different, hence any interpretation tied to a tree is most likely a folk etymology. 

See the top component of [[曹]] in the original version. See also [[柬]], [[熏]], [[西]] and [[鹵]]/[[卤]].
東.originText: a pictogram of a full 橐 tied at both ends. It is the original form of 重: forms with a human figure gave rise to 重, while forms without it gave rise to 東. Interpreted in the as an the sun (日) rising behind a tree (木). According to p. 47-50, the character represents the tree. However, the original form is rather different, hence any interpretation tied to a tree is most likely a folk etymology. See the top component of 曹 in the original version. See also 柬, 熏, 西 and 鹵/卤.

松.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 公.

板.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 反. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 闆 (etymology 2) in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (漢字簡化方案漢字簡化方案) in 1956.

析.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|木|斤|t1=wood|t2=axe}} - to split wood.
析.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + semantic 斤 (axe) - to split wood.

枕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 冘.

林.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{zh-etym-double|木|tree}} to give the idea of multiple trees (compare {{zh-l|*森}}), thus a forest. See also the top component of [[散]] in its original version.
林.originText: doubled 木 (tree) to give the idea of multiple trees (compare 森), thus a forest. See also the top component of 散 in its original version.

枚.originText: Generally thought to be an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 木 (tree; wood) + semantic 攴 (hand holding a stick). However, considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 文, where 文 was later corrupted to 攴.

果.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – fruits on a tree. Related to the original form of [[采]]. Compare [[栗]] and [[某]]. Unrelated to [[喿]].
果.originText: fruits on a tree. Related to the original form of 采. Compare 栗 and 某. Unrelated to 喿.

枝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 支 (branch).

枠.originRaw: {{ja-etym-kokuji}}. {{Han compound|木|卆|lang=ja}}; it is not a simplification of {{Han compound|木|卒|lang=ja}} ({{ja-l|椊}}).
枠.originText: Compound: 木 + 卆; it is not a simplification of Compound: 木 + 卒 (椊).

枯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 古.

架.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|加|木|t2=tree, wood|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a wooden prop.
架.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 加 + semantic 木 (tree, wood) – a wooden prop.

柄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|t1=wood|丙|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a wooden handle.
柄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 丙 – a wooden handle.

某.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + semantic 甘 (sweet); original form of 梅. Later borrowed to represent 某. Similar to 果 and 栗. Similar but unrelated to 柑.

染.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 水 (water) + semantic 九 (hook) + semantic 木 (tree) – to hang (on a hook 九) from a tree (木) into water (氵), so as to dye. Earlier forms more often graphically Compound: 水 + 杂; in the modern form, the water radical is moved upward to the upper-left corner.

柔.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|矛|木|t2=tree|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – wood soft enough that it can easily be cut.
柔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 矛 + semantic 木 (tree) – wood soft enough that it can easily be cut.

柱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 主.

柳.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|卯|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} in oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions.

Later {{zh-l|*桺}} ({{Han compound|木|丣|c1=s|c2=p}}) in small seal script.

The glyph finally turned back to {{l|zh|木}} + {{l|zh|卯}} in the current form.
柳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 卯 in oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions. Later 桺 (Compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 丣) in small seal script. The glyph finally turned back to 木 + 卯 in the current form.

components.sense: a form made by lining up pieces of wood and binding them together

柵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree; wood) + phonetic 冊 (a form made by lining up pieces of wood and binding them together).

査.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|木|且|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=wood}}. It represents the idea of a raft made from assembled wood. The original character is [[楂]]. It is later borrowed to mean "to examine" or "to investigate."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
査.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 且. It represents the idea of a raft made from assembled wood. The original character is 楂. It is later borrowed to mean "to examine" or "to investigate."

柿.originText: Originally written as 柹: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 𠂔. The current form is Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 市.

栓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 全 – a wooden peg.

校.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 交.

株.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 朱.

核.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 亥 – a kind of tree. Modern meanings are borrowed.

根.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 艮.

格.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 各.

栽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 𢦏.

桁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 行.

桃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 兆.

案.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 安.

桑.originText: of a mulberry tree. What were the shape of the tree's foliage is now 叒.

梅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 每.

梗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 更 – a type of plant.

械.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|木|戒|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=wood}}. The character originally represented the meaning of "handcuffs" or "shackles," and by extension, it came to be used to mean "device" or "mechanism."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
械.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 戒. The character originally represented the meaning of "handcuffs" or "shackles," and by extension, it came to be used to mean "device" or "mechanism."

棄.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 子 (child) + semantic 𠀠 (basket) + semantic 廾 (two hands) - throwing out a child in a basket. 子 was often inverted as 𠫓. In the oracle bone script form, 子 may appear with dots on either side of its head and body, perhaps representing amniotic fluid or dust.

棋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wooden) + phonetic 其.

棒.originRaw:

{{Han compound|木|t1=tree, wood|奉|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a wooden club.
棒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree, wood) + phonetic 奉 – a wooden club.

棚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 朋

棟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 東.

森.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}: {{zh-etym-triple|木|tree}}, to suggest a large number (compare {{zh-l|*三}}) of [[trees]] such as one would find in a [[forest]]. Compare {{l|och|林}}.
森.originText: tripled 木 (tree), to suggest a large number (compare 三) of trees such as one would find in a forest. Compare 林.

棺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 官.

椅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 奇.

植.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 直.

椎.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|木|隹|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=tree}}. It expresses the idea of a piece of wood used to smash things, signifying a “hammer” or “mallet.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
椎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 隹. It expresses the idea of a piece of wood used to smash things, signifying a “hammer” or “mallet.”

業.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Various explanations exist:
* {{liushu|p}} – [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:20230208_Chime_bells_of_Marquis_Yi_of_Zeng.jpg a beam from which bells and chimes hang].<ref name="漢多">[https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf/search.php?word=%E6%A5%AD 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 「業」]</ref>
* {{liushu|p}} – a person lifting said beam.<ref name="字源 ">李学勤，2012《字源》，Tianjin: 天津古籍出版社。p.199</ref>
* {{Han compound|丵|大|t1=chisel|t2=person; big|ls=ic}} – to launch a great attack.<ref name="說文新證">季旭昇，2004《說文新證》，台北：藝文印書館印行，2014年9月第二版。p.169</ref>
Up until the {{w|Warring States}} period, the character was written doubled as {{och-l|*𪴨}} and sometimes as {{och-l|*𫨱}}. The latter is a {{liushu|psc|nocap=y}} using {{och-l|*去}} (the original form of {{och-l|盍}}) as a phonetic component. In {{w|bamboo slips}} the vertical stroke of 丵 extended such that the bottom looks like 木.
<references/>
業.originText: Various explanations exist: Up until the period, the character was written doubled as 𪴨 and sometimes as 𫨱. The latter is a using 去 (the original form of 盍) as a phonetic component. In the vertical stroke of 丵 extended such that the bottom looks like 木.

極.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|亟|c1=s|t1=tree, wood|c2=p|ls=psc}} – originally meaning a [[crossbeam]] [[rafter]].
極.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree, wood) + phonetic 亟 – originally meaning a crossbeam rafter.

楷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 皆.

楽.originRaw: Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|樂|nocap=y}} ({{l|zh|𢆶}} → ⿱{{l|zh|[[丷]][[八]]}}) found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary <big>《字學三正》</big>.<!-- Refer http://dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/variants/rbt/word_attribute.rbt?quote_code=QTAyMDE2LTAwMw#33 --> Also found in 《{{lw|zh|宋元以來俗字譜}}》, a {{w|Variant Chinese character|variant forms}} dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms ({{l|zh|俗字}}) that have existed since the {{w|Song dynasty}}.
楽.originText: Unorthodox variant 樂 (𢆶 → ⿱丷八) found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《字學三正》. Also found in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the.

概.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 既 – strickle.

構.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 冓.

様.originRaw:
Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|樣|f=羕|t=𣴎}}; compare bottom of [[暴]].

Right component is approximately 𦍌 + 氺.
<!--
Right component is approximately 羊 + 水, but this is misleading. The composition is more similar to [[隶]]: there is a single vertical stroke (not two separate characters), and the bottom left component is drawn as two strokes, as in [[冫]], not one stroke, as in the left side of 水.
-->
様.originText: Japanese shinjitai 樣羕𣴎; compare bottom of 暴. Right component is approximately 𦍌 + 氺.

槽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 曹 – a wooden trough or vat.

標.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 票.

樹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|尌|c1=s|c2=p|t1=tree|t2=to plant a tree|ls=psc}}. Originally written as {{och-l|*尌}}; an extra {{och-l|*木}} was added to differentiate.
樹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + phonetic 尌 (to plant a tree). Originally written as 尌; an extra 木 was added to differentiate.

橋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 (wood) + phonetic 喬.

機.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 木 + phonetic 幾.

欠.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a kneeling person with mouth open for various reasons (e.g., begging 欠, speaking and/or spitting while speaking [[次]], blowing [[吹]], singing [[歌]], desiring [[欲]], being tired [[軟]], vomiting [[歐]]...).

The reversed version of this character is 㒫 > {{zh-l|*旡}} (e.g. 既), which must not be confused with 无.

Similar but unrelated to [[卩]], in which the person kneeling has the mouth shut.
欠.originText: a kneeling person with mouth open for various reasons (e.g., begging 欠, speaking and/or spitting while speaking 次, blowing 吹, singing 歌, desiring 欲, being tired 軟, vomiting 歐...). The reversed version of this character is 㒫 > 旡 (e.g. 既), which must not be confused with 无. Similar but unrelated to 卩, in which the person kneeling has the mouth shut.

次.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}} {{liushu|p}}: a person exhaling.徐山 「釈“次”」 『語言科学』第2巻4期、92-94頁。
黄徳寛主編 『古文字譜系疏証』 商務印書館、2007年、3066頁。
林志強等評注 『《文源》評注』 中国社会科学出版社、2017年、515頁。 Possibly the original form of {{och-l|咨|to sigh}}. {{Shuowen}} incorrectly interprets it as a phono-semantic compound of {{och-l|二}} + {{och-l|*欠}}, refuted by ancient forms of the character.趙彤 「利用古文字資料考訂幾個上古音問題」 『語言研究的務実与創新——慶祝胡明揚教授八十華誕学術論文集』 中国人民大学中文系編、外語教学与研究出版社、2014年、400頁。 The breath or saliva is is represented by {{och-l|*二}} or {{och-l|*冫}}, depending on the font. An old variant of the character is [[𣄭]]. See [[曰]], [[丂]], [[于]], [[只]], which also feature depictions of breathing. Unrelated to [[㳄]], which means "saliva" instead.
次.originText: a person exhaling. Possibly the original form of 咨. incorrectly interprets it as a phono-semantic compound of 二 + 欠, refuted by ancient forms of the character. The breath or saliva is is represented by 二 or 冫, depending on the font. An old variant of the character is 𣄭. See 曰, 丂, 于, 只, which also feature depictions of breathing. Unrelated to 㳄, which means "saliva" instead.

欲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 谷 + semantic 欠.

欺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 其 + semantic 欠 (breath)

款.originText: Originally 歀, Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 柰 + semantic 欠 (lacking, desire) + no_och=yes, meaning “desire”. The 木 component was simplified into 士 via, similar to 隸//. interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 窾 + semantic 欠 (lacking, desire).

歌.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|哥|欠|t2=blow|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. Specialized form of {{och-l|哥|to sing}}.
歌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 哥 + semantic 欠 (blow). Specialized form of 哥.

止.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a footprint pointing up, originally meaning "foot"; stylized as [[龰]]. The derivative {{och-l|趾}} refers to the original meaning. Compare {{zh-l|*手|hand}}. Note that in oracle script, composed of 3 toes and a sole.

Compare to {{zh-l|*夊}}, {{zh-l|*夂}}, which have similar shape in oracle script, but pointing down (toe pointing right), and {{zh-l|*𡕒}} (as in right side of {{zh-l|*舛}}, roughly {{zh-l|*ヰ}}, toe pointing left), hence different evolution.

Compare to [[丑]], which is the pictogram of an animal claw.

Eventually, note that the foot is represented with three toes, like the human hand in the characters {{zh-l|*爪}}, {{zh-l|*寸}}, {{zh-l|*九}}, {{zh-l|*又}}, and [[彐]].
止.originText: a footprint pointing up, originally meaning "foot"; stylized as 龰. The derivative 趾 refers to the original meaning. Compare 手. Note that in oracle script, composed of 3 toes and a sole. Compare to 夊, 夂, which have similar shape in oracle script, but pointing down (toe pointing right), and 𡕒 (as in right side of 舛, roughly ヰ, toe pointing left), hence different evolution. Compare to 丑, which is the pictogram of an animal claw. Eventually, note that the foot is represented with three toes, like the human hand in the characters 爪, 寸, 九, 又, and 彐.

正.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丁 + semantic 止 Oracle bone and Shang–Zhou bronze forms show 丁 with 止. Some late Western Zhou and early Spring and Autumn bronze forms reduce 丁 to a horizontal stroke joined to 止. Later bronze and Chu bamboo forms often show 上 over 止; one-stroke forms also occur in Chu bamboo slips. In oracle bone script, the graph is used for the word later written 征.

武.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 戈 (dagger-axe) + semantic 止 (foot; to walk; to stop) – army going on an expedition. In the character 武, the 戈 component is written above the 止 component. The graphical origin of 武 as “to stop violence” — the ultimate state of just warfare — is traditionally attributed to King Zhuang of Chu {{defdate|597 }}: {{zh-x|^楚 ^子 曰：「非 爾 所 知{zhī} 也。夫{fú} 文，止 戈 為{wéi} 武。」|Said Lord "Chǔ" (楚): “Not exactly as what you might have believed. The term itself means: stopping ("止") the blades ("戈") thus martiality ("武").”|CL|ref=Zuozhuan|collapsed=y}} Linguistically, this was likely a misinterpretation, as 止 always means “to walk” (趾) when used as a radical, compare 步, 歷 and 歧.

歩.originRaw: Assimilation of the bottom component {{m|zh|𣥂}} to the more common {{m|zh|少}}. While continuously proscribed, it has appeared since the Han era.
歩.originText: Assimilation of the bottom component 𣥂 to the more common 少. While continuously proscribed, it has appeared since the Han era.

歯.originRaw:
Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|齒|nocap=y}} ({{l|zh|⿳[[从]][[一]][[从]]}} → {{l|zh|米}}) found in various {{w|Movable type#Metal movable type in China|moveable type}} copies of classical novels.

First attested in 《{{lw|zh|宋元以來俗字譜}}》, a {{w|Variant Chinese character|variant forms}} dictionary compiled in 1930.
歯.originText: Unorthodox variant 齒 (⿳从一从 → 米) found in various copies of classical novels. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a dictionary compiled in 1930.

歴.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|歷}}, {{Han simp|歷|f=秝|t=林|nocap=1}}.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
歴.originText: Variant of 歷, 歷秝林. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

死.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 歹 + phonetic 尸.

殉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 歹 + phonetic 旬.

殊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 歹 + phonetic 朱.

残.originRaw: {{Han simp|殘|f=戔|t=㦮}} for Japanese shinjitai and {{Han simp|殘|f=戔|t=戋|nocap=y}} for simplified Chinese.
残.originText: 殘戔㦮 for Japanese shinjitai and 殘戔戋 for simplified Chinese.

殖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 歹 + phonetic 直.

段.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the bronze script it is a {{Han compound|厂|殳|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc|ls2=ic|nocap=y}}, showing a hammer in hand breaking a stone with fragments coming off ({{zh-ref|Li Xueqin, 2012}}); 殳 was the pictogram of a hammer and later was borrowed to indicate a bamboo halberd. Most of the character is identical to [[叚]].
段.originText: In the bronze script it is a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 厂 + semantic 殳, showing a hammer in hand breaking a stone with fragments coming off ; 殳 was the pictogram of a hammer and later was borrowed to indicate a bamboo halberd. Most of the character is identical to 叚.

殺.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the oracle bone script, it was an {{liushu|ic|nocap=y}} of a boar that had been impaled in the head.

In the seal script, the original compound was corrupted into {{zh-l|𣏂}} (sometimes written as {{zh-l|杀}}). It was also in the seal script that the {{Han compound|人|又|t1=person|t2=right hand|ls=p|nocap=y}}, which was later corrupted into {{zh-l|*殳|spear}} or {{zh-l|*攴}}, was added under the head of the boar to specify the killing was done by a person.

The modern-day character inherits this and can be thought of as a {{Han compound|𣏂|c1=p|殳|c2=s|t2=spear|ls=psc|nocap=yes}}.
殺.originText: In the oracle bone script, it was an of a boar that had been impaled in the head. In the seal script, the original compound was corrupted into 𣏂 (sometimes written as 杀). It was also in the seal script that the Pictogram: 人 (person) + 又 (right hand), which was later corrupted into 殳 or 攴, was added under the head of the boar to specify the killing was done by a person. The modern-day character inherits this and can be thought of as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𣏂 + semantic 殳 (spear).

殿.originText: ': Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臀 + semantic 殳 (hand holding a weapon) – the sound of hitting (not attested in ancient documents). considers the character to be developed from 𠂤; 尸 and 丌 are added to form 𡱂, and 殳 is added to emphasize the meaning of “hitting the buttocks”.

母.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Differentiated form of {{zh-l|女*}} with the addition of distinguishing dots. In the early oracle bone texts both words {{och-l|女|woman}} and {{lang|zh|母}} were written as {{zh-l|女*}} ({{zh-ref|Yao, 1989}}, {{zh-ref|Liu, 2011}}, {{zh-ref|Huang, 2014}}). Part of this character appears in [[乳]].
母.originText: Differentiated form of 女* with the addition of distinguishing dots. In the early oracle bone texts both words 女 and 母 were written as 女* (,, ). Part of this character appears in 乳.

毎.originRaw: {{Han simp|每|f=母|t=毋}}, replacing the two dots with one stroke.
毎.originText: 每母毋, replacing the two dots with one stroke.

毒.originText: Chen, Jian (2020): of a woman wearing a feathered ornament on her head – original form of 纛. Later borrowed for 毒. If this is the correct interpretation, see also 每. Alternatively, Li Xueqin (2012) proposes it is a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 屮 (vegetation) + phonetic 毐, meaning "a type of poisonous plant."

比.originText: Chu Wan-li (1948): Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 匕 + phonetic 匕. ' interprets it as an ideogrammic compound meaning to juxtapose. Graphically similar but unrelated to 从, 尼, 化 and 北.

氏.originText: Various interpretations exist: a man bending over to sow the field (see also 氐 > 低 and 昏), the root of a tree (see also 柢), a man bowing over to the right, a stick with a decoration on top to represent a clan, a spoon (according to Guo Moruo and due to similarity to 匕), a mallet, a man holding an object, etc. On bronze inscriptions, a black dot was added inside the vertical stroke of the character; then, this point turned into a horizontal stroke 一 while the vertical stroke mutated into a curved trait.

民.originRaw: {{Han etyl}} {{liushu|p}} {{och-l|民|the people}}: the oracle bone script forms resemble an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement. The graph may be connected with eye impairment or unclear vision, compare {{och-l|泯}}, {{och-l|眠}}, and {{och-l|眄}}; the ''Shiji'' has {{zh-x|視眩眠而無見兮|the sight was dizzy and dim, and nothing could be seen}}, while the ''Hanshu'' writes {{l|zh|泯}} for {{l|zh|眠}}.
民.originText: 民: the oracle bone script forms resemble an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement. The graph may be connected with eye impairment or unclear vision, compare 泯, 眠, and 眄; the Shiji has 視眩眠而無見兮, while the Hanshu writes 泯 for 眠.

気.originRaw: {{Han simp|氣|f=米|t=㐅}} in the 1946 {{w|Tōyō kanji}} list.

水.originText: of water flowing; sometimes written as the variant 氺 (e.g., 泰, 录, and 黎). Next to a character, it is compressed and stylized into 氵 (which is unrelated to 冫). Compare 川 and its variant 巛. Compare also 永 and its cognate 𠂢. See also the bottom part of 原 in its original version (厡).

永.originText: of a long river with tributaries. Cognate with 𠂢, 派. Alternatively, of a person swimming in the water. Original form of 泳.

氾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 𢎘.

汁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|水|alt1=氵|十|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=water}}. It expresses the idea of a liquid.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
汁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 十. It expresses the idea of a liquid.

求.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of a centipede. Original form of {{och-l|蛷}}.
求.originText: of a centipede. Original form of 蛷.

汎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 凡.

汗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 干.

江.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 工.

池.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 也.

汰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 太.

決.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 夬.

汽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 气. Alternatively, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 水 (water) + semantic 气 (air) - steam. Quite possibly both of these origins could be true, out of convenience.

沃.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|水|alt1=氵|t1=water|夭|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to irrigate with water.
沃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 夭 – to irrigate with water.

沈.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

In the oracle bone script, it was an {{Han compound|水|羊|ls=ic|nocap=1|t1=water|t2=sheep}} — to submerge a sheep into the water (as a form of sacrifice to the river god). Other forms included {{zh-l|*牛|ox}} or {{zh-l|*玉|jade}} instead of {{zh-l|*羊}}.

Starting from the bronze inscriptions, it became a {{Han compound|水|冘|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=water|nocap=1}}.

This character was later borrowed to signify the surname, and the variant {{och-l|沉}} was adopted for the original meaning.
沈.originText: In the oracle bone script, it was an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 水 (water) + semantic 羊 (sheep) — to submerge a sheep into the water (as a form of sacrifice to the river god). Other forms included 牛 or 玉 instead of 羊. Starting from the bronze inscriptions, it became a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 冘. This character was later borrowed to signify the surname, and the variant 沉 was adopted for the original meaning.

河.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
[[File:Evolution of Oracle Bone script for He-V2.png|thumb|right|420px|Evolution of the character 河]]
* '''Oracle bone script''':
** ''Shi group (thick strokes) / 師肥筆'': {{Han compound|水|何|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=water}}.
** ''Variant'': {{Han compound|水|可|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} (phonetic drawn wavy like water; possibly original form of {{zh-l|歌}}, representing wavy sound).
** ''Corruption'': Confused with {{zh-l|何}} ({{zh-l|水}} corrupted to {{zh-l|人}}; {{zh-l|可}} corrupted to a shoulder burden, possibly original form of {{zh-l|柯}}).
** ''He group / 何組'': {{Han compound|水|何|ls=psc}} (more pictographic).
** ''Huang group / 黃組'': Compound of {{zh-l|欠}} / {{zh-l|旡}}, a shoulder burden, and {{zh-l|水}}.
* '''Western Zhou bronze''': Inherits Huang group structure; adds {{zh-l|口}}.
* Possibly related to {{och-l|何|tr=*gˤaj}} (to bear).

法.originText: Earliest attested on the late Shang bronze 作册般銅黿. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + semantic 廌 (a type of antelope or caprid) + phonetic 盍. Later, 廌 was omitted. In bronze inscriptions, mostly used for 廢: {{zh-x|率 亡 @灋{fèi} 矢。|not a single arrow was wasted.|CL-PC|ref=Late, 作册般銅黿 inscription|collapsed=y}} A notable exception is the early Western Zhou 大盂鼎, where 灋 is analyzed as 廢 in the sense of "great" (per 《釋詁》：「廢，大也。」): {{zh-x|…故 天 異 臨 子、@灋 保 先王、☐ 有 四方。|...therefore Heaven watched over you with extraordinary [favour], greatly safeguarded the former kings, and [they] possessed the four quarters.|CL-PC|ref=Early, inscription|collapsed=y}}

泰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally a {{Han compound|大|廾|水|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|c3=s|t2=two hands|t3=water}}. A more conservative variant is [[𡙌]]. The 大 and 廾 later fused into {{zh-l|*𡗗}}. The original meaning according to Shuowen Jiezi was "to slip", perhaps with a reference to seize something wet or to seize a liquid with bare hands. Then it became "too <much>", which was written either as [[太]] or 𡙌 > 泰 or as its variant [[冭]], perhaps due to the influence of its pronunciation and/or the top component of the character, which has a reference to a great quantity. As a result of the changed meaning, it may have been reinterpreted as an {{Han compound|大|廾|水|ls=ic|c1=s|c2=s|c3=s|t1=big; great|t2=two hands|t3=water}}.
泰.originText: Originally a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 大 + semantic 廾 (two hands) + semantic 水 (water). A more conservative variant is 𡙌. The 大 and 廾 later fused into 𡗗. The original meaning according to Shuowen Jiezi was "to slip", perhaps with a reference to seize something wet or to seize a liquid with bare hands. Then it became "too ", which was written either as 太 or 𡙌 > 泰 or as its variant 冭, perhaps due to the influence of its pronunciation and/or the top component of the character, which has a reference to a great quantity. As a result of the changed meaning, it may have been reinterpreted as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大 (big; great) + semantic 廾 (two hands) + semantic 水 (water).

漢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:京師畯尊-西周早期.jpg|thumb|Jingshijun Zun 京師畯尊, Early Western Zhou period]]
{{och-l|漢|tr=*n̥ˤar}}: semantic {{l|zh|水}} (“water”) + phonetic {{och-l|熯|tr=*n̥ˤanʔ}}. Earliest attested in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, e.g. the {{l|zh|京師畯尊}} (銘圖 11784), where it is used as a river name: {{lang|zh|王涉漢伐楚}}.

{{och-l|熯|tr=*n̥ˤanʔ}} (⿱𦰩火) depicts a person bound behind the back, mouth open toward the sky, over fire. It may be related to {{och-l|灘|tr=*n̥ˤar}}, {{och-l|歎|tr=*n̥ˤar}}, {{och-l|嘆|tr=*n̥ˤar}}, {{och-l|熯|tr=*n̥ˤanʔ}}, {{och-l|暵|tr=*n̥ˤanʔ}}, and {{och-l|難|tr=*n̥ˤar}}, in senses connected with drought, burning, or exclamation. From the middle Western Zhou onward, {{l|zh|𦰩}} may have been confused with {{l|zh|黃}}.

The usage for the Chinese ethnicity first appeared during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, claiming the Han dynasty as one of the golden ages of Chinese history.{{rfv-etym|en}} Before the Han dynasty, the Chinese referred their land as [[華夏]] ("Huaxia"), and themselves as [[諸華]] ("various Hua people") or [[諸夏]] ("various people/descendants of the Xias"). "Xia" ("Summer; great, splendid") also gave the name to the first semi-legendary Chinese dynasty, the Xia Dinasty ([[夏朝]]).
漢.originText: 漢: semantic 水 (“water”) + phonetic 熯. Earliest attested in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, e.g. the 京師畯尊 (銘圖 11784), where it is used as a river name: 王涉漢伐楚. 熯 (⿱𦰩火) depicts a person bound behind the back, mouth open toward the sky, over fire. It may be related to 灘, 歎, 嘆, 熯, 暵, and 難, in senses connected with drought, burning, or exclamation. From the middle Western Zhou onward, 𦰩 may have been confused with 黃. The usage for the Chinese ethnicity first appeared during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, claiming the Han dynasty as one of the golden ages of Chinese history. Before the Han dynasty, the Chinese referred their land as 華夏 ("Huaxia"), and themselves as 諸華 ("various Hua people") or 諸夏 ("various people/descendants of the Xias"). "Xia" ("Summer; great, splendid") also gave the name to the first semi-legendary Chinese dynasty, the Xia Dinasty (夏朝).

煮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 者 + semantic 火 (fire) – to cook over a fire.

熊.originText: According to ', Phono-semantic compound: semantic 能 (bear) + phonetic 炎. This character originally represented an onomatopoetic word (熊熊). Later its semantic component 能, the character for the Old Chinese word "bear", was borrowed for another word. This character thus began to represent the word "bear" instead.

熟.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|孰|t1=cooked; ripe|火|alt2=灬|t2=fire|ls=ic|ls2=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – cooked with fire.
熟.originText: Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 孰 (cooked; ripe) + semantic 火 (fire) – cooked with fire.

熱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 埶 + semantic 火 (fire).

燃.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|火|然|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=fire}} – burn with fire. Originally {{och-l|然}}, but because it was phonetically borrowed for abstract senses, {{m|zh|火}} was added for differentiation.
燃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 火 (fire) + phonetic 然 – burn with fire. Originally 然, but because it was phonetically borrowed for abstract senses, 火 was added for differentiation.

燥.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 火 (fire) + phonetic 喿.

爆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|火|暴|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. However, the phonetic component originally meant "violence", hence it could add part of the meaning. A conservative variant is [[𤒺]]; later it was stylized into 爆.
爆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 火 + phonetic 暴. However, the phonetic component originally meant "violence", hence it could add part of the meaning. A conservative variant is 𤒺; later it was stylized into 爆.

爪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a hand grabbing from above (in earlier forms from side); compare {{zh-l|*手}}, {{zh-l|*寸}}, {{zh-l|*九}}. Even if it can indicate a claw, actually the pictogram depicts a human hand.
爪.originText: a hand grabbing from above (in earlier forms from side); compare 手, 寸, 九. Even if it can indicate a claw, actually the pictogram depicts a human hand.

爵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} of an alcohol vessel in the shape of a sparrow. Many variants showed a hand ({{och-l|*又}}) holding it, now written as {{och-l|*寸}}. In the seal script form {{och-l|𢋺*}}, the topmost and middle sections of the vessel are combined, while the legs have corrupted into {{zh-l|*鬯|cup of wine}}. In the modern form, the top and middle sections of the vessel are separated into {{och-l|*爫}} and {{och-l|罒*}} respectively. The bottom left sub-component similar to {{och-l|*艮}} is a simplification of {{lang|zh|鬯}}.
爵.originText: of an alcohol vessel in the shape of a sparrow. Many variants showed a hand (又) holding it, now written as 寸. In the seal script form 𢋺*, the topmost and middle sections of the vessel are combined, while the legs have corrupted into 鬯. In the modern form, the top and middle sections of the vessel are separated into 爫 and 罒* respectively. The bottom left sub-component similar to 艮 is a simplification of 鬯.

父.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – A [[hand]] holding a [[stone]] blade, referring to a [[man]] working with a stone [[axe]].
父.originText: A hand holding a stone blade, referring to a man working with a stone axe.

爽.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大 + semantic 㸚 – bright.

片.originText: Mirror image of 爿, which is the pictogram of a bed. ': half of 木 to denote “to pare; to slice”; but this interpretation is not based on oracle bones and bronzes.

版.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 片 + phonetic 反.

牙.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The pictogram of a pair of elephant tusks. According to Xu Shen, this pictogram was used to indicate human molars but not front teeth/incisors (齒).
牙.originText: The pictogram of a pair of elephant tusks. According to Xu Shen, this pictogram was used to indicate human molars but not front teeth/incisors (齒).

牛.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} of a bull's head, with two horns and two ears. Perhaps unrelated to [[告]]; unrelated to [[先]].
牛.originText: of a bull's head, with two horns and two ears. Perhaps unrelated to 告; unrelated to 先.

牧.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|牛|攴|ls=ic|t1=cow|t2=a whip}} – to herd.
牧.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 牛 (cow) + semantic 攴 (a whip) – to herd.

物.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 牛 + phonetic 勿.

牲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 牛 (cow) + phonetic 生.

特.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 牛 (ox) + phonetic 寺 – large bull.

犬.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – the side view of a [[dog]].
犬.originText: the side view of a dog.

犯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 + phonetic 𢎘.

狂.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|犬|alt1=犭|㞷|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=dog}}. The latter is the ancient form of {{och-l|往|to go}}.
狂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 (dog) + phonetic 㞷. The latter is the ancient form of 往.

狙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 + phonetic 且.

狩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 (dog) + phonetic 守.

猛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 + phonetic 孟.

猫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 + phonetic 苗.

猶.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|犬|酋|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=dog}} – a kind of monkey.
猶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 (dog) + phonetic 酋 – a kind of monkey.

猿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 + phonetic 袁.

獄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|㹜|t1=two dogs|言|t2=words|ls=ic}} (㹜 = [[犭]] + [[犬]], two forms of “dog”). A place where dogs are barking (言) at each other, a jail with guard dogs.
獄.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 㹜 (two dogs) + semantic 言 (words) (㹜 = 犭 + 犬, two forms of “dog”). A place where dogs are barking (言) at each other, a jail with guard dogs.

獲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|犬|alt1=犭|蒦|c1=s|c2=p|t1=dog|t2=to catch|ls=psc|ls2=ic}} — according to Kōjien, to hunt and catch animals with a dog.<ref>{{R:Kojien}}</ref>
獲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 犬 (dog) + phonetic 蒦 (to catch) — according to Kōjien, to hunt and catch animals with a dog.

玄.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}}, two interwoven threads {{zh-l|*幺}} and a distinguishing mark {{zh-l|*亠}} on top. The whole character should represent a rope, as seen in [[率]] and [[弦]]. However, this rope is different from [[己]] and [[乃]].
玄.originText: , two interwoven threads 幺 and a distinguishing mark 亠 on top. The whole character should represent a rope, as seen in 率 and 弦. However, this rope is different from 己 and 乃.

率.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – according to Xu Shen, a net to capture birds. {{lang|zh|冫幺冫}}is the net, and the top and bottom is the stick. But in the original version, the horizontal stroke in the lower part is missing, therefore the whole character should represent a rope, 繂.
率.originText: according to Xu Shen, a net to capture birds. 冫幺冫is the net, and the top and bottom is the stick. But in the original version, the horizontal stroke in the lower part is missing, therefore the whole character should represent a rope, 繂.

玉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The character's shape was historically very similar to {{zh-l|*王}}; a dot was introduced to differentiate the two.

{{liushu|p}}: a picture of a [[w:Cong_(jade)|cong]] ({{zh-l|*琮}}), a sort of ritual jade totem.

It is also interpreted as three pieces of jade strung together on a string.

It is also used as a simplification of 或.
玉.originText: The character's shape was historically very similar to 王; a dot was introduced to differentiate the two. a picture of a cong (琮), a sort of ritual jade totem. It is also interpreted as three pieces of jade strung together on a string. It is also used as a simplification of 或.

王.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}

{{liushu|p}} of a ritual axe made perhaps of jade, symbols of the king's power. A ceremonial axe was kept near the throne, and was used for performing rituals in ancient China.
