The traditional interpretation (most likely a folk etymology given the original appearance of the character) is that the character metaphorically indicates the king or emperor according to the ancient Chinese thought: three horizontal strokes represent Heaven, Man and Earth, and the vertical stroke is the king or emperor, the one who connects them together. However, compare {{l|zh|天}} (a man with a horizontal stroke above his head to indicate the sky).

Unrelated to {{m|zh|玉|t=a string with three pieces of jade}} and {{m|zh|主|t=master}}; partly related to [[士]] (a war axe and, perhaps, sometimes a variant of 王), to [[戉]] (an axe drawn vertically), to the inner component of {{m|zh|匡|t=square‑shaped bamboo basket}}, and to the right component of [[往]] (< [[𢓸]]).
王.originText: of a ritual axe made perhaps of jade, symbols of the king's power. A ceremonial axe was kept near the throne, and was used for performing rituals in ancient China. The traditional interpretation (most likely a folk etymology given the original appearance of the character) is that the character metaphorically indicates the king or emperor according to the ancient Chinese thought: three horizontal strokes represent Heaven, Man and Earth, and the vertical stroke is the king or emperor, the one who connects them together. However, compare 天 (a man with a horizontal stroke above his head to indicate the sky). Unrelated to 玉 and 主; partly related to 士 (a war axe and, perhaps, sometimes a variant of 王), to 戉 (an axe drawn vertically), to the inner component of 匡, and to the right component of 往 (< 𢓸).

玩.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|玉|元|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|t1=jade}} – ancient toys made of jade.
玩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 元 – ancient toys made of jade.

珍.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|玉|㐱|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. Originally meant a rich, robust gemstone (玉), and then also developed the meaning of "rare".
珍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 + phonetic 㐱. Originally meant a rich, robust gemstone (玉), and then also developed the meaning of "rare".

珠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 朱.

班.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|珏|刀|t1=pieces of jade|t2=knife|ls=ic}} – to cut jade to pieces with knife. The pieces of jade appear as a more conservative version [[玨]]. The knife in the middle is well visibile in the conservative variant [[𤤻]]. Unrelated to [[师]].
班.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 珏 (pieces of jade) + semantic 刀 (knife) – to cut jade to pieces with knife. The pieces of jade appear as a more conservative version 玨. The knife in the middle is well visibile in the conservative variant 𤤻. Unrelated to 师.

現.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 見 — to appear.

球.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 求.

理.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 里. According to ', the character meant “to polish jade”. The current meaning “to order, tidy up” may be derived from it.

琴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 珡 + phonetic 今.

瑠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 留.

璃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 离.

璧.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辟|玉|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a type of jade.
璧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 辟 + semantic 玉 – a type of jade.

環.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 玉 (jade) + phonetic 睘.

璽.originText: From 壐. Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 爾 + semantic 玉 (jade).

瓦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – fired earthenware pottery, or a tile.
瓦.originText: fired earthenware pottery, or a tile.

瓶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 并 + semantic 瓦 (earthenware). According to the radical, it originally indicates an earthenware vessel, i.e., not a glass bottle. It had a long slender neck opening up to a narrow mouth. However, 瓶 was also part of ritual bronzes in ancient China, hence it was made of bronze when used during rituals. Today, it indicates bottles of any kind and dimension.

甘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}} – something sweet in an open mouth; the original drawing is [[𠁿]]. Original form of {{zh-l|*含}}. See also [[敢]], [[旨]], [[香]], and [[音]].
甘.originText: something sweet in an open mouth; the original drawing is 𠁿. Original form of 含. See also 敢, 旨, 香, and 音.

甚.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 甘 + semantic 匕.

生.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|屮|一|ls=ic|t1=bud|t2=ground}} – [[sprouting]] from the ground. A conservative version is [[𤯓]], which is unrelated to [[㞷]] ([[匩]] > [[匡]]) and [[𡴀]] > [[丰]].
生.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 屮 (bud) + semantic 一 (ground) – sprouting from the ground. A conservative version is 𤯓, which is unrelated to 㞷 (匩 > 匡) and 𡴀 > 丰.

用.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|psc}}: formed by adding a handle to {{och-l|同|tr=*lˤoŋ}}.
用.originText: formed by adding a handle to 同.

田.originText: pictographic representation of a field divided into four sections. See the original version of 甫 and 里. Sometimes it means mask. See 異 and 鬼. Unrelated to 思, 黄, 果, 由, 甲, and perhaps 番.

由.originText: pictogram of new shoots or leaves growing from 木; possibly the original graph of 㽕, with its upper part later extracted as 由. Alternatively interpreted as the upper part of the oracle-bone form of 柚 (“pomelo”), depicting the fruit itself.

甲.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: A [[pictogram]] of the protective [[hard]] [[shell]], [[carapace]], or [[scales]] of an animal, or a suit of [[armor]] made of connected plates.
甲.originText: A pictogram of the protective hard shell, carapace, or scales of an animal, or a suit of armor made of connected plates.

申.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}

{{liushu|p}} — a bolt of lightning. Original character of {{och-l|電|lightning}} and {{och-l|神|god; deity; spirit}}.
申.originText: a bolt of lightning. Original character of 電 and 神.

男.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|田|t1=field|力|t2=strength|ls=ic}} – man providing the strength for agricultural and/or other kinds of (physical) labour on a field.
男.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 田 (field) + semantic 力 (strength) – man providing the strength for agricultural and/or other kinds of (physical) labour on a field.

町.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + phonetic 丁

画.originText: Seemingly from 畵 with 𦘒 omitted.

界.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + phonetic 介.

畏.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|卜|鬼|c1=s|c2=p}}. In the bronze inscriptions, {{och-l|*心}} and {{och-l|*攴}} were sometimes added. During the Warring States period, the {{och-l|*卜}} corrupted into {{och-l|*止}}<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref>.

Hsiao-ting Li: In oracle bone script form, this character depicts a ghost {{och-l|*鬼}} standing and holding a stick.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' mistakes the small seal glyph as a ghost head ({{och-l|*甶}}) with part of a tiger, including its claw.
畏.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 卜 + phonetic 鬼. In the bronze inscriptions, 心 and 攴 were sometimes added. During the Warring States period, the 卜 corrupted into 止. Hsiao-ting Li: In oracle bone script form, this character depicts a ghost 鬼 standing and holding a stick. ' mistakes the small seal glyph as a ghost head (甶) with part of a tiger, including its claw.

畔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + phonetic 半.

留.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In bronze inscriptions, {{Han compound|卯|田|t2=field|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc|nocap=y}}. Later in small seal script, {{Han compound|丣|田|c1=p|c2=s|nocap=y}}.
留.originText: In bronze inscriptions, Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 卯 + semantic 田 (field). Later in small seal script, Compound: phonetic 丣 + semantic 田.

components.sense: rope tying the bag of feed

畜.originText: Pictogram: 玄 (rope tying the bag of feed) + 田 (bag of feed) – a bag of feed, hence livestock. Alternatively, Compound: 玄 (rope) + 田囿 (pen; fold; enclosure) – tying animals and raising them in the enclosure.

畝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Originally written as {{m|zh|畮|tr=-}}, a {{Han compound|ls=psc|c1=s|田|t1=field|c2=p|每|nocap=1}}. The phonetic component {{m|zh|每|tr=-}} was later replaced with {{m|zh|又|tr=-}}, now written as the new phonetic component {{och-l|久}}. The component {{m|zh|十|tr=-}} was added above {{m|zh|田|tr=-}} in the Warring States period and was later corrupted into {{m|zh|亠|tr=-}} in clerical script.
畝.originText: Originally written as 畮, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + phonetic 每. The phonetic component 每 was later replaced with 又, now written as the new phonetic component 久. The component 十 was added above 田 in the Warring States period and was later corrupted into 亠 in clerical script.

略.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|田|t1=field|各|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to walk around a field (to outline it).
略.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + phonetic 各 – to walk around a field (to outline it).

番.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|釆|田|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. Original meaning is unclear. 

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' instead interprets it as a pictogram of an animal's footprint; original form of {{och-l|蹯}}.

Tadashi Takada (高田忠周): a pictogram of some seeds on the palm of an open hand, which conveys the concept of "spreading"; original form of {{och-l|播}}.

Neither ''Shuowen'' nor Tadashi Takada interpret the bottom component as representing a field.
番.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 釆 + semantic 田. Original meaning is unclear. ' instead interprets it as a pictogram of an animal's footprint; original form of 蹯. Tadashi Takada (高田忠周): a pictogram of some seeds on the palm of an open hand, which conveys the concept of "spreading"; original form of 播. Neither Shuowen nor Tadashi Takada interpret the bottom component as representing a field.

異.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}} – a man with a mask ({{zh-l|*田}}) over his face. Possible interpretations:
* Strange, bizarre — "uncommon".
* Different face — "different".

Compare {{zh-l|*鬼|demon}}, where the {{lang|zh|田}} also derives from a face or a mask. Compare also [[禺]], in which the top component represents either a mask or a monkey's face.

Alternatively, may be a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a person carrying something on his head, the original form of {{zh-l|*戴|to carry on the head}}.

Modern form is graphically {{Han compound|田|共}}, though this is not the etymology.
異.originText: a man with a mask (田) over his face. Possible interpretations: Compare 鬼, where the 田 also derives from a face or a mask. Compare also 禺, in which the top component represents either a mask or a monkey's face. Alternatively, may be a of a person carrying something on his head, the original form of 戴. Modern form is graphically Compound: 田 + 共, though this is not the etymology.

畳.originRaw: Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|疊|f=畾|t=田|nocap=y}}. In current form {{Han compound|田|冝|lang=ja}}.
畳.originText: Japanese shinjitai 疊畾田. In current form Compound: 田 + 冝.

畿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 + phonetic 幾.

疑.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{multiple images
|width=75
|image1=疑-clerical-han.svg
|image2=疑-clerical-han-2.svg
|footer={{m-self|zh|疑}} from the {{w|Mawangdui}} manuscripts, Western Han.
}}

Originally an {{Han compound|[[大]] or [[文]]|夂|丨|t1=standing human figure|t2=tilted head with open mouth|t3=cane|ls=ic|nocap=1}} – a man with a cane looking around with his mouth wide open, not know where to go – to be confused; to doubt. Compare: {{m|zh|欠//|tr=-}} and {{m|zh|既//|tr=-}}, both showing the "open-mouth" component but on a seated figure. In the oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions, {{m|zh|彳//|tr=-}} or {{m|zh|辵//|tr=-}} = {{m|zh||彳//|tr=-}} + {{m|zh|止//|tr=-|gloss=foot; toes}} was often added to indicate travelling or movement.

Various components were added later, e.g. {{m|zh|牛//|tr=-}} in the bronze script of {{w|Western Zhou}}, {{m|zh|子//|tr=-}} in the {{w|Qin (state)|Qin}}-style scripts including the proto-[[clerical script]], and {{m|zh|乙//|tr=-}} in the early clerical script of Western Han. Meanwhile the main graphical element showing a standing figure eventually became {{m|zh|𠤕//|tr=-}} or sometimes {{m|zh|矣//|tr=-}} as in the {{w|Chu (state)|Chu}}-style script (shown in the table). The Chu also added a {{m|zh|心//|tr=-|gloss=heart}} component indicating "the mind".

The ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', in which headwords were written in the Qin-style [[seal script]], interpreted the character as “a child standing on an obstructed road to compare the paths”: {{Han compound|子|止|匕|矢|c1=s|c2=s|c3=s|c4=p|t1=child|t2=to be obstructed|t3=to compare|nocap=1}}. {{w|Duan Yucai}}'s commentary on ''Shuowen'' offered an alternative interpretation, pointing out that {{m|zh|矢//|tr=-}} was unlikely to have a phonetic component: {{Han compound|子|𠤕|止|c1=s|c2=s|c3=p|t1=child|t2=uncertain}}. However, it is unlikely that any of the currently extant components had once indicated the pronunciation. {{zh-ref|Zhengzhang (2003)}} conjectured that the {{m|zh|子//|tr=-}} was a corruption of {{och-l|牛}} that had been the phonetic component.

The current form is derived from the Qin–Han clerical scripts, where on the right-hand side the elements {{Han compound|子|止}} or {{Han compound|子|乙}} have recombined into {{Han compound|龴|疋}}.
疑.originText: {{multiple images |width=75 |image1=疑-clerical-han.svg |image2=疑-clerical-han-2.svg |footer=疑 from the manuscripts, Western Han. }} Originally an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大文 (standing human figure) + semantic 夂 (tilted head with open mouth) + semantic 丨 (cane) – a man with a cane looking around with his mouth wide open, not know where to go – to be confused; to doubt. Compare: 欠//, both showing the "open-mouth" component but on a seated figure. In the oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions, 彳// was often added to indicate travelling or movement. Various components were added later, e.g. 牛// in the -style scripts including the proto-clerical script, and 乙// in the early clerical script of Western Han. Meanwhile the main graphical element showing a standing figure eventually became 𠤕// as in the -style script (shown in the table). The Chu also added a 心// component indicating "the mind". The ', in which headwords were written in the Qin-style seal script, interpreted the character as “a child standing on an obstructed road to compare the paths”: Compound: semantic 子 (child) + semantic 止 (to be obstructed) + semantic 匕 (to compare) + phonetic 矢. 's commentary on Shuowen offered an alternative interpretation, pointing out that 矢// was unlikely to have a phonetic component: Compound: semantic 子 (child) + semantic 𠤕 (uncertain) + phonetic 止. However, it is unlikely that any of the currently extant components had once indicated the pronunciation. conjectured that the 子// was a corruption of 牛 that had been the phonetic component. The current form is derived from the Qin–Han clerical scripts, where on the right-hand side the elements Compound: 子 + 止 or Compound: 子 + 乙 have recombined into Compound: 龴 + 疋.

疫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (sickness) + phonetic 役.

疲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|疒|t1=sick|皮|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – sick and tired.
疲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (sick) + phonetic 皮 – sick and tired.

疾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 疒 (illness) + phonetic 疾 (fast). The two characters, originally representing different words, have merged into one character representing both senses. The oracle glyph of sc=Hani depicts an arrow flying towards a person - "fast". The "illness" sense preserves the original meaning of 疒. The 亠 component represents the person found in both pictograms.

病.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|疒|t1=sickness|丙|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – illness. Note that {{lang|zh|丙}} also means “fire”, hence connotations of “lying feverishly in bed”.
病.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (sickness) + phonetic 丙 – illness. Note that 丙 also means “fire”, hence connotations of “lying feverishly in bed”.

症.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (disease) + phonetic 正.

痕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 + phonetic 艮.

痘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|疒|豆|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=illness|t2=bean|ls2=ic}} - a disease causing bean-shaped skin eruption.
痘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (illness) + phonetic 豆 (bean) - a disease causing bean-shaped skin eruption.

痛.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|疒|甬|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=illness}}. The character conveys the meaning of "pain" or "to hurt."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
痛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (illness) + phonetic 甬. The character conveys the meaning of "pain" or "to hurt."

痢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|疒|t1=illness|利|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a kind of illness.
痢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (illness) + phonetic 利 – a kind of illness.

瘍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (illness) + phonetic 昜.

療.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 疒 (disease) + phonetic 尞.

癒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 病 + phonetic 愈.

癖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 病 + phonetic 辟.

components.sense: pictogrammic of raised object; stepping stone

登.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|癶|豆|ls=ic|t1=left and right feet|t2=pictogrammic of raised object; stepping stone}}. The two hands at the bottom disappeared, but they are retained in the conservative variant [[𤼷]]. <!--see https://xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw/yanbian?kaiOrder=2716-->
登.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 癶 (left and right feet) + semantic 豆 (pictogrammic of raised object; stepping stone). The two hands at the bottom disappeared, but they are retained in the conservative variant 𤼷.

白.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Two theories:
*{{liushu|p|nocap=1}} of an acorn. Compare {{zh-l|櫟}}.
*A human head. Compare {{zh-l|皃}} ({{zh-l|貌}}) and {{zh-l|黑}}.

Possibly part of a phonetic family contrasting stop initials (P/B) for exposure/brightness against nasal initials (M) for concealment/darkness; compare {{och-l|黑|tr=*m̥ˤək}} and {{och-l|白|tr=*bˤrak}}.
白.originText: Two theories: human head. Compare 皃 (貌) and 黑. Possibly part of a phonetic family contrasting stop initials (Pbrightness against nasal initials (M) for concealment/darkness; compare 黑 and 白.

百.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 一 + phonetic 白.

的.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 白 (white) + phonetic 勺. The original form was 旳 with the meaning of “bright”, hence the initial 日 semantic. See Etymology 1 below.

皆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Oracle bone script: {{Han compound|虍|几|口|c1=s|c2=p|c3=s|ls=psc}}.

Bronze script: {{Han compound|比|甘|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}.

The bottom component later corrupted into {{zh-l|*白}}, leading to the ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' reinterpretation of {{Han compound|ls=ic|比|白|nocap=y}}.
皆.originText: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虍 + phonetic 几 + semantic 口. Bronze script: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 比 + phonetic 甘. The bottom component later corrupted into 白, leading to the ' reinterpretation of Ideogrammic compound: semantic 比 + semantic 白.

皇.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Shang dynasty forms of the Chinese character 皇 (Huang).jpg|thumb|300px|{{w|Shang dynasty}} forms of {{m|zh|皇}}.]]

{{liushu|p}} — the oracle bone form depicts a single plume of a {{zh-l|*鳳凰}} (peacock); a phonetic {{och-l|王|tr=*waŋ}} was later added, giving {{Han compound|𤼽|王|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|nocap=y|tr=*wˤaŋ|tr2=*waŋ}}.

Belongs to a word family associated with radiant light, great size, vivid colour, and resonant sound.
皇.originText: the oracle bone form depicts a single plume of a 鳳凰 (peacock); a phonetic 王 was later added, giving Phono-semantic compound: semantic 𤼽 + phonetic 王. Belongs to a word family associated with radiant light, great size, vivid colour, and resonant sound.

皮.originText: a hand (又) stripping the fur from an animal pelt (similar to 革). The pelt moved to the top left and became abstracted. The character 叚 is similar, but actually it depicts two hands and some rocks 石 on oracle bones; a conservative variant is 𠭊.

皿.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} A pictograph of an empty container, such as a [[chalice]]. The handles are conjoined in the modern form.
皿.originText: A pictograph of an empty container, such as a chalice. The handles are conjoined in the modern form.

盆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 分 + semantic 皿.

益.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 水 (water) + semantic 皿 (vessel). Original form of 溢. Upper component resembles 氺 in a horizontal form. Compare 易.

盛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 成 + semantic 皿.

盟.originText: (𥁰): Phono-semantic compound: semantic 囧 + phonetic 皿. (𥂗): Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朙 + semantic 皿. 月 was added to 𥁰. 朙 is an ancient form of 明, and now this character (盟) is a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 明 + semantic 皿.

components.sense: a person with an emphasized eye

監.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 臥 (a person with an emphasized eye) + semantic 皿 (container): a person looking into a container . Original form of 鑑. The container later corrupted into 血; in the regular script, this additional stroke has migrated to below the 人 → sc=Hani/sc=Hani.

盤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 般 + semantic 皿. 凡 originally referred to this word, 殳 and 皿 were added later. The 凡 has also corrupted into 舟.

目.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}} – human eye, now rotated 90 degrees. Compare the Egyptian hieroglyph {{m|egy|𓁹}}.

See also [[直]], [[見]], [[頁]], [[夏]], [[面]], {{zh-l|*臣}} and the earlier versions of [[要]]. The eye is not rotated in the character {{zh-l|*𢛳}}, [[曼]], [[睪]], and [[眔]] (used in [[褱]]).

Sometimes it depicts a web ([[网]]) through its variant [[罒]], e.g., [[買]], [[罵]], [[罪]], [[詈]] (used in [[罰]]) and [[羅]] (> [[罗]]). Unrelated to [[鼎]], [[貝]], and [[真]].
目.originText: human eye, now rotated 90 degrees. Compare the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓁹. See also 直, 見, 頁, 夏, 面, 臣 and the earlier versions of 要. The eye is not rotated in the character 𢛳, 曼, 睪, and 眔 (used in 褱). Sometimes it depicts a web (网) through its variant 罒, e.g., 買, 罵, 罪, 詈 (used in 罰) and 羅 (> 罗). Unrelated to 鼎, 貝, and 真.

盲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亡 + semantic 目 (eye).

直.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Oracle bone script: {{Han compound|目|丨|ls=ic|t1=eye|t2=vertical stroke}} – vertical stroke above the eye; looking straight ahead. Then, a black dot was drawn inside the vertical stroke and this point later became a horizontal stroke (hence getting a shape similar to [[十]]).

The line on the side appears in bronze script and subsequently stretched under the 目 shape, while the traditional form appears in seal script.

A conservative version is used inside the character [[𢛳]] (> [[德]]), while the modern version is used inside its variant [[惪]]. Unrelated to [[具]] and [[真]].
直.originText: Oracle bone script: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + semantic 丨 (vertical stroke) – vertical stroke above the eye; looking straight ahead. Then, a black dot was drawn inside the vertical stroke and this point later became a horizontal stroke (hence getting a shape similar to 十). The line on the side appears in bronze script and subsequently stretched under the 目 shape, while the traditional form appears in seal script. A conservative version is used inside the character 𢛳 (> 德), while the modern version is used inside its variant 惪. Unrelated to 具 and 真.

相.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|木|目|ls=ic|t1=tree|t2=eye}} – an eye looking at a tree — original character for {{och-l|相|to observe|id=2}}. Later {{Han phonetically borrowed}} to represent {{och-l|相|mutually|id=1}}.
相.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 木 (tree) + semantic 目 (eye) – an eye looking at a tree — original character for 相. Later to represent 相.

盾.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} — a [[shield]] (in the [[oracle bone script]]). Note that under the 𠂆 is not 直 - one less stroke here. See also [[古]], perhaps a differentiation of 盾.
盾.originText: a shield (in the oracle bone script). Note that under the 𠂆 is not 直 - one less stroke here. See also 古, perhaps a differentiation of 盾.

省.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally {{lang|zh|[[眚]]}}. In {{w|oracle bone script}}, an {{Han compound|ls=psc|生|目|c1=p|t2=eye|nocap=yes}} – "to inspect". In {{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}, {{lang|zh|眚}} and {{lang|zh|省}} became separate characters. {{lang|zh|生}} corrupted over time into {{lang|zh|少}}.
省.originText: Originally 眚. In, an Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 生 + 目 (eye) – "to inspect". In, 眚 and 省 became separate characters. 生 corrupted over time into 少.

眉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|𠃜|目|tr2=eye|ls=p}}, hair above an eye. The component for hair became {{l|mul|𠃜}} during the development into the [[seal script|seal]] and [[clerical script]]s.
眉.originText: Pictogram: 𠃜 + 目, hair above an eye. The component for hair became 𠃜 during the development into the seal and clerical scripts.

看.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|手|目|t1=hand|t2=eye|ls=ic}} – to put a hand above eyes to gaze afar.
看.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 手 (hand) + semantic 目 (eye) – to put a hand above eyes to gaze afar.

真.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Bronze inscriptions: {{Han compound|貝|𠂈|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=cowrie; shell|tr2=*tˤiŋ|tr=*tiŋ}}. {{zh-l|𠂈}} is the original pictograph of {{och-l|顛|tr=*tˤiŋ}} (“to fall headlong”).<ref>謝明文：《釋“顛”字》</ref><ref>蔣玉斌：《釋殷墟花東卜辭的“顛”》</ref> From the late Western Zhou period, forms with {{zh-l|鼎}} instead of {{zh-l|*貝}} are also attested.

Oracle-bone forms are composed of {{zh-l|匕}} (“spoon”) and {{zh-l|鼎}}. These have been read by some scholars as {{zh-l|真}}<ref>陳年福：《實用甲骨文字典》，四川辭書出版社，2019年。</ref>, but some of them are better interpreted as {{zh-l|肆}}<ref>陳劍：《甲骨金文舊釋“䵼”之字及相關諸字新釋》，《出土文獻與古文字研究》第二輯，上海：復旦大學出版社，2008年，第13–47頁。</ref> or {{zh-l|煮}}<ref>王子楊：《甲骨文煮字補釋》，《出土文獻研究》第十八輯，上海：中西書局，2019年，第22–35頁。</ref>.

In Chu bamboo-slip script, forms with {{zh-l|鼎}} became dominant. The legs of {{zh-l|鼎}} gradually became graphically confused with {{zh-l|火}}, and the lower horizontal stroke, left-falling stroke, and dot in Qin-slip and later forms of {{zh-l|真}} may be reduced from {{zh-l|火}}. In the Zeng Hou Yi bamboo slips, an elaborated form with an added {{zh-l|丌}} at the bottom is also attested.
真.originText: Bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (cowrie; shell) + phonetic 𠂈. 𠂈 is the original pictograph of 顛 (“to fall headlong”). From the late Western Zhou period, forms with 鼎 instead of 貝 are also attested. Oracle-bone forms are composed of 匕 (“spoon”) and 鼎. These have been read by some scholars as 真, but some of them are better interpreted as 肆 or 煮. In Chu bamboo-slip script, forms with 鼎 became dominant. The legs of 鼎 gradually became graphically confused with 火, and the lower horizontal stroke, left-falling stroke, and dot in Qin-slip and later forms of 真 may be reduced from 火. In the Zeng Hou Yi bamboo slips, an elaborated form with an added 丌 at the bottom is also attested.

眠.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|目|t1=eye|民|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – close your eyes and go to sleep.
眠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 民 – close your eyes and go to sleep.

眺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 兆.

眼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 艮.

着.originRaw:
Corrupted variant of {{l|zh|著}} ({{l|zh|艹}} → {{l|zh|䒑}}; {{l|zh|日}} → {{l|zh|目}}). Recorded as an unorthodox form ({{zh-l|俗字*}}) in the {{w|Tang dynasty}} orthographic dictionary ''{{w|Ganlu Zishu}}'' {{lw|zh|pref=《|干祿字書|suf=》}}. <!-- Refer http://dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/variants/rbt/word_attribute.rbt?educode=A03506-015#18 -->

Later dictionaries such as the {{w|Ming dynasty}} {{lang|zh|《字學三正》}} and {{w|Qing dynasty}} ''{{w|Zhengzitong}}'' {{lw|zh|pref=《|正字通|suf=》}} recorded the glyph as {{lang|zh|⿱𦍌⿰丿目}}.
着.originText: Corrupted variant of 著 (艹 → 䒑; 日 → 目). Recorded as an unorthodox form (俗字*) in the orthographic dictionary ' 干祿字書. Later dictionaries such as the 《字學三正》 and ' 正字通 recorded the glyph as ⿱𦍌⿰丿目.

睡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 垂 – sleep.

督.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|叔|目|t2=eye|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – to look over, to oversee (with eyes).
督.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 叔 + semantic 目 (eye) – to look over, to oversee (with eyes).

睦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eyes) + phonetic 坴.

瞬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 舜.

瞭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 (eye) + phonetic 尞.

瞳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 + phonetic 童.

矛.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
The pictogram of a bamboo spear with a ring in the middle. Unrelated to [[予]].
矛.originText: The pictogram of a bamboo spear with a ring in the middle. Unrelated to 予.

矢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – an arrow. More recognizable in older forms. Compare [[畀]] and [[至]]. See also the bottom component of [[睪]] and the original versions of [[弗]] and [[𢦏]].
矢.originText: an arrow. More recognizable in older forms. Compare 畀 and 至. See also the bottom component of 睪 and the original versions of 弗 and 𢦏.

知.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally the same character as {{zh-l|*智}}, used interchangeably. In {{w|oracle bone inscriptions}}, {{Han compound|ls=ic|大|口|子|t1=adult|t2=mouth|t3=child|nocap=yes}} – to transmit knowledge. In the {{w|Warring States}} period, {{zh-l|*大}} corrupted into {{och-l|矢}} and became a sound component. In {{w|Han_dynasty#Western_Han|Western Han}} script the component {{zh-l|*子}} started being dropped, arriving at the modern form.
知.originText: Originally the same character as 智, used interchangeably. In, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大 (adult) + semantic 口 (mouth) + semantic 子 (child) – to transmit knowledge. In the period, 大 corrupted into 矢 and became a sound component. In script the component 子 started being dropped, arriving at the modern form.

短.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 矢 + phonetic 豆.

矯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|矢|喬|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=arrow}}: to straighten; to make as straight as an arrow shaft.
矯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 矢 (arrow) + phonetic 喬: to straighten; to make as straight as an arrow shaft.

石.originText: a stone beneath a cliff (厂). The cliff was subsequently distorted into 丆; compare 叚, 段 as well as 度, 席. Alternatively, a cave set into the side of a cliff or mountain.

砂.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|石|沙|alt2=少|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=stone}}. Originally, this character was a variant form of 沙, a {{liushu|p}} that represents the appearance of sand along a riverbank.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
砂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 沙. Originally, this character was a variant form of 沙, a that represents the appearance of sand along a riverbank.

研.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 + phonetic 幵.

砲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|石|包|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=stone}}. It originally referred to the catapult that launches stones far away, and by extension, it came to mean "cannon."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
砲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 包. It originally referred to the catapult that launches stones far away, and by extension, it came to mean "cannon."

破.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 + phonetic 皮.

硝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 肖

硫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 流.

硬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 + phonetic 更.

碁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 其.

碑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 卑.

確.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|石|隺|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=rock}} – rock-solid, as certain as a rock.
確.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (rock) + phonetic 隺 – rock-solid, as certain as a rock.

磁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (rock; stone) + phonetic 兹.

磨.originText: Originally written as 䃺. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (rock) + phonetic 靡.

礁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (rock) + phonetic 焦.

礎.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|石|t1=stone|楚|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a kind of stone, a [[plinth]].
礎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 石 (stone) + phonetic 楚 – a kind of stone, a plinth.

示.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p|5}} – an altar. The original form is similar to unrelated character {{lang|zh|[[丅]]}}, and additional strokes are added to prevent confusion with an ancient variant of [[下]] and the ancient version of [[主]]. See also [[帝]]. Unrelated to [[小]] and the bottom part of [[京]].
示.originText: an altar. The original form is similar to unrelated character 丅, and additional strokes are added to prevent confusion with an ancient variant of 下 and the ancient version of 主. See also 帝. Unrelated to 小 and the bottom part of 京.

礼.originRaw: Based on an ancient form of {{zh-l|禮*}} recorded in [[w:Shuowen Jiezi|''Shuowen'']] as [[File:禮-ancient.svg|text-bottom|30px]]. In [[regular script]], the earliest record can be traced back to the [[w:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]] orthographical dictionary ''[[w:Ganlu Zishu|Ganlu Zishu]]'' {{lw|zh|pref=《|干祿字書|suf=》}}.
礼.originText: Based on an ancient form of 禮* recorded in Shuowen as. In regular script, the earliest record can be traced back to the Tang dynasty orthographical dictionary Ganlu Zishu 干祿字書.

社.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 示 (god; deity) + semantic 土 (soil)

祈.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 (altar) + phonetic 斤.

祉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 (altar) + phonetic 止.

祖.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|示|且|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. Specialization of {{zh-l|*且}}. See there for more.
祖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 + phonetic 且. Specialization of 且. See there for more.

祝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|i}} – a man kneeling with open mouth ({{zh-l|*兄}}) next to an altar ({{zh-l|*示}}).
祝.originText: a man kneeling with open mouth (兄) next to an altar (示).

神.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 (god; deity) + phonetic 申 (lightning). Originally 申 in the oracle bone script and in some bronze inscriptions. The ancients feared the unpredictable lightning and considered it to be divine or of divine origin. 示 was added for specialization.

祥.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|示|c1=s|t1=altar|羊|c2=p}}. Originally just {{lang|zh|羊}}, {{lang|zh|示}} was added later to distinguish it.
祥.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 (altar) + phonetic 羊. Originally just 羊, 示 was added later to distinguish it.

票.originText: 𤐫火示𢍱覀. Ideogrammic compound: semantic 火 (fire) + semantic 𢍱 (to rise high), which represents two pairs of hands holding and rising an object, perhaps a bag or basket (西). The character originally represented the idea of sparks rising up. By extension, it was also used to mean "token" or "label." Then, the two pair of hands disappeared in the modern version. Unrelated to the original version of 要 and 栗.

祭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|肉|t1=meat|又|t2=hand|示|t3=altar, ceremony|ls=ic}} – the hand offers a piece of meat at the altar during a ceremony.

The {{och-l|*肉}} is turned on its side and appears as {{och-l|*𱼀}} in the regular script (compare {{zh-l|*將}}, {{zh-l|*然}}). The top right part is a form of {{lang|zh|又}}.

The top is not related to but may be corrupted to {{zh-l|*癶}} in calligraphy and handwriting; this form also appeared in the [[w:Second round of simplified Chinese characters|second-round simplified]] list.
祭.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + semantic 又 (hand) + semantic 示 (altar, ceremony) – the hand offers a piece of meat at the altar during a ceremony. The 肉 is turned on its side and appears as 𱼀 in the regular script (compare 將, 然). The top right part is a form of 又. The top is not related to but may be corrupted to 癶 in calligraphy and handwriting; this form also appeared in the second-round simplified list.

禁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 林 + semantic 示 (altar).

禅.originRaw:
{{Han simp|禪}}.
* {{Han simp|禪|f=示|t=礻|f2=單|t2=单}} (2 strokes on top of phonetic) in simplified Chinese.
* {{Han simp|禪|f=示|t=礻|f2=單|t2=単}} (3 strokes on top of phonetic) in Japanese shinjitai.

禍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 (sacrifice) + phonetic 咼.

福.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 示 + phonetic 畐.

秀.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

From an earlier form {{zh-l|𥝙}}, attested in the stone drum inscriptions ({{zh-l|石鼓文}}) from the [[w:Warring States period|Warring States period]].

According to {{zh-ref|Chi (2010)}}, the character is an {{Han compound|禾|引|t1=rice plant|t2=to [[draw out]] flowers|ls=ic|nocap=y}} — blooming of a rice plant. The [[w:Shuihudi Qin bamboo texts|Shuihudi Qin bamboo texts]] ({{lw|zh|睡虎地秦簡|睡簡}}) recorded this character as {{lang|zh|⿱禾引}}. The bottom component {{zh-l|弓*}} found in the stone drum inscriptions is likely a reduction of {{zh-l|引*}}.

Xu Kai ({{lw|zh|徐鍇}}), the author of {{lw|zh|pref=《|說文解字繫傳|suf=》}} (10th century AD) gave the following explanation: {{Han compound|禾|乃|ls=p|t1=plant}}, resembling a fruit/an ear hanging off a plant.

[[w:Shuowen Jiezi|''Shuowen'']] states that this character was [[w:naming taboo|tabooed]] at that time (2nd century AD) and so did not elaborate on its origin, due to it being the birth name of [[w:Emperor Guangwu of Han|Emperor Guangwu of Han]].
秀.originText: From an earlier form 𥝙, attested in the stone drum inscriptions (石鼓文) from the Warring States period. According to, the character is an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 禾 (rice plant) + semantic 引 (to draw out flowers) — blooming of a rice plant. The Shuihudi Qin bamboo texts (睡虎地秦簡睡簡) recorded this character as ⿱禾引. The bottom component 弓* found in the stone drum inscriptions is likely a reduction of 引*. Xu Kai (徐鍇), the author of 說文解字繫傳 (10th century AD) gave the following explanation: Pictogram: 禾 (plant) + 乃, resembling a fruit/an ear hanging off a plant. Shuowen states that this character was tabooed at that time (2nd century AD) and so did not elaborate on its origin, due to it being the birth name of Emperor Guangwu of Han.

私.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|禾|厶|c1=s|c2=p|t2=private|ls=psc}}. {{och-l|*厶}} originally referred to this word, {{och-l|*禾}} was added later.
私.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 厶 (private). 厶 originally referred to this word, 禾 was added later.

秋.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The oracle bone forms and bronze inscriptions show the {{liushu|p|nocap=1}} of a [[cricket]] or a [[locust]], sometimes with a fire {{zh-l|*火}} glyph underneath. In its later form, became a {{Han compound|禾|𤒅|c1=s|c2=p|t1=grain|ls=psc|abb2=y}}. Often thought of as an {{Han compound|禾|t1=grain|火|t2=fire|ls=ic}}; after harvesting the grain, the fields are burned to kill locusts and their eggs.
秋.originText: The oracle bone forms and bronze inscriptions show the of a cricket or a locust, sometimes with a fire 火 glyph underneath. In its later form, became a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + phonetic 𤒅. Often thought of as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + semantic 火 (fire); after harvesting the grain, the fields are burned to kill locusts and their eggs.

科.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 禾 + semantic 斗 (measuring tool).

秒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (cereal; grain) + phonetic 少.

秘.originText: In current form: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 必. Variant (俗字) of 祕 via 示 → 禾, hence there is a reference to secret rituals and the concept of arcane.

租.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 且. Land rent was paid in grain.

秩.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|禾|失|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=grain}}. It originally referred to rice plants being piled up in order, and by extension, conveys the idea of "sequence" or "order."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
秩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + phonetic 失. It originally referred to rice plants being piled up in order, and by extension, conveys the idea of "sequence" or "order."

称.originRaw:
{{Han simp|穪|f=爾|t=尔}}, where {{lang|zh|穪}} is corrupted from {{lang|zh|稱}}. It was found in various {{w|Movable type#Metal movable type in China|moveable type}} copies of {{w|Classic Chinese Novels|classical novels}}. First attested in 《{{lw|zh|宋元以來俗字譜}}》, a {{w|Variant Chinese character|variant forms}} dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms ({{l|zh|俗字}}) that have existed since the {{w|Song dynasty}}.

Adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956 {{w|Chinese Character Simplification Scheme}}. <!-- Refer https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/漢字簡化方案 -->
称.originText: 穪爾尔, where 穪 is corrupted from 稱. It was found in various copies of. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the. Adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956.

移.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 多.

程.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + phonetic 呈 – measurements.

税.originText: 稅兌兑. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 兑.

稚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (rice) + phonetic 屖. During the Han Dynasty, the 屖 component was commonly substituted with 隹.

種.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 重.

稲.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|稻}}. The component {{l|mul|旧}} is a variant of {{l|mul|臼}}.

The Japanese usage is of reform ({{w|shinjitai}}) nature.
稲.originText: Variant of 稻. The component 旧 is a variant of 臼. The Japanese usage is of reform nature.

稼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 家.

稽.originText: Originally 𩒨, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 旨 + semantic 頁 (person's head). In the modern form it is a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 𥝌 (bent, stunted tree) + semantic 尤 + phonetic 旨.

稿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 高.

穀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 (grain) + phonetic 𣪊.

穂.originRaw: Found in the historical {{w|Longkan Shoujian}} 《{{lw|zh|龍龕手鑑}}》 dictionary compiled in 997 AD.
穂.originText: Found in the historical 《龍龕手鑑》 dictionary compiled in 997 AD.

積.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 責.

穫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 禾 + phonetic 蒦.

穴.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}—possibly an entrance to a cave or a door flap. A conservative version is [[𠕉]]. See also [[奐]] and the top component of [[罙]].
穴.originText: —possibly an entrance to a cave or a door flap. A conservative version is 𠕉. See also 奐 and the top component of 罙.

究.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 (cave) + phonetic 九.

空.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 (cave, hole) + phonetic 工.

突.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Shuowen: {{Han compound|穴|犬|ls=ic|t1=cave; den|t2=dog}} – a dog suddenly coming out of a den.
突.originText: Shuowen: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 穴 (cave; den) + semantic 犬 (dog) – a dog suddenly coming out of a den.

窒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 + phonetic 至.

窟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 (hole; cave) + phonetic 屈.

窮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 (cave; nest; confinement) + phonetic 躬.

窯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|穴|羔|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=cave; hole}}. It represents a hole used for firing pottery, which is a pottery kiln.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
窯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 穴 (cave; hole) + phonetic 羔. It represents a hole used for firing pottery, which is a pottery kiln.

立.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a person standing on the ground; compare {{l|zh|大}} and {{l|zh|文}}.
立.originText: a person standing on the ground; compare 大 and 文.

竜.originRaw: Recorded as an ancient form of {{zh-l|龍*}} in the [[w:Kangxi dictionary|Kangxi dictionary]] in 1716 AD. Earlier dictionaries such as ''[[w:Longkan Shoujian|Longkan Shoujian]]'' {{lw|zh|pref=《|龍龕手鑑|suf=》}} in 997 AD and ''[[w:Jiyun|Jiyun]]'' {{lw|zh|pref=《|集韻|suf=》}} in 1037 AD recorded the glyph as {{zh-l|𥪖*}}.
竜.originText: Recorded as an ancient form of 龍* in the Kangxi dictionary in 1716 AD. Earlier dictionaries such as Longkan Shoujian 龍龕手鑑 in 997 AD and Jiyun 集韻 in 1037 AD recorded the glyph as 𥪖*.

章.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}: A chisel {{zh-l|*辛}} piercing a piece of untreated jade in the middle of the character (now {{zh-l|*日}}). Originally meaning "to treat jade", likely the original character of {{zh-l|*璋}} or {{zh-l|*彰}}.
章.originText: A chisel 辛 piercing a piece of untreated jade in the middle of the character (now 日). Originally meaning "to treat jade", likely the original character of 璋 or 彰.

components.sense: kneeling person with a huge eye

童.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In oracle bone inscriptions, {{Han compound|ls=ic|䇂|見|t1=chisel|t2=kneeling person with a huge eye|nocap=y}}. It depicts a person getting their eye ([[目]]) gouged out, a common punishment for slaves in ancient China. Compare {{zh-l|*民}}, {{zh-l|*臧}}. 

In bronze inscriptions, the phonetic component {{och-l|東}} was added, making the character {{liushu|psc|adj=yse|nocap=yes}}. 

In the modern form {{zh-l|*䇂}} has corrupted into {{zh-l|*立}}. The bottom {{zh-l|*里}} derives from {{zh-l|*東}} combining with {{zh-l|*土}}, similar to {{zh-l|*重}}.
童.originText: In oracle bone inscriptions, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 䇂 (chisel) + semantic 見 (kneeling person with a huge eye). It depicts a person getting their eye (目) gouged out, a common punishment for slaves in ancient China. Compare 民, 臧. In bronze inscriptions, the phonetic component 東 was added, making the character. In the modern form 䇂 has corrupted into 立. The bottom 里 derives from 東 combining with 土, similar to 重.

端.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 立 + phonetic 耑.

競.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
According to ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', an {{Han compound|誩|儿|儿|t3=man|t2=man|t1=argument|ls=ic}} – two individuals debating vigorously. Also possibly a {{Han compound|誩|儿|儿|c1=p|c2=s|c3=s|t2=man|t3=man|ls=psc}}. Compare  [[友]].
競.originText: According to ', an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 誩 (argument) + semantic 儿 (man) + semantic 儿 (man) – two individuals debating vigorously. Also possibly a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 誩 + semantic 儿 (man) + semantic 儿 (man). Compare 友.

竹.originText: two bamboo stalks, with leaves. Earlier forms resembled 个 + 个, current form resembles rather ケ + ケ, or 亇 + 亇. See also the original version of 散.

笑.originText: Originally Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 艸 (grass) + semantic 犬 (dog). Later, Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 + phonetic 夭.

笛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 由.

符.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 付.

第.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 弟. 竹 here refers to the bamboo strips used for writing (e.g. accounting, classification) in ancient times. See also 等. Alternatively, may have originally been written 弟.

筆.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|竹|聿|t1=bamboo|t2=writing brush|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. {{och-l|*聿}} originally referred to this word; {{och-l|*竹}} was added later to differentiate.
筆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 聿 (writing brush). 聿 originally referred to this word; 竹 was added later to differentiate.

等.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 寺. 竹 here refers to the bamboo strips used for writing (e.g. grading, classification) in ancient times. 寺 was originally used phonetically; the character was subsequently borrowed for another word with the same meaning, but with no phonetic resemblance to 寺.

筋.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|竹|𠛧|ls=ic|t1=bamboo|t2=peel}} – sinew (bamboo is sinewy when peeled). The component {{zh-l|*力}} is a corruption of {{zh-l|*刀}} ({{zh-l|*刂}}).
筋.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + semantic 𠛧 (peel) – sinew (bamboo is sinewy when peeled). The component 力 is a corruption of 刀 (刂).

筒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 同

答.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|竹|合|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bamboo}}. Originally, it was a variant of [[荅]], where the semantic component [[艸]] (grass) was later mistakenly replaced by [[竹]] (bamboo). It expresses the meaning of "to respond."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
答.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 合. Originally, it was a variant of 荅, where the semantic component 艸 (grass) was later mistakenly replaced by 竹 (bamboo). It expresses the meaning of "to respond."

策.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 朿. ;"to whip" Originally 敇.

箇.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|竹|固|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bamboo|ls=psc}} — a stalk of bamboo.
箇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 固 — a stalk of bamboo.

箋.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|竹|戔|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bamboo}}. It expresses the idea of a small bamboo strip, and by extension, signifies a “tag” or “label.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
箋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 戔. It expresses the idea of a small bamboo strip, and by extension, signifies a “tag” or “label.”

算.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In current form, {{Han compound|竹|目|廾|t1=bamboo}}.

The {{lang|zh|目}} portion may have originally represented [[w:Counting_rods|counting rods]] (or possibly an [[abacus]], although the character is believed to predate its invention). Such rods were typically made from bamboo. Perhaps related to the top component of [[學]], hence to [[爻]].

Similar but unrelated to [[具]].
算.originText: In current form, Compound: 竹 (bamboo) + 目 + 廾. The 目 portion may have originally represented counting rods (or possibly an abacus, although the character is believed to predate its invention). Such rods were typically made from bamboo. Perhaps related to the top component of 學, hence to 爻. Similar but unrelated to 具.

管.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 官.

箱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 相 – a bamboo box.

箸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 者.

節.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|竹|alt1=⺮|即|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=bamboo}}. It represents the "node" of bamboo, and by extension, signifies a segment or boundary.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
節.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 即. It represents the "node" of bamboo, and by extension, signifies a segment or boundary.

範.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (carriage) + phonetic 笵.

築.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 筑 + semantic 木 (wood).

篤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 竹 + semantic 馬 (horse).

簡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 + phonetic 閒

簿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 溥.

籍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 (bamboo) + phonetic 耤 – the (bamboo) census books.

籠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 竹 + phonetic 龍.

米.originText: rice kernels without husk. The character 粟, by contrast, refers to rice kernels with husk. According to Li Xiaoding (李孝定), the horizontal stroke is a bamboo sieve (籭 or 篩子). See also the bottom component of 暴 in its original form. Unrelated to 木, 禾, and 来.

粉.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|米|分|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|t1=rice}} – [[face powder]] made of [[rice]].
粉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 分 – face powder made of rice.

粒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 立.

粗.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 且.

粘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|米|t1=rice|占|c2=p|c1=s|ls=psc}} – glutinous, sticky rice.
粘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 占 – glutinous, sticky rice.

粧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 庄. It conveys the meaning of "face powder" and, by extension, is used to mean "to adorn oneself." Originally, it was a popular variant of the character 妝.

精.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 青 – polished rice.

糖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 (rice) + phonetic 唐.

糧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 米 + phonetic 量.

系.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|手|糸|abb1=1|ls=ic}}. Also used as simplified forms:
* {{Han simp|繫|f=𣪠|t=丿}} (through an intermediate form 毄).
* {{Han simp|係|f=人|t= }}.
系.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 手 + semantic 糸. Also used as simplified forms:

糾.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|丩|c1=s|c2=p|t1=silk|t2=to entangle|alt1=糹|ls=psc}}. {{och-l|*丩}} originally referred to this word, {{och-l|*糸}} was added later.
糾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 丩 (to entangle). 丩 originally referred to this word, 糸 was added later.

紀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 己.

約.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (rope) + phonetic 勺.

紅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 工.

紋.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|t1=thread|文|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a line of thread. Specialised character from {{och-l|文}}.
紋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 文 – a line of thread. Specialised character from 文.

納.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk, thin thread) + phonetic 内.

純.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|糸|屯|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=thread}}. It conveys the meaning of "without any impurities," and also "exclusively."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
純.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 屯. It conveys the meaning of "without any impurities," and also "exclusively."

紙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 氏.

級.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|alt1=糹|t1=thread|及|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. According to Shuowen Jiezi, the original meaning was referred to a "sequence" related to silk (絲的次第), however Xu Shen didn't specify the exact kind of sequence he was talking about.
級.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 及. According to Shuowen Jiezi, the original meaning was referred to a "sequence" related to silk (絲的次第), however Xu Shen didn't specify the exact kind of sequence he was talking about.

紛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 分.

素.originText: hands 廾 braiding thread 糸. In modern form, top component looks like 生 without the diagonal stroke – compare 責, 青.

紡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 方.

components.sense: strip fibres off a hemp stalk

索.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + semantic 𣎳 (strip fibres off a hemp stalk). Threads (rope) being removed from a fabric. 糸 visually represents the middle interior of the small seal script form, whereas 𣎳 is the three-pointed top part and the left and right lines.

紫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 此 + semantic 糸.

累.originText: 纍畾田. Folk etymology considers this character as an ideographic compound representing the tiredness after work. In ancient China, men were working in the field (田) while women sewed (糸).

細.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|囟|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. The right component is etymologically unrelated to {{zh-l|*田}} in which it was corrupted to after the Han dynasty.
細.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 囟. The right component is etymologically unrelated to 田 in which it was corrupted to after the Han dynasty.

紳.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|糸|申|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=thread}}. It represents a large sash used for formal dress, called a "large obi."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
紳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 申. It represents a large sash used for formal dress, called a "large obi."

紹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 召.

紺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk; thread) + phonetic 甘.

終.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally a {{liushu|p|nocap=1}}, [[夂]] (definition 2) – the knot at the end of a cord. Later reformulated as a {{Han compound|糸|alt1=糹|冬|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|nocap=1}}.
終.originText: Originally a, 夂 (definition 2) – the knot at the end of a cord. Later reformulated as a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 冬.

組.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 且.

経.originRaw: {{Han simp|經|f=巠|t=圣}}. Also a Japanese shinjitai. Current form {{Han compound|糸|圣}}, but not etymologically related to [[圣]].
経.originText: 經巠圣. Also a Japanese shinjitai. Current form Compound: 糸 + 圣, but not etymologically related to 圣.

結.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 吉.

絞.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|糸|交|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=thread}}.<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref> ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
絞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 交. ' interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.

絡.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|糸|t1=thread|各|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – wrapped in thread, a web of thread.
絡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 各 – wrapped in thread, a web of thread.

給.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
According to Shuowen Jiezi, {{Han compound|糸|合|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – "rich, abundant", perhaps with a reference to precious silk; today it also means "to give". The phonetic component means "to join, to unite", however it is likely unrelated to the original meaning.
給.originText: According to Shuowen Jiezi, Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 合 – "rich, abundant", perhaps with a reference to precious silk; today it also means "to give". The phonetic component means "to join, to unite", however it is likely unrelated to the original meaning.

統.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 充.

絹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|糸|肙|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=thread}}. The character conveys the meaning of "silk."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
絹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 肙. The character conveys the meaning of "silk."

維.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|t1=thread|唯|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|abb2=y}}.

The original pronunciation of {{och-l|隹|tr=*ɢʷi}} was lost after the classical period, but can still be seen in other characters of the phonetic series:
* {{och-l|惟|to think}},
* {{och-l|唯|only}},
* {{och-l|雖|although}},
* {{och-l|帷|curtain, screen}} and
* {{och-l|淮|Huai River}}.
維.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 唯. The original pronunciation of 隹 was lost after the classical period, but can still be seen in other characters of the phonetic series:

綱.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (rope) + phonetic 岡.

網.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (rope) + phonetic 罔.

綻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 定.

綿.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
A compound of {{l|mul|糸||silk thread}} + {{l|mul|帛||silk textile}} reorganized from {{l|mul|緜}} ({{l|mul|系}} became {{l|mul|糸}} and moved to the left).
綿.originText: A compound of 糸 + 帛 reorganized from 緜 (系 became 糸 and moved to the left).

緊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臤 + semantic 糸.

総.originRaw: Variant of {{l|mul|總}}. {{Han simp|總|f=悤|t=忩}}. It can be analysed as inheriting the variant {{l|mul|忩}} of component {{l|mul|悤}}.
総.originText: Variant of 總. 總悤忩. It can be analysed as inheriting the variant 忩 of component 悤.

緒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 者.

線.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 泉.

締.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 帝.

編.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|t1=thread|扁|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to knit together a book (with thread).
編.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 扁 – to knit together a book (with thread).

緩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 爰.

緯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 韋.

練.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 柬.

緻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 𦤶.

縛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (rope) + phonetic 尃.

縫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 + phonetic 逢.

縮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (string, thread) + phonetic 宿.

績.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|t1=thread|責|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to spin thread.
績.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 責 – to spin thread.

繁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敏 + semantic 糸 (silk)

織.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + phonetic 戠.

繕.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|糸|善|t1=thread; textile|t2=good|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. Also {{liushu|ic}}: to repair; to make good.
繕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread; textile) + phonetic 善 (good). Also : to repair; to make good.

繭.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 糸 (silk) + semantic 虫 (insect) + semantic 黹 (needlework).

繰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|糸|喿|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=thread}}. It refers to dark blue silk. By extension, it is used to mean "to wind" or "to twist" thread.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
繰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 糸 (thread) + phonetic 喿. It refers to dark blue silk. By extension, it is used to mean "to wind" or "to twist" thread.

缶.originText: an earthenware jar with a lid. See also the bottom part of the original versions of 由. Unrelated to the top component of 鬱, in which it represents a stylized man (大).

罪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|网|非|ls=ic|alt1=罒|t1=net|t2=mistake}}. The original version is [[𦋛]] and its original meaning was a net for fishing, then used instead of [[辠]] due to the similarity of the latter character to [[皇]], which represents the Emperor.
罪.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 网 (net) + semantic 非 (mistake). The original version is 𦋛 and its original meaning was a net for fishing, then used instead of 辠 due to the similarity of the latter character to 皇, which represents the Emperor.

置.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 网 + phonetic 直.

罰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|詈|刀|c1=s|c2=s|t1=abuse verbally|t2=knife|ls=ic}}. To abuse verbally and to use a knife improperly represent a crime. The original version is [[𠟑]], in which the left component is [[𧧧]].
罰.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 詈 (abuse verbally) + semantic 刀 (knife). To abuse verbally and to use a knife improperly represent a crime. The original version is 𠟑, in which the left component is 𧧧.

署.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 网 (net) + phonetic 者.

罵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|网|馬|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. The original version is [[𦋻]]. See also [[詈]] (< [[𧧧]]).
罵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 网 + phonetic 馬. The original version is 𦋻. See also 詈 (< 𧧧).

罷.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|网|能|t1=|t2=|ls=ic}} - catch a bear with a web. According to Shuowen Jiezi, it originally means "catch criminals"; according to Zhang Shunhui (張舜徽), it means "tired" with a reference to a bear being caught while tired after a chase. The web at the top of the character is well visible in its original version [[𦋼]].
罷.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 网 + semantic 能 - catch a bear with a web. According to Shuowen Jiezi, it originally means "catch criminals"; according to Zhang Shunhui (張舜徽), it means "tired" with a reference to a bear being caught while tired after a chase. The web at the top of the character is well visible in its original version 𦋼.

羅.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|网|維|t1=net|t2=bird (tied with string)|ls=ic}} — net for catching birds. The original version is [[𦌴]].
羅.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 网 (net) + semantic 維 (bird (tied with string)) — net for catching birds. The original version is 𦌴.

羊.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – picture of a [[ram]]'s head. See also the original version of [[沈]].
羊.originText: picture of a ram's head. See also the original version of 沈.

美.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a person ({{zh-l|*大}}) wearing a headdress (now written {{zh-l|*羊}}) of feathers or ram's horn.

The modern form could be considered an {{Han compound|羊|t1=ram or feathers|大|t2=person|ls=ic|nocap=y}}.

See also {{zh-l|*敖}}, {{zh-l|*冒}}, and {{zh-l|*免}}.
美.originText: a person (大) wearing a headdress (now written 羊) of feathers or ram's horn. The modern form could be considered an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 羊 (ram or feathers) + semantic 大 (person). See also 敖, 冒, and 免.

羞.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|羊|丑|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}; phonetic previously [[又]]. Not related to [[差]] or [[着]].
羞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 羊 + phonetic 丑; phonetic previously 又. Not related to 差 or 着.

群.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|君|羊|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a herd of sheep; a group.
群.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 君 + semantic 羊 – a herd of sheep; a group.

羨.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 羊 (sheep) + semantic 㳄 (saliva) – to envy. 羊 may be interpreted as a beautiful sheep or good mutton (cf. 美 “beautiful” and 善 “good”). The Kangxi Dictionary, following 《佩觿》, enters the word in etymology 2 as 羡, separating it from 羨 (etymology 1). This is also followed by dictionaries such as ' and ', but ' disagrees with this treatment. (' regards 羡 as the main form of all pronunciations.) According to 《說文解字羣經正字》: {{zh-x|羨，貪欲 也，今 經典 往往 作 羡。@^郭.^忠恕《@^佩觿》分 羨、羡 爲 二 字。羡，以 脂 翻，江夏 地名；羨，似 面 翻，慕 也。非 也，字書 無 从 次 之 字，惟 一 字 而 數 音 耳。|羨, meaning "to covet", is now frequently written as 羡 in the classics. 's Peixi distinguishes 羨 and 羡 as separate characters. 羡, fanqie 以脂, name of a place in Jiangxia. 羨, fanqie 似面, to desire. This is not the case. There's no such character with the 次 element in character dictionaries. There is only one character but several pronunciations.|CL|tr=羨 (Xiàn), tānyù yě, jīn jīngdiǎn wǎngwǎng zuò 羡. Guō Zhōngshù “Pèixī” fēn 羨 (xiàn), 羡 (yí) wéi èr zì. Yí, yǐ zhī fān, Jiāngxià dìmíng; xiàn, sì miàn fān, mù yě. Fēi yě, zìshū wú cóng 次 (cì) zhī zì, wéi yī zì ér shù yīn ěr.|ref=《說文解字羣經正字》, quoted from '|collapsed=y}}

義.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|我|羊|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. The component {{lang|zh|羊}} here signifies "good; beautiful; auspicious" and not "sheep". See {{lang|zh|[[祥]]}}, {{lang|zh|[[善]]}} and {{lang|zh|[[幸]]}}.
義.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 我 + semantic 羊. The component 羊 here signifies "good; beautiful; auspicious" and not "sheep". See 祥, 善 and 幸.

翁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|公|羽|c1=p|c2=s|t2=wings}}. Originally representing the meaning “feathers”, it was later loaned to mean “old man” and similar senses, by association with the semantic {{zh-m|公|tr=-}}.
翁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 公 + semantic 羽 (wings). Originally representing the meaning “feathers”, it was later loaned to mean “old man” and similar senses, by association with the semantic 公.

翌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 羽 + semantic 昱

習.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|羽|t1=wings|日|t2=sun|ls=ic}} – to learn to fly, to practice flying.

In the current form, {{zh-l|日|sun}} has changed to {{zh-l|白|white}}, so the present form is {{Han compound|羽|t1=wings|白|t2=white}}.

Alternatively, the original form may have been a {{Han compound|彗|日|c1=p|c2=s|t2=sun|ls=psc|nocap=y}}.
習.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 羽 (wings) + semantic 日 (sun) – to learn to fly, to practice flying. In the current form, 日 has changed to 白, so the present form is Compound: 羽 (wings) + 白 (white). Alternatively, the original form may have been a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 彗 + semantic 日 (sun).

翻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 番 + semantic 羽 (wings) – to flutter.

翼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 羽 + phonetic 異.

老.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (man) + semantic 毛 (hair) + semantic 匕 (cane) – a man with long hair (an old man), leaning on a cane. Compare top component to 孝. Cognate to 考; the most commonly cited example of 轉注.

components.sense: an old man with long hair, bent over

考.originText: Variant of 老 – Ideogrammic compound: semantic 耂 (an old man with long hair, bent over) + semantic 丂 (a walking cane) originally drawn as 匕 – an old man, leaning on a cane. Compare top component to 孝. Structurally related to 老; the most commonly cited example of 轉注.

者.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} – a sugarcane with full stems, with some points around (either leaves or drops of sweet liquid) and an open and smiling mouth at the bottom. This is the original character for either {{och-l|蔗|sugarcane}} or {{och-l|煮|to boil}}. Phonetically loaned for abstract meanings.

Top component {{zh-l|*耂}} is unrelated to {{zh-l|*老}}, {{zh-l|*考}}, and {{zh-l|*孝}}.

The variant form with an additional {{zh-l|*丶}} stroke below {{zh-l|*耂}} is influenced by ''{{w|Shuowen}}'', which considered {{zh-l|*白}} as the bottom component of {{zh-l|*者}}.
[[File:者-俗書刊誤.png|thumb|{{lang|zh|《俗書刊誤》}} considered {{lang|zh|者}} (without {{zh-l|*丶}}) as a variant form, and {{lang|zh|者}} (with {{zh-l|*丶}}) as the orthodox form.]]
者.originText: a sugarcane with full stems, with some points around (either leaves or drops of sweet liquid) and an open and smiling mouth at the bottom. This is the original character for either 蔗 or 煮. Phonetically loaned for abstract meanings. Top component 耂 is unrelated to 老, 考, and 孝. The variant form with an additional 丶 stroke below 耂 is influenced by ', which considered 白 as the bottom component of 者.

耐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 而 + semantic 寸.

耕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 耒 (tilling tool) + phonetic 井.

聖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 耳 (ear) + phonetic 呈. Compare 聽.

聞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 門 + semantic 耳 (ear). Compare 問.

職.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 耳 (ear) + phonetic 戠.

肉.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – ribs of an animal’s torso or simply a physical representation of a slice of meat. Stylized into [[月]] when next to a phonetic component and [[𱼀]] and/or [[夕]] inside some characters.
肉.originText: ribs of an animal’s torso or simply a physical representation of a slice of meat. Stylized into 月 when next to a phonetic component and 𱼀 and/or 夕 inside some characters.

肌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 几.

肖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 小 + semantic 月 (moon). The character may have been the original form of 宵. ' has erroneously analyzed the character as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 小 + semantic 肉 (meat).

肘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|肉|寸|c1=s|c2=p|tr2={{och-retrieve-pron}}}}. Originally written as {{och-l|*寸}}, an ideogram of a hand ({{zh-l|*又}}) with a stroke outlining the elbow. This character was distinct from {{zh-l|*寸}}; however, their shapes were too similar, so a {{och-l|*肉}} was added to distinguish it.
肘.originText: {{Han compound|ls=psc|肉|寸|c1=s|c2=p|tr2=}}. Originally written as 寸, an ideogram of a hand (又) with a stroke outlining the elbow. This character was distinct from 寸; however, their shapes were too similar, so a 肉 was added to distinguish it.

肝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh; body part) + phonetic 干.

股.originText: Originally written 夃, according to 趙平安. Later the 夃 component came to be written 殳, and a 肉 component was added, making the modern form an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 肉 (body) + phonetic 夃 (thigh). Shuowen incorrectly considered it Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (body) + phonetic 殳 (action) – the hips as an active part of the body.

肢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh) + phonetic 支.

肥.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + semantic 卪 (person kneeling). posits that its actually a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 妃.

肩.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}}. The component [[戶]] (representing the shape of a shoulder) is combined with [[月]] (the radical of [[肉]], meaning "flesh" or "meat") to convey the meaning of "shoulder."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
肩.originText: The component 戶 (representing the shape of a shoulder) is combined with 月 (the radical of 肉, meaning "flesh" or "meat") to convey the meaning of "shoulder."

肪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat/flesh) + phonetic 方.

肯.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|冎|肉|t1=bone|t2=meat|ls=ic|abb1=y}} – meat attached to the bone. Originally {{zh-m|*肎}} or {{zh-m|*𦘫}}; the top component was later corrupted to {{zh-m|*止}}.
肯.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 冎 (bone) + semantic 肉 (meat) – meat attached to the bone. Originally 肎 or 𦘫; the top component was later corrupted to 止.

育.originText: Evolved geometrically from 胄 in Han dynasty era . Before that, Pronunciation 1 was written as 毓; see there for more.

肺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat; flesh) + phonetic 巿.

胃.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}}: a stomach with food inside, originally appearing as {{zh-l|*𱕻}}. A semantic {{och-l|*肉}} was added later to differentiate.

The bronze script form merely consisted of two concentric circles. An inner portion of the character was later added, namely a mutated form of the [[seal script]] character of {{zh-l|*米}} ("rice"), representing grains within the stomach (see also [[鬯]]).

The character looked like {{och-l|*𦞅}} in the small seal script. In the [[clerical script]] form, the upper component was simplified to the unrelated {{och-l|*田}} as an instance of ''{{w|libian}}'' simplification.

The ancient form of the character can be seen within the lower component of {{och-l|*𦳊}}.
胃.originText: a stomach with food inside, originally appearing as 𱕻. A semantic 肉 was added later to differentiate. The bronze script form merely consisted of two concentric circles. An inner portion of the character was later added, namely a mutated form of the seal script character of 米 ("rice"), representing grains within the stomach (see also 鬯). The character looked like 𦞅 in the small seal script. In the clerical script form, the upper component was simplified to the unrelated 田 as an instance of ' simplification. The ancient form of the character can be seen within the lower component of 𦳊.

胆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (body part) + phonetic 旦.

背.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|北|肉|alt2=月|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc|t2=meat}}. Originally written as {{lang|zh|北}}, semantic {{lang|zh|肉}} was added to be distinguished from the derived meaning of {{lang|zh|北}} (“north”).
背.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 北 + semantic 肉 (meat). Originally written as 北, semantic 肉 was added to be distinguished from the derived meaning of 北 (“north”).

胎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 台.

components.sense: a shape representing a pregnant figure

胞.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|肉|alt1=月|包|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=s|c2=p|t1=flesh|t2=a shape representing a pregnant figure}}. It conveys the meaning of the membrane that encloses the fetus.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
胞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh) + phonetic 包 (a shape representing a pregnant figure). It conveys the meaning of the membrane that encloses the fetus.

胴.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|肉|alt1=月|同|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=flesh}}. It expresses the meaning of a large intestine.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
胴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh) + phonetic 同. It expresses the meaning of a large intestine.

胸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|肉|匈|c1=s|c2=p|t1=meat|ls=psc}}. {{zh-l|*匈}} is the original form of this character, with {{zh-l|*肉}} added later.
胸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + phonetic 匈. 匈 is the original form of this character, with 肉 added later.

能.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: a bear. Compare {{och-l|熊|bear}}. In the character, two paws are visible as a pair of 匕 and the face with the open mouth is stylized as 月.
能.originText: a bear. Compare 熊. In the character, two paws are visible as a pair of 匕 and the face with the open mouth is stylized as 月.

脂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + phonetic 旨.

脅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 劦 + semantic 肉.

脇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 劦.

脈.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh) + phonetic 𠂢.

脊.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}} of a fish spine. {{zh-l|*肉}} was added later to distinguish it. The top component corrupted into {{zh-l|*𠦬}}, making it a {{Han compound|ls=psc|朿|肉|c1=p|c2=s|t2=flesh|nocap=y}}.
脊.originText: Originally a of a fish spine. 肉 was added later to distinguish it. The top component corrupted into 𠦬, making it a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朿 + semantic 肉 (flesh).

腎.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|臤|肉|alt2=⺼|t2=meat; flesh|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a body part, the kidneys.
腎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臤 + semantic 肉 (meat; flesh) – a body part, the kidneys.

腐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 府 + semantic 肉 (flesh; body).

腕.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|肉|alt1=⺼|t1=meat, body part|宛|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a part of the body.
腕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat, body part) + phonetic 宛 – a part of the body.

腫.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat, flesh) + phonetic 重.

腰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (flesh) + phonetic 要.

腸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (body) + phonetic 昜.

腹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|肉|t1=meat; flesh|复|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a part of the body.
腹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat; flesh) + phonetic 复 – a part of the body.

膚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + phonetic 盧.

膜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 莫.

膝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat, body) + phonetic 桼 – the knee. Originally 厀, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 桼 + semantic 卩 (kneeling person).

膨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (meat; flesh) + phonetic 彭.

膳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 + phonetic 善.

臆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (body) + phonetic 意.

臓.originRaw:
Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|臟|f=藏|t=蔵}}.

In current form {{Han compound|肉|蔵|lang=ja|alt1=⺼|t1=body|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a kind of body part.
臓.originText: Japanese shinjitai 臟藏蔵. In current form Phono-semantic compound: semantic 肉 (body) + phonetic 蔵 – a kind of body part.

臣.originText: A vertical eye of a man looking downwards. As an individual character it has taken on the meanings “slave; servant; minister”, while the meaning relating to eyes appears when used as a radical, such as in 臨 and 監. Compare 目. Unrelated to 𦣞.
