臨.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 臣 (eye) + semantic 人 (person) + phonetic 品 (objects) – a person looking down at some objects. Alternatively analyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 臥 + phonetic 品.

自.originText: a nose — original form of 鼻. Later phonetically borrowed as an instance of for 自. Folk etymology considers the meaning to arise from a habit of pointing at one’s nose to indicate oneself.

臭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|犬|t1=dog|自|t2=nose|ls=ic}}, referring to the dog's strong sense of smell. Original form of {{och-l|嗅|to smell}}.
臭.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 犬 (dog) + semantic 自 (nose), referring to the dog's strong sense of smell. Original form of 嗅.

至.originText: an arrow stuck into the ground. Some folk etymologies interpret the whole pictogram as an eagle catching a prey. Compare 畀 and 矢. See also the bottom component of 睪, the original versions of 弗 and the top component of 𢦏.

致.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 至 + semantic 攴.

臼.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}: a [[mortar]]. See the original version of [[舂]], in which a pestle is visible on top. Unrelated to the top component of [[學]], [[兒]], [[䳔]], [[鼠]], and [[叟]].
臼.originText: a mortar. See the original version of 舂, in which a pestle is visible on top. Unrelated to the top component of 學, 兒, 䳔, 鼠, and 叟.

興.originText: four hands (舁) lifting an object. In oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, the central object had various shapes (such as a lifting tray, sometimes resembling 井). It eventually standardized into 同 in later scripts.

舌.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a snake's tongue emerging upwards from a mouth ({{zh-l|*口}}).

Evolution:
* '''Oracle bone script''': Originally a mouth + a forked snake tongue. Later variants added a horizontal stroke at the base to indicate location, which often evolved into a second fork (double-forked).
* '''Bronze script''' (Late Shang / Early Western Zhou): Standardized with four dots symmetrically placed between the double forks and the mouth. 
* '''Later''': The dots disappeared, simplifying into the modern form.

Compare {{och-l|舌|tr=*m-lat}} and {{och-l|蛇|tr=*m-laj|snake}}. See also [[言]], [[音]] and [[告]]. Unrelated to [[舍]], in which it represents a hut.
舌.originText: a snake's tongue emerging upwards from a mouth (口). Evolution: Compare 舌 and 蛇. See also 言, 音 and 告. Unrelated to 舍, in which it represents a hut.

舗.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

The original character is [[鋪]]. {{Han compound|金|甫|lang=ja|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=metal|no_och2=y}}. It originally referred to a metal fitting used to attach a metal ring to a door. Its phonetic component is related to [[布]] and [[敷]], and had their meanings ("spreading" or "laying out") borrowed, which later extended to mean "store" or "shop." The modern standard form of the character had its semantic component changed to [[舎]] (meaning "house" or "building") to emphasize its meaning as a "store" or "shop."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
舗.originText: The original character is 鋪. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 甫 + no_och2=y. It originally referred to a metal fitting used to attach a metal ring to a door. Its phonetic component is related to 布 and 敷, and had their meanings ("spreading" or "laying out") borrowed, which later extended to mean "store" or "shop." The modern standard form of the character had its semantic component changed to 舎 (meaning "house" or "building") to emphasize its meaning as a "store" or "shop."

舞.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|無|舛|t2=steps, feet in convergent direction|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|abb1=y}}. This character was coined to preserve the original meaning of {{zh-l|*無}}, which is "dancing"; hence, the upper component also adds part of the meaning. A conservative variant is [[𦨅]].
舞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 無 + semantic 舛 (steps, feet in convergent direction). This character was coined to preserve the original meaning of 無, which is "dancing"; hence, the upper component also adds part of the meaning. A conservative variant is 𦨅.

舟.originText: a boat. Later sometimes written as 月, 肉 or 凡 in components.

航.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 (boat) + phonetic 亢.

般.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The proto-form of {{zh-l|*盤}} + {{zh-l|*攴}}. The proto-form of {{zh-l|*盤}} was later corrupted into {{zh-l|*舟}}, and {{zh-l|*攴}} evolved into {{zh-l|*殳}}.
般.originText: The proto-form of 盤 + 攴. The proto-form of 盤 was later corrupted into 舟, and 攴 evolved into 殳.

舶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 (boat) + phonetic 白.

舷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 (boat) + phonetic 玄.

船.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 (boat) + phonetic 㕣.

艇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 (boat) + phonetic 廷

艦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 舟 + phonetic 監.

良.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}}. Possibly depicts corridors and a room, in which case it would be the original form of {{zh-l|*廊}}. See also the top component of [[复]]. Unrelated to [[食]], [[艮]] and [[即]].
良.originText: Possibly depicts corridors and a room, in which case it would be the original form of 廊. See also the top component of 复. Unrelated to 食, 艮 and 即.

色.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}

{{Han compound|爪|卩|ls=ic|t1=claw; hand|t2=kneeling person}}. It depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person. {{zh-l|*色}} was an ancient form of {{zh-l|*印}}; they both originally meant "to press down", meaning now written with {{zh-l|*抑}}. The character was later borrowed phonetically to mean "color".

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets this character as an {{Han compound|人|卪|ls=ic|t1=person; human|nocap=y}}, which refers to the expression, vitality or complexion of a person's face.

Sometimes, especially in folk etymology, the character is misinterpreted as a proto-form of {{och-l|*絕}}. The bottom part is unrelated to {{och-l|*巴}}.
色.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 爪 (claw; hand) + semantic 卩 (kneeling person). It depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person. 色 was an ancient form of 印; they both originally meant "to press down", meaning now written with 抑. The character was later borrowed phonetically to mean "color". ' interprets this character as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person; human) + semantic 卪, which refers to the expression, vitality or complexion of a person's face. Sometimes, especially in folk etymology, the character is misinterpreted as a proto-form of 絕. The bottom part is unrelated to 巴.

芋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 于 – taro.

芝.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|alt1=艹|t1=grass|之|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a type of plant.
芝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 之 – a type of plant.

芯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 心.

花.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|alt1=艹|化|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=grass; plant}}. Originally {{zh-l|*𠌶}} or {{zh-l|*華}} before the {{w|Han dynasty}}.
花.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 化. Originally 𠌶 or 華 before the.

芳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 方

芽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 牙.

苗.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + semantic 田 (field).

苛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 可.

若.originText: a person combing their hair; obedient. Later 口 was added and the original component came to be written 叒.

苦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|古|c1=s|c2=p|t1=grass|ls=psc}} – bitter (as in bitter plants).
苦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 古 – bitter (as in bitter plants).

英.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 央.

茂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 戊. Applying this character to mean “cyclopentadiene” in organic chemistry results from the decomposition of the character as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 艸 (radical for aromatic compounds) + semantic 戊 (five-carbon ring), since the conjugate base of cyclopentadiene (cyclopentadienyl anion) is aromatic.

茨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 次.

茶.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 余. 茶, then slightly modified into a more conservative 茶, originates as a graphical modification of archaic 荼, used for “tea” in classical sources. The modern version is unrelated to the bottom right component of 條 .

草.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|alt1=艹|早|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=grass; plant}}. Originally referred to {{zh-l|*皂}}, and later borrowed for the “grass” sense, replacing {{zh-l|*艸}}.
草.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 早. Originally referred to 皂, and later borrowed for the “grass” sense, replacing 艸.

荒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass, plant) + phonetic 巟. Note: The middle part could be found as 亾 instead of 亡.

荷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 何.

菊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 匊.

菌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 囷.

菓.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 果 (fruit).

菜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 采.

華.originText: ; this was the original form of 花. In the bronze inscription form, the top part of the glyph resembles flowers of a plant, and the bottom part (于) resembles its stalk and leaves. Also, with 于 functioning as the phonetic part. In the seal script, 艸 was added as a semantic component. 華 (𦻏) and 𠌶 were initially the same character, but they were erroneously split in ' into two entries.

萎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 委.

落.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 洛.

葉.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|枼|c1=s|c2=p|t2=leaf|ls=psc|no_och2=y}}. {{och-l|*枼}} is the original pictogram for this word; {{och-l|*艸}} was added to differentiate.<ref>裘錫圭 『文字学概要』 商務印書館、1988年、119頁。
張世超、孫凌安、金国泰、馬如森 『金文形義通解』 中文出版社、1996年、1467-1468頁。
季旭昇撰 『説文新証』 芸文印書館、2014年、491頁。</ref>
葉.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 枼 (leaf) + no_och2=y. 枼 is the original pictogram for this word; 艸 was added to differentiate.

著.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass; plant) + phonetic 者.

葛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 曷.

葬.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|茻|t1=grass|死|t2=dead person|ls=ic}} – bury the dead 死 in the grass 茻. Top is now grass radical ({{zh-l|艹|tr=-}}), while bottom is simplified to [[廾]], hence graphically {{Han compound|艸|死|廾|alt1=艹}}.
葬.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 茻 (grass) + semantic 死 (dead person) – bury the dead 死 in the grass 茻. Top is now grass radical (艹), while bottom is simplified to 廾, hence graphically Compound: 艸 + 死 + 廾.

蒸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 烝.

蓄.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|alt1=艹|t1=grass, plant|畜|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to cultivate plants, to store grain, to save.
蓄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass, plant) + phonetic 畜 – to cultivate plants, to store grain, to save.

蓋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 盍 — a thatch. 盍 is the original character for the “cover” sense. However, because this original character was borrowed to mean “why not”, the scope of senses for 蓋 expanded to include the “cover” sense (and its extended meanings).

蔑.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𦰋 (person) + semantic 戈 (dagger-axe) – a weapon striking a person's lower leg — to obliterate. 𦰋 (“person”) was composed of an eye with eyebrows (now written 眉) on top of 人. The eye and eyebrows are written sc=Hani in the modern form, and 人 has combined with 戈 to form 戍.

蔽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 敝.

薄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 溥.

薦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|廌|t1=grass|t2=wild beast|ls=ic|ls2=j}} - "pasture". Later borrowed for sound to mean "recommend".
薦.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + semantic 廌 (wild beast) - "pasture". Later borrowed for sound to mean "recommend".

薪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 + phonetic 新.

藍.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 監.

藤.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|艸|t1=grass|滕|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a type of plant.
藤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 滕 – a type of plant.

藩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 潘

藻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 艸 (grass) + phonetic 澡. Originally 薻.

虎.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{liushu|p}}. {{zh-l|*虍}} represents the tiger's head. The torso has disappeared and the legs and the tail have transformed into {{zh-l|*人}} in the small seal script and later {{zh-l|*儿}} in the clerical script.
虎.originText: 虍 represents the tiger's head. The torso has disappeared and the legs and the tail have transformed into 人 in the small seal script and later 儿 in the clerical script.

虐.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the oracle bone script, an {{Han compound|虎|人|ls=ic|t1=tiger|t2=person|nocap=1}} — a tiger about to eat a person. Meaning later extended to mean "cruel", "tyrannical".<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref>
虐.originText: In the oracle bone script, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 虎 (tiger) + semantic 人 (person) — a tiger about to eat a person. Meaning later extended to mean "cruel", "tyrannical".

虞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虍 (tiger) + phonetic 吳.

虫.originRaw:
[[File:Britannica Rattlesnake.jpg|thumb|120px|A venomous snake, from which this character originated.]]
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: a snake.

The character originally represented a type of venomous snake, while the derivative {{l|zh|蟲}} represented worms and insects (or insect-like things). {{lang|zh|虫}} was later borrowed for {{l|zh|蟲}} (possibly via simplification), and the character {{l|zh|虺}} was created to represent the original meaning.
虫.originText: a snake. The character originally represented a type of venomous snake, while the derivative 蟲 represented worms and insects (or insect-like things). 虫 was later borrowed for 蟲 (possibly via simplification), and the character 虺 was created to represent the original meaning.

虹.originText: Originally in the oracle bone script. The ancient Chinese regarded the rainbow as a two-headed dragon, as in an oracle-bone divination inscription: 有出虹自北飲于河 In the seal script, it has become a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虫 (insect; creature) + phonetic 工.

蚊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虫 (insect) + phonetic 文.

蛇.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|虫|它|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. {{zh-l|*它}} was also the original pictographic form of this character.
蛇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虫 + phonetic 它. 它 was also the original pictographic form of this character.

蜂.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han simp|蠭}}. {{Han compound|虫|t1=insect|夆|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – a kind of insect.
蜂.originText: 蠭. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虫 (insect) + phonetic 夆 – a kind of insect.

蜜.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|宓|虫|t2=insect|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. The original form is {{zh-m|𧖅}}.
蜜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 宓 + semantic 虫 (insect). The original form is 𧖅.

融.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 鬲 (cauldron) + phonetic 蟲.

血.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 一 (drop of blood) + semantic 皿 (container) - a drop of blood inside a chalice for sacrificial uses. In the oracle bone script, the character was used to refer to killing animals to obtain blood to sacrifice to ancestors: {{zh-x|血 三 羊。|to (ritually) bleed three sheep|CL-PC|collapsed=y|ref=' #22231}} {{zh-x|在\才{zài} 血 室|to be in the blood (sacrifice) hall|CL-PC|collapsed=y|ref=' #41091}}

衆.originRaw: Variant of {{zh-l|*眾}}, with the top component {{zh-l|*罒}} replaced by {{zh-l|*血}}, and the bottom component {{zh-l|*𫡑}} replaced by {{zh-l|*乑}}.
衆.originText: Variant of 眾, with the top component 罒 replaced by 血, and the bottom component 𫡑 replaced by 乑.

行.originText: a street intersection. Original form of 行. Later to represent 行. Originally symmetric, it has been simplified asymmetrically; the left half 彳 is widely used as a radical, while the right half 亍 finds occasional use, and the character can be broken up as Compound: 彳 + 亍, though originally it was not a compound.

術.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 行 (street, path) + phonetic 朮. For the “to throw” definition, from.

街.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 行 + phonetic 圭. Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character and 厓 either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.

衛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 行 + phonetic 韋.

衝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 行 + phonetic 重.

衡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 行 + semantic 角 (horn) + semantic 大 (big).

衣.originText: Outline of the chest, upper clothing. Compare to the upper part of 文. This pictogram 衣 can be split into two parts and hold another component (e.g., 裹, 衮, 褱, 襄, and 𧝑 as used in 㞡 > 展). See also the top component of 雜.

表.originText: Originally 𧘝, an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 衣 (garment; clothing) + semantic 毛 (hair; feather) — outer garment. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 錶 (etymology 2) in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (漢字簡化方案漢字簡化方案) in 1956.

衰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} — a piece of clothing made from palm fibers to be used as a raincoat (original form of [[蓑]]) ({{zh-ref|Ji Xusheng, 2004}}).
衰.originText: a piece of clothing made from palm fibers to be used as a raincoat (original form of 蓑) .

衷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + phonetic 中 (middle; center).

袋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 代 + semantic 衣 (clothes).

袖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothing) + phonetic 由.

被.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothing) + phonetic 皮.

裁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|衣|𢦏|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. However, the phonetic component has a reference to a blade and an arrow, hence to the concept of cutting (e.g., fabric).
裁.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 + phonetic 𢦏. However, the phonetic component has a reference to a blade and an arrow, hence to the concept of cutting (e.g., fabric).

裂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 列 (to tear) + semantic 衣 (clothes) — to cut and tear clothes. The phonetic 列 depicts bones being cut up with a blade and arranged in a line.

裏.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + phonetic 里.

裕.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|谷|衣|c1=p|c2=s|t2=clothes}}. Folk etymology claims {{lang|zh|sc=Hani|谷}} to represent space in the clothes.
裕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 谷 + semantic 衣 (clothes). Folk etymology claims sc=Hani to represent space in the clothes.

補.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + phonetic 甫.

裸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothing) + phonetic 果 – lacking clothes, naked.

製.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|制|衣|t1=to cut out; to make|t2=clothes|ls=ic|ls2=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}.
製.originText: Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 制 (to cut out; to make) + semantic 衣 (clothes).

裾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + phonetic 居.

複.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|衣|复|c1=s|c2=p|t1=clothes|t2=to return|ls=psc}} – lined garment.
複.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothes) + phonetic 复 (to return) – lined garment.

褒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 + phonetic 保.

襟.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|衣|alt1=⻂|禁|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=clothing}}. It refers to the seam of a garment, conveying the idea of a “collar.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
襟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 衣 (clothing) + phonetic 禁. It refers to the seam of a garment, conveying the idea of a “collar.”

襲.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 龖 + semantic 衣 (cloth). The bronze inscription and ' zhouwen forms were in the form of 𧟟. The Shuowen small seal script form and subsequent forms are in the form of 襲, as the phonetic component 龖 has been reduced to 龍.

西.originText: The oracle-bone forms of 西 fall into two types: open-topped and closed-topped. The open-topped type is found only in periods I–II, especially in the Bin and Chu groups; later scripts inherit the closed-topped type. The open-topped form has been interpreted as a bird's nest, possibly related to 栖 (“to perch; to roost”). The later closed-topped form may be related to 囟: in the Zhouyuan oracle-bone inscriptions, 囟 is used for 西.

要.originText: a man 大 then drawn as a woman (女) with two hands pointing to his/her midsection. On top of the character there was huge eye 目, then stylized as a horn 角. The hands gradually shifted upwards; hence, a nearly original version of the character is 𡢗. All the upper part was eventually stylized as 覀. Unrelated to 栗 but partly related to 票. Original meaning was “waist” (now 腰).

覆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 襾 + phonetic 復.

見.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|ic}} - {{Han compound|目|t1=eye|卩|t2=kneeling person}} – a kneeling human figure with a large eye for a head. Similar but unrelated to {{zh-l|*艮}}. See also {{zh-l|*夏}} and {{zh-l|*監}}.
見.originText: Compound: 目 (eye) + 卩 (kneeling person) – a kneeling human figure with a large eye for a head. Similar but unrelated to 艮. See also 夏 and 監.

規.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally a {{liushu|p|nocap=y}}: a cross-shaped measuring compass similar to {{zh-l|*乂}}. The protoform also appears as the bottom component in the oracle bone script of {{och-l|*畫}}.

Later reformulated as {{Han compound|夫|見|t1=husband|t2=see|nocap=yes}}, which is traditionally considered an {{liushu|ic|nocap=y}}. However, {{zh-ref|Smith (2011)}} proposes that the left component is an abbreviation of the phonetic component {{och-l|癸}}. Compare the [[癸#Glyph_origin|''Shizhoupian'' script form]] of {{lang|zh|癸}}.

Chen (2021) instead suggests that the {{lang|zh|夫}} is the left-hand side of {{och-l|*矩}}, after {{och-l|*矩}} became seen as a compound; since both characters refer to tools, it would be natural for their semantic components to align.<ref>[https://www.fdgwz.org.cn/Web/Show/7845 陳劍：說“規”等字並論一些特別的形聲字意符]</ref>
規.originText: Originally a : a cross-shaped measuring compass similar to 乂. The protoform also appears as the bottom component in the oracle bone script of 畫. Later reformulated as Compound: 夫 (husband) + 見 (see), which is traditionally considered an. However, proposes that the left component is an abbreviation of the phonetic component 癸. Compare the Shizhoupian script form of 癸. Chen (2021) instead suggests that the 夫 is the left-hand side of 矩, after 矩 became seen as a compound; since both characters refer to tools, it would be natural for their semantic components to align.

視.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 示 + semantic 見 (see). Related to 見. The Chu form did not include the phonetic 示 component, making it near-identical to 見, but with the lower component a kneeling figure rather than a standing one.

親.originText: Bronze script: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 辛 + semantic 見 (see). Seal script: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𣓀 + semantic 見 (see). The left part (a chisel with a tree at the bottom to indicate "hazelnut branch" used as a whip) was then stylized as 亲, which originally is a variant of 辛, the chisel.

観.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|觀}}. {{Han simp|觀|f=雚|t=𮥶}}. Compare [[権]].

The modern Japanese usage is of reform ({{w|shinjitai}}) nature.
観.originText: Variant of 觀. 觀雚𮥶. Compare 権. The modern Japanese usage is of reform nature.

角.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a horn. A conservative version is [[𧢲]]. Similar but unrelated to [[甬]], [[用]], and the bottom part of [[備]].
角.originText: a horn. A conservative version is 𧢲. Similar but unrelated to 甬, 用, and the bottom part of 備.

解.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|角|t1=horn|刀|t2=knife|牛|t3=cow|ls=ic}} – a knife separates a horn from a cow, i.e. “cut up (an ox)”.
解.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 角 (horn) + semantic 刀 (knife) + semantic 牛 (cow) – a knife separates a horn from a cow, i.e. “cut up (an ox)”.

触.originRaw:
Unorthodox variant {{Han simp|觸|f=蜀|t=虫|nocap=y}} found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary <big>《字學三正》</big>. Also found in 《{{lw|zh|宋元以來俗字譜}}》, a {{w|Variant Chinese character|variant forms}} dictionary compiled in 1930.

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956 {{w|Chinese Character Simplification Scheme}}. <!-- Refer https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/漢字簡化方案 -->
触.originText: Unorthodox variant 觸蜀虫 found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《字學三正》. Also found in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a dictionary compiled in 1930. Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956.

言.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}} – From {{zh-l|*口}} and ▽(possibly original form of {{zh-l|*弋}}, marking location). Later: from {{zh-l|*口}} and {{zh-l|*辛}} or {{zh-l|*䇂}} (possibly mixed with {{zh-l|*舌}}).

Possibly related to the semantic family of {{zh-l|*舌}} ("protruding/emerging", opposite to {{zh-l|*音}} "converging/covering") or {{zh-l|*語}} ("facing/front"). May also relate to {{zh-l|*獻}}, {{zh-l|*諺}}, and {{zh-l|*唁}} ("formal presentation/declaration").

See also {{zh-l|*音}}.
言.originText: From 口 and ▽(possibly original form of 弋, marking location). Later: from 口 and 辛 or 䇂 (possibly mixed with 舌). Possibly related to the semantic family of 舌 ("protrudingcovering") or 語 ("facing/front"). May also relate to 獻, 諺, and 唁 ("formal presentation/declaration"). See also 音.

訂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 丁.

訃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 卜.

計.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 言 (say) + semantic 十 (all).

討.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 肘 + semantic 言. ' interprets it as an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + semantic 寸 (hand) – rectify.

訓.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|言|川|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=speech}}. It conveys the meaning of "preaching a teaching."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
訓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 川. It conveys the meaning of "preaching a teaching."

託.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 乇.

記.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech; words) + phonetic 己.

訟.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (say) + phonetic 公.

訪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (talk) + phonetic 方.

設.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|埶|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. {{zh-l|埶}} in this character initially appears as an ancient short form ⿰𡉣攴 ({{zh-ref|Jiang, 2019}}).
設.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 埶. 埶 in this character initially appears as an ancient short form ⿰𡉣攴 .

許.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech; words) + phonetic 午.

訴.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|t1=word, speak|斥|t2=accuse, blame|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to accuse verbally.
訴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word, speak) + phonetic 斥 (accuse, blame) – to accuse verbally.

診.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 㐱.

証.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han simp|證|f=登|t=正}}. {{Han compound|言|正|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=speech}}. The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to admonish" and was later used in the sense of "proof" or "evidence."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
証.originText: 證登正. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 正. The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to admonish" and was later used in the sense of "proof" or "evidence."

詐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 乍.

詔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word; speech) + phonetic 召

評.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 平.

詞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 司.

詠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 永.

詣.originText: By ' and 字統字通, and following Zhengzhang (2003), a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 旨. Alternatively, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + semantic 旨 (delicious) — word use so skilled as to be delicious. The first interpretation is seemingly most accepted.

試.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 式.

詩.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|t1=speech|寺|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – poetry is a form of language, speech.
詩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 寺 – poetry is a form of language, speech.

詮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 全.

詰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|言|吉|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=speech}}. It expresses the meaning of inquiring in detail.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
詰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 吉. It expresses the meaning of inquiring in detail.

話.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|𠯑|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=word}}. The right component is not related to {{och-l|舌|tongue|id=2}}.
話.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word) + phonetic 𠯑. The right component is not related to 舌.

該.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 亥.

詳.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 羊.

誇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (words, language) + phonetic 夸

誌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 志.

認.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 忍.

誓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 折 + semantic 言 (speech).

誕.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word, speech) + phonetic 延.

誘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word, language) + phonetic 秀.

語.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 吾. Part of a *ŋa- word family centred on "to face; to respond to": 御, 禦, 圉, 迓, 逆, 晤, 忤. The original sense was likely "to face someone with speech; speech directed at an interlocutor", as opposed to 言, which denotes the speech act itself. Compare : 直言曰言，論難曰語.

誠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 成.

誤.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|t1=speech|吳|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to speak an error.
誤.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 吳 – to speak an error.

誰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speak) + phonetic 隹.

課.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|果|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=to say}} – to assess; to examine.
課.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (to say) + phonetic 果 – to assess; to examine.

調.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 周.

談.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 炎.

請.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (say) + phonetic 青.

論.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (say) + phonetic 侖.

諦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 帝.

諧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 皆.

諭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 俞.

諮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 咨 (to consult) + semantic 言 (speak).

諸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 者.

諾.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|言|若|c1=s|c2=p|t1=word, speak|t2=like this; such}} — to answer affirmatively.
諾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word, speak) + phonetic 若 (like this; such) — to answer affirmatively.

謀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 某.

謁.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

The original character is [[謁]]. {{Han compound|言|曷|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=speech}}. It expresses the meaning "to accuse" or "to inform." It is also used with the meaning "to meet face-to-face." The modern Jōyō kanji is a simplified form.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
謁.originText: The original character is 謁. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 曷. It expresses the meaning "to accuse" or "to inform." It is also used with the meaning "to meet face-to-face." The modern Jōyō kanji is a simplified form.

謄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朕 + semantic 言 (say)

謎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 迷 (to be lost).

謙.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|言|兼|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=speech}}. It expresses the state of being respectful or reverent.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
謙.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 兼. It expresses the state of being respectful or reverent.

講.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (say) + phonetic 冓.

謝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (word; speech) + phonetic 射.

謹.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|言|t1=speech|堇|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to speak caution.
謹.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (speech) + phonetic 堇 – to speak caution.

識.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (say) + phonetic 戠.

譜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (sound) + phonetic 普.

警.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敬 + semantic 言 (spoken language, speech).

議.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 (talk) + phonetic 義.

譲.originRaw: {{Han simp|讓|f=襄|t=㐮}}. The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
譲.originText: 讓襄㐮. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

護.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 言 + phonetic 蒦.

谷.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} — [[valley]] ({{zh-l|*口}}) in between two [[mountain]] walls represented by near-parallel lines. The original version is [[𠔌]]. See also [[㕣]].
谷.originText: valley (口) in between two mountain walls represented by near-parallel lines. The original version is 𠔌. See also 㕣.

豆.originText: some kind of container. Borrowed phonetically for the plant name. Displaced Old Chinese 菽. Unrelated to the bottom part of 豊.

豊.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally an {{Han compound|壴|玨|ls=ic|t1=drum|t2=strings of jade|nocap=1}} – ceremony. Original form of {{zh-l|*禮}}.

In some bronze inscriptions, {{zh-l|*壴}} has been split into two, with {{zh-l|*豆}} on the bottom. Later scripts, including the seal script, have inherited this corruption, leading ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' to interpret this character as a {{liushu|p|nocap=1}} containing {{zh-l|*豆|vessel}}.

Due to similarity with the unrelated {{zh-l|*豐}}, 豊 has also been used as one of its variants.
豊.originText: Originally an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 壴 (drum) + semantic 玨 (strings of jade) – ceremony. Original form of 禮. In some bronze inscriptions, 壴 has been split into two, with 豆 on the bottom. Later scripts, including the seal script, have inherited this corruption, leading ' to interpret this character as a containing 豆. Due to similarity with the unrelated 豐, 豊 has also been used as one of its variants.

豚.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 肉 (meat) + semantic 豕 (pig).

象.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} - [[pictographic]] representation of an elephant. {{zh-l|⺈}} represents the trunk, {{zh-l|𫩏}} represents the head, and {{zh-l|𧰨|tr=-}} represents the body.
象.originText: pictographic representation of an elephant. ⺈ represents the trunk, 𫩏 represents the head, and 𧰨 represents the body.

豪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 高 + semantic 豕 (pig, boar).

貌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 豹 + semantic 皃 (looks). Originally written as 皃, which is a of the face.

貝.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – [[cowrie]] used as currency in ancient China. Unrelated to the original version of [[則]]. See also the top component of [[得]]. Unrelated to [[目]].
貝.originText: cowrie used as currency in ancient China. Unrelated to the original version of 則. See also the top component of 得. Unrelated to 目.

貞.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|p}} - a [[ding#Etymology 3|ding]] (oracle bone script [[File:貞-oracle.svg|30px|class=skin-invert]], [[File:貞-oracle-2.svg|30px|class=skin-invert]]; same as {{och-l|鼎}}). Borrowed phonetically for “to divine”; however, bronze tripods in ancient China were sometimes used during rituals. Later, a new character was created by adding {{zh-l|*卜|to divine}} as a radical, hence a semantic component, thus getting {{zh-l|*鼑}} (oracle bone script [[File:貞-oracle-3.svg|30px|class=skin-invert]]; bronze script [[File:貞-bronze.svg|30px|class=skin-invert]]. The bottom component was stylized into the unrelated {{zh-l|*貝}} during the Warring States. Compare {{zh-l|*𠟭}} > {{zh-l|*則}}.
貞.originText: a ding (oracle bone script,; same as 鼎). Borrowed phonetically for “to divine”; however, bronze tripods in ancient China were sometimes used during rituals. Later, a new character was created by adding 卜 as a radical, hence a semantic component, thus getting 鼑 (oracle bone script; bronze script. The bottom component was stylized into the unrelated 貝 during the Warring States. Compare 𠟭 > 則.

負.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 人 (person) + semantic 貝 (cowry).

財.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|貝|才|c1=s|c2=p|t1=shell|ls=psc}}. 才 is also a reference to one's abilities, hence intellectual resources; in this particular syllable, the abilities are probably thought as financial possibilities and resources.
財.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell) + phonetic 才. 才 is also a reference to one's abilities, hence intellectual resources; in this particular syllable, the abilities are probably thought as financial possibilities and resources.

貢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 工 + semantic 貝.

貧.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|分|貝|t2=money|c1=p|c2=s|ls=psc}}. Since the phonetic means "to divide", a possible mnemonic is "to divide one's money".
貧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 分 + semantic 貝 (money). Since the phonetic means "to divide", a possible mnemonic is "to divide one's money".

貨.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|化|貝|t2=shell, money|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – valuable goods.
貨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 化 + semantic 貝 (shell, money) – valuable goods.

販.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (cowry) + phonetic 反.

貪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 今 (open mouth) + semantic 貝 (money) + no_och2=1.

貫.originText: two 貝 strung together. ' mistakes the character for a compound of 毌 + 貝.

責.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朿 + semantic 貝 (cowry; money) – tax; debt. Top component now resembles 生 (without the diagonal stroke) – compare 青, 素.

貯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shellfish) + phonetic 宁.

貴.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han simp|䝿|f=臾|t=𠀐}}. {{Han compound|臾|貝|c1=p|c2=s|t2=money cowrie|ls=psc}}.
貴.originText: 䝿臾𠀐. Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臾 + semantic 貝 (money cowrie).

買.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 网 (net) + semantic 貝 (money cowrie). The original version is 𧵽. consider it to be a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 羅 + semantic 貝 (money cowrie) + no_och=1.

貸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|貝|代|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=shell}}. The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to give" or "to bestow," and later came to be used with the meaning of "to lend."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
貸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell) + phonetic 代. The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to give" or "to bestow," and later came to be used with the meaning of "to lend."

費.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 弗 + semantic 貝 (cowry).

貼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell) + phonetic 占.

貿.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 卯 + semantic 貝 (cowrie).

賀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 加 + semantic 貝 (shellfish money).

賂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell; money) + phonetic 各.

賃.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|任|貝|t2=shell, money|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – a kind of payment. 任 has meaning of “duty, employment”, so connotations of “money paid for employment (hire)” or “money that one has a duty to pay (rent)”.
賃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 任 + semantic 貝 (shell, money) – a kind of payment. 任 has meaning of “duty, employment”, so connotations of “money paid for employment (hire)” or “money that one has a duty to pay (rent)”.

賄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (cowry; money) + phonetic 有.

資.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 次 + semantic 貝 (shell-money) – “property, resource”.

賊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 則 + semantic 戈 (weapon). This was later reinterpreted as a compound of 貝 and 戎 to produce the modern form.

賓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 𡧍 + semantic 貝.

賜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell, money) + phonetic 易.

賞.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 商 + semantic 貝 (cowry).

賠.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|貝|咅|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=shell; money}}. It expresses the idea of “atoning for” or “making amends.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
賠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell; money) + phonetic 咅. It expresses the idea of “atoning for” or “making amends.”

賢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|臤|貝|t2=money|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – worthy, valuable (like money)
賢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 臤 + semantic 貝 (money) – worthy, valuable (like money)

賦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|貝|武|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=shell; money}}. It expresses the meaning of collecting taxes.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
賦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell; money) + phonetic 武. It expresses the meaning of collecting taxes.

質.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|斦|貝|ls=ic}}. [[w:zh:朱骏声|Zhu Junsheng]] also interpret this as a {{liushu|psc|nocap=1}}, where he regards {{lang|zh|斦}} as an original form of {{och-l|櫍}}.
質.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 斦 + semantic 貝. Zhu Junsheng also interpret this as a, where he regards 斦 as an original form of 櫍.

賭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|貝|者|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=shell; money}}. It expresses the meaning “to wager” or “to bet.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
賭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shell; money) + phonetic 者. It expresses the meaning “to wager” or “to bet.”

購.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 (shellfish) + phonetic 冓.

贈.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 貝 + phonetic 曾.

赤.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 大 (person, big) + semantic 火 (fire) – the color of fire (a person by a fire). The original version is 𤆍. The man on top is simplified as 土 as in 去 and 走 (< 𧺆). The fire is stylized as well, but an intermediate and obsolete variant is 灻.

赦.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the bronze script, it was written as {{zh-l|𢼜}}, a {{Han compound|亦|攴|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=hand holding a stick|nocap=1}}. In later scripts, the phonetic component was replaced with {{och-l|赤}}.
赦.originText: In the bronze script, it was written as 𢼜, a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 亦 + semantic 攴 (hand holding a stick). In later scripts, the phonetic component was replaced with 赤.

走.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: a running man. An additional {{och-l|*止|foot}} was added later. The variant form {{och-l|*𧺆}} preserves the form in the Small Seal Script.

In the modern form, the top component ({{lang|zh|sc=Hani|夭}}) is simplified to the unrelated {{och-l|*土}} and the bottom part is stylized as [[龰]]. See also the top component of {{och-l|*去}} and {{och-l|*赤}}.

As with {{och-l|*圭}}, there are two separate vertical strokes, not a single one.
走.originText: a running man. An additional 止 was added later. The variant form 𧺆 preserves the form in the Small Seal Script. In the modern form, the top component (sc=Hani) is simplified to the unrelated 土 and the bottom part is stylized as 龰. See also the top component of 去 and 赤. As with 圭, there are two separate vertical strokes, not a single one.

跡.originText: Variant of 迹 using a semantic component with similar meaning; see there for more. Current form is a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 足 (foot) + phonetic 亦.

践.originText: 踐戔㦮 for Japanese shinjitai and 踐戔戋 for simplified Chinese.

車.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
[[File:Ancient Chinese chariot and oracle bone script for Che.svg|class=skin-invert-image|thumb|right|Reconstruction of Ancient Chinese Chariots and the Bronze Script of the Character {{zh-l|*車}}]]
{{liushu|p}} – originally a carriage seen from above. In the oracle bone script, there were large wheels on both sides and a central shaft at the front. 

Unrelated to {{zh-l|*倝}} and {{zh-l|*朝}}.
車.originText: originally a carriage seen from above. In the oracle bone script, there were large wheels on both sides and a central shaft at the front. Unrelated to 倝 and 朝.

軌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 + phonetic 九.

軍.originText: semantic 車 + phonetic 勹. The phonetic component here is not 勹, but the original form of 螾, which also acts as the phonetic component of 旬, 勻 and 云. The interprets it as Ideogrammic compound: semantic 車 (cart; chariot) + semantic 勹 (to surround).

軒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (carriage) + phonetic 干

軟.originText: Originally written 輭, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (carriage) + phonetic 耎. 耎 turned into 欠 over time due to a popular variant. The meaning of the carriage is not fully clear. It could be linked to the synonym 柔, which indicates the wood soft enough to be cut, or it could indicate the concept of being tired and weak after dragging a heavy carriage, hence "soft"; the right component could add part of the meaning, since it originally depicts a man under the rain, hence getting soaked (perhaps while dragging a heavy carriage). The modern component 欠 depicts a man kneeling with an open mouth, perhaps while breathing due to exhaustion.

軸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=psc|ls2=ic|車|由|t1=cart, carriage|c1=s|c2=p|t2=to pass through}} — the axle that passes through a cartwheel.
軸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (cart, carriage) + phonetic 由 (to pass through) — the axle that passes through a cartwheel.

較.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (vehicle) + phonetic 交. The original phonetic component was 爻, later corrupted to 交

載.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (chariot) + phonetic 𢦏.

輝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 光 (light; bright) + phonetic 軍.

輩.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 + phonetic 非.

輪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 (carriage) + phonetic 侖.

輸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 車 + phonetic 俞.

轄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 害 + semantic 車 (cart) – linchpin.

辛.originText: Older oracle bone forms of 辛 (⿱∇木) depict newly grown tree shoots, acting as the original ideogram for 新 and 薪. In 新, the top of the axe component (斤) aligns with the bottom of ∇, signifying the chopping of wood. Traditionally interpreted as a pictogram of a tool—a chisel, awl, or spike—used to mark slaves and criminals. However, some scholars suggest this view stems from a conflation with the character 䇂.

辞.originRaw: {{Han simp|⿰⿱厶古辛|f=厶|t=丿}}. In China, first attested in the《張郎墓》stele (300 A.D.). In Japan, first attested in the《長谷寺法華説相圖記》stele (686 A.D.).<ref>{{cite-book|en|author=Roar Bökset|url=https://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01|archivedate=2021-12-02|series=Stockholm East Asian Monographs|volume=11|year=2006|publisher=Stockholm University|title=Long Story of Short Forms: The Evolution of Simplified Chinese Characters|isbn=978-91-628-6832-1|page=99|pageurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202010517/http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:200810/FULLTEXT01#page=103}}</ref>
辞.originText: 厶古辛厶丿. In China, first attested in the《張郎墓》stele (300 A.D.). In Japan, first attested in the《長谷寺法華説相圖記》stele (686 A.D.).

辣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辛 + phonetic 剌.

辱.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 辰 (hoe) + semantic 寸 (hand).

農.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|林|辰|t1=vegetation|t2=hoe}} — to remove weeds.<ref>{{R:yue:Hanzi}}</ref>

In the bronze inscriptions, a semantic {{och-l|*田}} was added.
The {{och-l|*林}} later corrupted into {{och-l|*𦥑}} and the {{och-l|*田}} into {{och-l|*囟}} and in the clerical script they finally combined into {{och-l|*曲}}.
農.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 林 (vegetation) + semantic 辰 (hoe) — to remove weeds. In the bronze inscriptions, a semantic 田 was added. The 林 later corrupted into 𦥑 and the 田 into 囟 and in the clerical script they finally combined into 曲.

辺.originRaw: Etymology 1: {{Han simp|道}}, where the original phonetic component {{och-l|首}} was replaced with the more apparent and less complicated phonetic component {{zh-l|刀}}.
辺.originText: Etymology 1: 道, where the original phonetic component 首 was replaced with the more apparent and less complicated phonetic component 刀.

込.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + semantic 入 (in; enter).

近.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 斤 – to be near something.

返.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|辵|alt1=辶|反|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=s|c2=p|t1=movement|t2=to return}}. It originally conveyed the meaning of "to return along the path one came from" and, by extension, came to signify the idea of "to restore" or "to revert."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>

追.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (movement) + phonetic 𠂤 – moving after, pursuit. See also 師 and 官.

退.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In oracle bone script, {{Han compound|ls=ic|nocap=y|皀|夊|t1=food vessel|t2=downward foot}} – to leave the table after eating. Variants that depicted the vessel as {{zh-l|*酉}} or {{zh-l|*豆}} were common. Bronze inscriptions added {{zh-l|*彳}} to emphasize the action of walking away.

In the modern form the vessel {{zh-l|*皀}} has simplified to the unrelated {{zh-l|*艮}}, similar to {{zh-l|*⾷}}, {{zh-l|*即}}, {{zh-l|*既}}, {{zh-l|*郷}}.

{{w|Shuowen}} misinterprets the seal script form as {{Han compound|辵|alt1=彳|t1=move|夊|t2=walk|日|t3=sun|ls=ic|nocap=y}} – to walk away from the sun, to retreat.
退.originText: In oracle bone script, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 皀 (food vessel) + semantic 夊 (downward foot) – to leave the table after eating. Variants that depicted the vessel as 酉 or 豆 were common. Bronze inscriptions added 彳 to emphasize the action of walking away. In the modern form the vessel 皀 has simplified to the unrelated 艮, similar to ⾷, 即, 既, 郷. misinterprets the seal script form as Ideogrammic compound: semantic 辵 (move) + semantic 夊 (walk) + semantic 日 (sun) – to walk away from the sun, to retreat.

送.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (to walk) + phonetic 灷.

逃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 兆.

透.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walking) + phonetic 秀. This character is not attested in the or.

逐.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 辵 (walking) + semantic 豕 (pig) – "to chase; pursue".

途.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 余.

逝.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walking) + phonetic 折

速.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 束.

Unclear. Generally considered to be unrelated to {{zh-l|*告}} in its original form.

The bronze script forms are identified by 漢語多功能字庫 as being {{Han compound|辵|屮|口|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|c3=s|t1=to walk|tr2=sʰuːʔ}} – “to go, to arrive”.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' incorrectly identifies it as a {{Han compound|辵|alt1=辶|告|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=to walk}}.
造.originText: Unclear. Generally considered to be unrelated to 告 in its original form. The bronze script forms are identified by 漢語多功能字庫 as being Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (to walk) + phonetic 屮 + semantic 口 – “to go, to arrive”. Considered a {{zh-l|後起字}}. {{Han compound|辵|周|alt1=辶|c1=s|c2=p|t1=walking|ls=psc}}.
週.originText: Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walking) + phonetic 周.

{{Han compound|辵|㒸|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc}}. The original version is [[㒸]], which has no reference to pigs (the pig is a phonetic component).
遂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 㒸. The original version is 㒸, which has no reference to pigs (the pig is a phonetic component).

The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
遅.originText: Variant of 遲. 遲犀𡱝. 𡱝 is a variant of 犀. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

遇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 禺.

遊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 斿.

運.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (motion) + phonetic 軍.

道.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the bronze inscriptions, a {{Han compound|行|首|止|alt2=𩠐|c1=s|c2=p|ls=psc|t1=street|t3=foot|c3=s|nocap=y}}. The {{och-l|*亍}} on the right eventually disappeared, leading to the semantic components combining into {{och-l|*辵}} in the seal script.
道.originText: In the bronze inscriptions, a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 行 (street) + phonetic 首 + semantic 止 (foot). The 亍 on the right eventually disappeared, leading to the semantic components combining into 辵 in the seal script.

達.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 羍. Note that inner component is not 幸 – these are not related, and there is an extra stroke in 達 (three horizontal strokes at the bottom, not two).

違.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 + phonetic 韋.

遜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (to walk) + phonetic 孫.

遠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 袁.

遡.originText: The original character is 㴑. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 (water) + phonetic 㡿. It expresses the meaning “to go upstream” or “to go back.” The commonly used modern character is based on a different form. Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (movement) + phonetic 朔.

遣.originText: Originally 𠳋, an in the : two 又 in a configuration of commanding + 𠂤 – “to send; to dispatch”. The 辵 component was later added in some, which is retained in the modern glyph.

適.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辵|alt1=辶|啻|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}, hence the original form is [[𨗁]]. The inner component was then stylized into [[啇]].

遭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辵|alt1=辶|t1=movement|曹|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to meet with (on the road).
遭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (movement) + phonetic 曹 – to meet with (on the road).

遵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辵|尊|c1=s|t1=walk|c2=p|ls=psc}}. However, the phonetic component (offering a vessel of wine) conveys the concept of veneration and showing respect, which is linked to "follow; obey".
遵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 尊. However, the phonetic component (offering a vessel of wine) conveys the concept of veneration and showing respect, which is linked to "follow; obey".

選.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 止 + phonetic 巽. Xu Shen argues that the original meaning was to respectfully reject and send someone back; to choose also implies rejecting others, hence the meaning.

遺.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (move) + phonetic 貴.

避.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (to walk) + phonetic 辟.

還.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|辵|睘|c1=s|c2=p|t1=walk|ls=psc}} – to go back; to return.
還.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 (walk) + phonetic 睘 – to go back; to return.

那.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 冉 + semantic 邑 (city). Originally the name of a state; later borrowed for a distal demonstrative.

邦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丰 + semantic 邑.

邪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 牙 + semantic 邑 (town; city). The semantic component suggests that this character was originally used in a place name, which ' suggests to be 琅邪. It was later borrowed for other meanings, the most prominent being “wrong; evil” (originally written as 衺).

邸.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|邑|alt1=⻏|氐|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=settlement}}. It originally referred to a building where feudal lords stayed when visiting the capital, and by extension, represents the idea of a “residence” or “mansion.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
邸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 邑 (settlement) + phonetic 氐. It originally referred to a building where feudal lords stayed when visiting the capital, and by extension, represents the idea of a “residence” or “mansion.”

郊.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 交 + semantic 邑.

郎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 良 + semantic 邑 (county; town).

郡.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|邑|alt1=⻏|君|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=city; town}}. It represents one of the ancient local administrative divisions.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
郡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 邑 (city; town) + phonetic 君. It represents one of the ancient local administrative divisions.

部.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|咅|邑|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}. It originally refers to a place in today's [[Gansu]].
部.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 咅 + semantic 邑. It originally refers to a place in today's Gansu.

郭.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
The original version on oracle bones shows a tall tower similar to [[京]] and [[高]] (< [[髙]]) which perhaps was part of the outer city walls in ancient Chinese cities. At the bottom, there was an enclosed space [[囗]] to represent city walls or a city in general and another tower.

Later, the tower at the bottom was stylized like the unrelated [[子]] and the enclosed space was drawn as the unrelated [[回]]. Hence, the whole character was written like {{zh-l|*𩫖}} and {{zh-l|*𩫏}}. Sometimes, the second variant had the bottom part contracted into [[十]].

Eventually, {{zh-l|*邑}} was added to form an {{Han compound|𩫖|t1=tall building|邑|t2=city|ls=ic|nocap=yes}}, hence [[𩫩]], sometimes simplified into [[𨟍]] – outer city walls with tall towers.

From {{w|clerical script}}, the {{zh-l|*𩫖}} became written as the unrelated {{zh-l|*享}} through the process of ''{{w|libian}}''; the two characters are unrelated.
郭.originText: The original version on oracle bones shows a tall tower similar to 京 and 高 (< 髙) which perhaps was part of the outer city walls in ancient Chinese cities. At the bottom, there was an enclosed space 囗 to represent city walls or a city in general and another tower. Later, the tower at the bottom was stylized like the unrelated 子 and the enclosed space was drawn as the unrelated 回. Hence, the whole character was written like 𩫖 and 𩫏. Sometimes, the second variant had the bottom part contracted into 十. Eventually, 邑 was added to form an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 𩫖 (tall building) + semantic 邑 (city), hence 𩫩, sometimes simplified into 𨟍 – outer city walls with tall towers. From, the 𩫖 became written as the unrelated 享 through the process of '; the two characters are unrelated.

郵.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 垂 (far, remote) + semantic 邑 (city) – "relay station".

都.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 者 + semantic 邑 (town, city).

酌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 + phonetic 勺.

配.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 酉 (alcohol vessel) + semantic 卩 (kneeling person).

酎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 (wine) + phonetic 肘.

酒.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|水|酉|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. {{och-l|酉}} is the original pictogram for this word; {{och-l|*水}} was added later to distinguish.
酒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 + phonetic 酉. 酉 is the original pictogram for this word; 水 was added later to distinguish.

酔.originRaw: Unorthodox variant of {{l|mul|醉}}. The phonetic component {{l|mul|卆}} is a variant of {{l|mul|卒}}.
酔.originText: Unorthodox variant of 醉. The phonetic component 卆 is a variant of 卒.

酢.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

{{Han compound|酉|乍|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=wine vessel}}. It conveys the meaning of "vinegar."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
酢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 (wine vessel) + phonetic 乍. It conveys the meaning of "vinegar."

酪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 各 + semantic 酉 (alcohol; fermented drink)

酬.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|酉|州|c1=s|c2=p|t1=liquor vessel; liquor|ls=psc}}<!-- – to present liquor ceremonially; to toast; to reward and honour with the presentation of liquor.-->
酬.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 (liquor vessel; liquor) + phonetic 州

酵.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|酉|孝|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – fermenting in a vessel, making alcoholic drink. 孝 is composed of “young + old”, hence connotations of “aging (in a vase), fermentation”.
酵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 + phonetic 孝 – fermenting in a vessel, making alcoholic drink. 孝 is composed of “young + old”, hence connotations of “aging (in a vase), fermentation”.

酷.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 (alcoholic drink vessel) + phonetic 告.

酸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 + phonetic 夋.

醒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 (alcohol) + phonetic 星.

醜.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|酉|鬼|ls=psc|t2=ghost, demon|c1=p|c2=s}} - demons are ugly in Chinese culture.
醜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 酉 + semantic 鬼 (ghost, demon) - demons are ugly in Chinese culture.

采.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{liushu|ic}}. Two forms can be found in oracle bone script:
# {{Han compound|爪|t1=hand|果|t2=fruit}} – a hand ({{l|zh|爪}}) picking fruits from a tree ({{l|zh|果}}).
# {{Han compound|爪|t1=hand|木|t2=tree}} – a hand ({{l|zh|爪}}) picking from a tree ({{l|zh|木}}).
The current glyph is of composition 2.
采.originText: Two forms can be found in oracle bone script: # Compound: 爪 (hand) + 果 (fruit) – a hand (爪) picking fruits from a tree (果). # Compound: 爪 (hand) + 木 (tree) – a hand (爪) picking from a tree (木). The current glyph is of composition 2.

里.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|田|土|ls=ic|t1=field|t2=soil; earth}} – a measure of land and fields; mile; place.
里.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 田 (field) + semantic 土 (soil; earth) – a measure of land and fields; mile; place.

重.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 人 (man) + phonetic 東 (bag) – a man carrying a bag. A glyph 土 was later added to show that the bag-carrying man is standing on the ground. From this composition (𡍺) is the current form. In the modern form, the man on top can be seen as 亻 (however, the upper part of the character is unrelated to 千). See also 以, in which a person is carrying something, 央, in which a person is carrying a pole, and 年, in which a person is carrying the harvest.

野.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 田 (field) + semantic 土 (earth) + phonetic 予.

量.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
Inconclusive. In the oracle bone and bronze scripts, the most common form was {{Han compound|日|東|t1=sun|t2=bag; east}}. Here are a few proposed interpretations as an {{liushu|ic|nocap=1}}:
* {{zh-l|*日}} was sometimes replaced with {{zh-l|*田}}, so {{w|Qiu Xigui}} thinks that it may be the original character of {{och-l|糧|grain field}}.
* {{w|Yu Xingwu}} interprets it as measuring something under the sun.
* {{w|Guo Moruo}} interprets it as the sun rising in the east – original character of {{och-l|亮}}.
* Huang Dekuan suspects the {{och-l|*日}} is actually {{och-l|昜}} as the phonetic component.

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' interprets this as a {{Han compound|曏|重|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=weight; heavy|nocap=1}}.
量.originText: Inconclusive. In the oracle bone and bronze scripts, the most common form was Compound: 日 (sun) + 東 (bag; east). Here are a few proposed interpretations as an : ' interprets this as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 曏 + semantic 重 (weight; heavy).

金.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|psc}}: semantic {{zh-l|士}} or {{zh-l|王}}, + semantic {{zh-l|*呂}} (“two blocks of metal”) + phonetic {{zh-l|亼}} ({{och-l|今|tr=*kum}}). The blocks of metal were originally drawn as : and later as {{zh-l|丷}}.

Shuowen interprets it as an image of metal in the [[earth]] (Xu Shen writes "象金在土中形") with {{lang-lite|zh|sc=Hani|亼}} as phonetic. But the most ancient versions do not contain the pictogram of the earth.

Originally referred to [[copper]], first used during the Copper Age and the Jade Age in China (hence before the Bronze Age, during which the first bronzes were produced); later the meaning was extended to [[metal]] as a whole, and then to [[gold]].
金.originText: semantic 士 or 王, + semantic 呂 (“two blocks of metal”) + phonetic 亼 (今). The blocks of metal were originally drawn as : and later as 丷. Shuowen interprets it as an image of metal in the earth (Xu Shen writes "象金在土中形") with 亼 as phonetic. But the most ancient versions do not contain the pictogram of the earth. Originally referred to copper, first used during the Copper Age and the Jade Age in China (hence before the Bronze Age, during which the first bronzes were produced); later the meaning was extended to metal as a whole, and then to gold.

釜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 父 + semantic 金 (metal).

針.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 十.

釣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 勺.

鈴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 + phonetic 令.

鉄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 + phonetic 失.

鉛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 㕣 – a kind of metal.

鉢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (gold) + phonetic 本

Japanese {{Han simp|鑛|f=廣|t=広|nocap=y}}. First attested in 1889.<ref>Mari {{smallcaps|Yamashita}}, [http://www.kanken.or.jp/project/data/investigation_incentive_award_2010_yamashita.pdf {{lang|ja|「広」の字体について―略字体の出現時期とその要因―}}], 2011</ref>

In current form, {{Han compound|金|t1=metal|広}}.
鉱.originText: Japanese 鑛廣広. First attested in 1889. In current form, Compound: 金 (metal) + 広.

銀.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 艮.

銃.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 充.

銅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 同.

銘.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|金|t1=metal|名|t2=name|c1=s|c2=p|ls=ic|ls2=psc}} – to engrave in metal.
銘.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 名 (name) – to engrave in metal.

銭.originRaw:
Variant of {{l|mul|錢}}, {{Han simp|錢|f=戔|t=㦮|nocap=1}}; compare {{l|ja|残}}.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
銭.originText: Variant of 錢, 錢戔㦮; compare 残. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

鋭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 兌. It represents the idea of a "sharp" or "pointed" tip of a blade or cutting tool.

鋼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 岡.

錠.originRaw:

{{Han compound|金|定|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=metal}}. It conveys the meaning of a ritual vessel.<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
錠.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 定. It conveys the meaning of a ritual vessel.

錦.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 金 + semantic 帛.

錮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 固.

錯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 昔 – grindstone.

鍋.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 咼.

鍛.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 段.

鍵.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 建 – a metal key.

鎌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (gold; metal) + phonetic 兼

鎖.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 𧴪.

{{Han compound|金|真|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=metal}} – to press down on (with a metal weight).
鎮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 真 – to press down on (with a metal weight).

鏡.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 竟.

鐘.originRaw:

{{Han compound|金|童|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. It indicates a bell, including a bronze large bell used in rituals in ancient China.
鐘.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 + phonetic 童. It indicates a bell, including a bronze large bell used in rituals in ancient China.

鑑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 金 (metal) + phonetic 監.

長.originText: an old man with long hair; an ancient variant still used is 镸 (e.g., ⾽ and 鬓). Compare 彡 and the top component of 老 and its variant 考.

門.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}}: a gate. Compare {{och-l|戶|(one) door}}, which is half of this character ([[𠁣]]).
門.originText: a gate. Compare 戶, which is half of this character (𠁣).

閉.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 門 (door) + semantic 材 (material; timber).

components.sense: latch and/or wooden pole that shuts a door

開.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 門 (door) + semantic 一 (latch and/or wooden pole that shuts a door) + semantic 廾 (a pair of hands) — a pair of hands opening a latched door. 一 and 廾 are combined into 开 since the Small Seal script; however, in the conservative variant 𨵑, the two hands and the latch are well visible. Compare 闢. See also 關, in which the door is kept shut by two wooden poles.

閑.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 門 (door) + semantic 木 (wood) – a fence.

間.originRaw:

Variant form of {{och-l|閒|space, gap}} with {{och-l|*月|moon}} replaced by {{och-l|*日|day}}.
間.originText: Variant form of 閒 with 月 replaced by 日.

関.originText: 關𢇇关. Unorthodox form of 關 listed in the. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

閣.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 門 (gate) + phonetic 各.

閥.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 門 + phonetic 伐.

闇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 門 + phonetic 音.

{{Han simp|鬪|f=鬥|t=門}}, itself a simplified variant of [[鬭]], ultimately {{liushu|psc}}, with semantic {{m|mul|鬥||fight|sc=Hant}} (unrelated to [[門]]).

Phonetic is originally [[斲]] but this is graphically simplified to [[𭔰]]; compare [[尌]], which is similar.
闘.originText: 鬪鬥門, itself a simplified variant of 鬭, ultimately, with semantic 鬥 (unrelated to 門). Phonetic is originally 斲 but this is graphically simplified to 𭔰; compare 尌, which is similar.

防.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 阜 + phonetic 方.

阻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 阜 + phonetic 且.

{{Han compound|阜|alt1=阝|t1=hill, wall|夅|t2=to descend|ls=psc|ls2=ic|c1=s|c2=p}} – descending a hill.

{{Han etym}}
Derivation from {{m|zh|敶|tr=-}}, itself derived from an {{Han compound|nocap=1|ls=ic|東|東|攴|t1=sack?}}; later, one {{lang|zh|[[東]]}} was abbreviated, and a {{m|zh|阜|tr=-}} added on the left.

陪.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 阜 (soil mountain) + phonetic 咅 The 阜 suggests, by extension from the meaning of “pile up soil”, to join up with, to be close to: to accompany.

陵.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 阜 (mound) + phonetic 夌 (mound; hill). Originally written 夌.

陶.originText: In oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, Ideogrammic compound: semantic 阜 (mound of dirt) + semantic 勹 (two people) + semantic 土 (earth) – "to dig", original character of 掏. The shapes beneath the outermost 勹 were corrupted in, arriving at the modern form 缶 in seal script. Now a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 阜 (soil mountain) + phonetic 匋 (make pottery).

陽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 阜 (hill) + phonetic 昜 (sunshine). 昜 is the original character for this word, 阜 was added later.

隆.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 降 + semantic 生, with 𡕒 later dropped.

{{Han compound|隹|牙|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p|t1=a short-tailed bird}}. It represents the meaning of a rook, which is a type of crow. By extension, it is used metaphorically to mean "elegant" or "refined."<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
雅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 隹 (a short-tailed bird) + phonetic 牙. It represents the meaning of a rook, which is a type of crow. By extension, it is used metaphorically to mean "elegant" or "refined."

雇.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 戶 + semantic 隹.

雌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 此 + semantic 隹.

雑.originText: Unorthodox variant of 雜. Compare 卆 from 卒. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

{{Han compound|暵|隹|c1=p|c2=s|abb1=y|t2=bird|ls=psc}} – a type of bird. Phonetically borrowed for other senses.

雪.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Ancient simplification of {{och-l|䨮}}, which is in turn {{Han compound|雨|彗|c1=s|c2=p|t1=rain|ls=psc|nocap=1}}.
雪.originText: Ancient simplification of 䨮, which is in turn Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 彗.

雰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 分 (divide, small).

{{Han compound|雨|云|c1=s|c2=p|t1=rain|t2=cloud|ls=ic|ls2=psc}}. Originally written {{lang|zh|云}}, with the {{lang|zh|雨}} radical added to {{lang|zh|云}} to distinguish from the borrowed sense of “to speak”.
雲.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 云 (cloud). Originally written 云, with the 雨 radical added to 云 to distinguish from the borrowed sense of “to speak”.

{{Han compound|雨|t1=rain|令|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}. On the oracle bone script, only thick raindrops are depicted falling from the sky.
零.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 令. On the oracle bone script, only thick raindrops are depicted falling from the sky.
