雷.originText: Ancient simplification of 靁, which was a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 畾.

電.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 申; also : 雨 + 申.

需.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|ls=ic|天|雨|t1=person|t2=rain}} — a person getting wet in the rain. Original character of {{och-l|濡|to get wet}}. The component {{zh-l|*天}} corrupted into {{zh-l|*而}} during the Han dynasty.
需.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 天 (person) + semantic 雨 (rain) — a person getting wet in the rain. Original character of 濡. The component 天 corrupted into 而 during the Han dynasty.

震.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 + phonetic 辰.

霜.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 相.

霧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 (rain) + phonetic 務.

露.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 雨 + phonetic 路.

青.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}

Zhang (2022): {{Han compound|ls=psc|生|井|c1=p|c2=p|tr=*tsʰˤeŋ|tr2=*tseŋʔ|tr1=*sreŋ}}. <ref>張富海 「説“井”」 『出土文献与古文字研究』第10輯 復旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心編、上海古籍出版社、2022年、126-136頁。</ref>

{{Shuowen}} interprets it as an ideogrammic compound of {{och-l|*生|growth of plants}} + {{och-l|*丹|[[cinnabar]]}}. A variant inspired by this interpretation is {{och-l|*𤯞}}. The implication being that cinnabar, being used for dyeing, would imply “color” in general, giving the combined meaning “color of growing plants” → “blue-green”.

In the modern glyph, the top component is reduced to {{l|zh|龶}}, and the bottom component resembles the unrelated {{l|zh|月|t=moon}}.

The {{w|Second round of simplified Chinese characters|second-round simplified form}} of the character is based on the calligraphic form of the character.
青.originText: Zhang (2022): Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 生 + phonetic 井. interprets it as an ideogrammic compound of 生 + 丹. A variant inspired by this interpretation is 𤯞. The implication being that cinnabar, being used for dyeing, would imply “color” in general, giving the combined meaning “color of growing plants” → “blue-green”. In the modern glyph, the top component is reduced to 龶, and the bottom component resembles the unrelated 月. The of the character is based on the calligraphic form of the character.

非.originText: two wings facing opposite directions. Originally, it represented wings; then, according to Xu Shen, its meaning changed into "leave; disobey" (違). Eventually, it was used perhaps as a phonetic loan to mean "not to be". Unrelated to the Kangxi radical 韭.

面.originText: , A man’s face, with an eye exaggerated, derived from 𦣻. The horizontal stroke was added later. Unrelated to 自. Etymology 2: 麵麥 as adopted by the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (漢字簡化方案漢字簡化方案) in 1956.

革.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a stretched animal hide: the upper is head, the bottom is the tail and legs. The hands [[臼]] around the hide were briefly added later.
革.originText: a stretched animal hide: the upper is head, the bottom is the tail and legs. The hands 臼 around the hide were briefly added later.

靴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 革 (leather) + phonetic 化.

韓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 倝 + semantic 韋 (surround).

音.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|i}} – based on the structure of {{zh-l|*言}}, with an additional short horizontal stroke inside the {{zh-l|*口|mouth}}, forming a shape similar to {{zh-l|*甘}}. The ''{{w|Shuowen Jiezi}}'' describes the structure as {{lang|zh|从言含一}} ("from {{zh-l|*言}} containing {{zh-l|*一}}").

The added stroke graphically seals the mouth, likely representing partially closed or muffled vocalization, in contrast with {{zh-l|*言|articulate speech}}. This is consistent with the ''*ʔəm'' word family, which clusters around meanings of covering and closure: compare homophones {{zh-l|*瘖|tr=*ʔum}} and {{zh-l|*喑||mute|tr=*ʔəmʔ}}, and {{zh-l|*韽||faint, weak sound|tr=*ʔˤəm}}.

See also {{zh-l|*言}}.
音.originText: based on the structure of 言, with an additional short horizontal stroke inside the 口, forming a shape similar to 甘. The ' describes the structure as 从言含一 ("from 言 containing 一"). The added stroke graphically seals the mouth, likely representing partially closed or muffled vocalization, in contrast with 言. This is consistent with the word family, which clusters around meanings of covering and closure: compare homophones 瘖 and 喑, and 韽. See also 言.

韻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 音 + phonetic 員.

響.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 鄉 + semantic 音 (sound).

頂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 丁 + semantic 頁 (head).

頃.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 匕 + semantic 頁 (head). The head is askew, the original meaning of 傾.

項.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 工 + semantic 頁 (head).

順.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 川 + semantic 頁. Shuowen considers it to be an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 川 (river) + semantic 頁 (head) - flowing in the river, i.e. following/obeying the river's current. Compare the English phrase go with the flow.

須.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|彡|頁|ls=p|t1=hair|t2=head}} – a head with hair on its side – [[beard]]; [[whisker]]s — original character of {{och-l|鬚}}. Originally a single picture, but abstracted in the seal script into a compound.
須.originText: Pictogram: 彡 (hair) + 頁 (head) – a head with hair on its side – beard; whiskers — original character of 鬚. Originally a single picture, but abstracted in the seal script into a compound.

預.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 予 + semantic 頁.

頑.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 元 (head) + semantic 頁 (head). As 元 came to be used to mean “original”, rather than “head”, this character was formed from the original meaning of 元 + the semantic element 頁 to affirm the “head” meaning, but with the modification in meaning to “an intransigent head”; the head of a heady person.

頒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 分 + semantic 頁 (head).

頓.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|屯|頁|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t1=head of a kneeling person}}. It expresses the meaning “to bow” or “to kowtow.”<ref>Digital Shinjigen 2017</ref>
頓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 屯 (head of a kneeling person) + semantic 頁. It expresses the meaning “to bow” or “to kowtow.”

領.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 令 + semantic 頁.

頭.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 豆 + semantic 頁 (head).

頰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|夾|頁|t2=head|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}} – part of the head.
頰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 夾 + semantic 頁 (head) – part of the head.

頻.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
Originally  {{och-l|*瀕}}, {{liushu|ic|nocap=1}}: a person {{och-l|*頁}} near the water's edge {{och-l|*涉}}, extended to mean "on the verge". The water component {{och-l|*氵}} was removed to distinguish its usage for "frequent".
頻.originText: Originally 瀕, : a person 頁 near the water's edge 涉, extended to mean "on the verge". The water component 氵 was removed to distinguish its usage for "frequent".

題.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 是 + semantic 頁 (head) – “forehead”.

額.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 客 + semantic 頁 (head).

顎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 咢 + semantic 頁.

顔.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{w|Variant Chinese character|Variant form}} of {{l|mul|顏}} ({{l|mul|彥}} → {{l|mul|彦}}).

願.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 原 + semantic 頁.

類.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 頪 + semantic 犬.

顧.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 雇 + semantic 頁.

風.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|j}} of {{och-l|鳳|fenghuang}} borrowed for sound to represent {{och-l|風|wind}}. The right part of the bronze inscription of the character consists of phonetic {{och-l|凡}} at the top, and three parts depicting the fur on the tail of the male ''fenghuang'' at the bottom.

Subsequent forms of {{lang|zh|風}} are based on the right part of its bronze inscription, with two of the three threads of "fur" removed for simplification. The {{zh-l|虫}} in the Chu script and Qin script of {{lang|zh|風}} was likely a result of further simplification of the "fur".

''{{w|Shuowen}}'' misinterpreted the character {{lang|zh|風}} by associating it with insects. ({{zh-ref|Li, 2012}})
風.originText: of 鳳 borrowed for sound to represent 風. The right part of the bronze inscription of the character consists of phonetic 凡 at the top, and three parts depicting the fur on the tail of the male fenghuang at the bottom. Subsequent forms of 風 are based on the right part of its bronze inscription, with two of the three threads of "fur" removed for simplification. The 虫 in the Chu script and Qin script of 風 was likely a result of further simplification of the "fur". ' misinterpreted the character 風 by associating it with insects.

飛.originText: a bird flying upwards. In its modern form, resembles a tasseled 升.

components.sense: a bowl of rice on a stand

食.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 亼 (mouth) + semantic 皀 (a bowl of rice on a stand). In the modern form, the bowl of rice has corrupted into the similar but unrelated 良 or 艮. The variant form 𠊊 preserves the original composition. Shuowen interprets the 亼 as a phonetic component.

飢.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 + phonetic 几.

飯.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 (food) + phonetic 反.

飲.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
In the oracle bone script, it was an {{Han compound|酉|人|口|ls=ic|t1=bottle (of alcoholic beverages)|t2=person|t3=mouth (occasionally with the tongue protruding)|nocap=1}} – a person bending over a bottle to drink the alcoholic beverage. The droplets represented drops of the drink or saliva.

In the bronze script, the mouth separated from the body and corrupted into {{och-l|今}}, while the rest of the body became {{och-l|欠}}. These two components also acted as phonetic components. These changes were inherited in the seal script, leading ''{{w|Shuowen}}'' to interpret this character ({{zh-l|*㱃}}) as a {{Han compound|酓|欠|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|t2=yawn|nocap=1}}.

In the clerical script, {{zh-l|*酓}} has been modified to {{zh-l|*食|to eat}}, which is inherited in the current form.
飲.originText: In the oracle bone script, it was an Ideogrammic compound: semantic 酉 (bottle (of alcoholic beverages)) + semantic 人 (person) + semantic 口 (mouth (occasionally with the tongue protruding)) – a person bending over a bottle to drink the alcoholic beverage. The droplets represented drops of the drink or saliva. In the bronze script, the mouth separated from the body and corrupted into 今, while the rest of the body became 欠. These two components also acted as phonetic components. These changes were inherited in the seal script, leading ' to interpret this character (㱃) as a Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 酓 + semantic 欠 (yawn). In the clerical script, 酓 has been modified to 食, which is inherited in the current form.

飼.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 + phonetic 司.

飽.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 (food) + phonetic 包. For etymology 2, the 食 radical specifies its dietary use (instead of just being a generic wrap).

飾.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 飤 + semantic 巾 (cloth). The 人 has changed shape into 𠂉.

餅.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|食|alt1=飠|t1=food|并|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}}; traditional glyph form during [[Ming]] and [[Qing]] dynasty used to advocate {{l-lite|zh||sc=Hani|幷}} (as in {{l-lite|zh||sc=Hani|餠}}) based on the influence of ''[[w:Shuowen Jiezi|Shuowen]]''.
餅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 (food) + phonetic 并; traditional glyph form during Ming and Qing dynasty used to advocate 幷 (as in 餠) based on the influence of Shuowen.

養.originText: Ideogrammic compound: phonetic 羊 (sheep) + semantic 食 (to feed).

餌.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 (to eat) + phonetic 耳.

餓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 + phonetic 我.

館.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 食 + phonetic 官.

首.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han simp|𩠐|f=巛|t=丷}}. Originally {{liushu|p|nocap=1}} of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns. In the oracle bone script, it appeared with or without hair ({{zh-l|*巛}}), but {{zh-l|*𩠐}}, the form with hair, was the form that was perpetuated.
首.originText: 𩠐巛丷. Originally of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns. In the oracle bone script, it appeared with or without hair (巛), but 𩠐, the form with hair, was the form that was perpetuated.

香.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
In the oracle bone script, it was {{Han compound|黍|口|ls=ic|nocap=1|t1=glutinous millet|t2=mouth}}. The whole character perhaps indicate that millet was used to produce liquor from fermentation which could be drank and/or sacrificed.

In the seal script, the {{zh-l|*口}} was replaced with the related {{zh-l|*甘|sweet}}. Hence, the most conservative variant is [[𪏽]].

Currently, the {{zh-l|*黍}} has simplified into {{zh-l|*禾}} and the form of the bottom component {{zh-l|*甘}} has become akin to the unrelated {{zh-l|*曰}}.
香.originText: In the oracle bone script, it was Ideogrammic compound: semantic 黍 (glutinous millet) + semantic 口 (mouth). The whole character perhaps indicate that millet was used to produce liquor from fermentation which could be drank and/or sacrificed. In the seal script, the 口 was replaced with the related 甘. Hence, the most conservative variant is 𪏽. Currently, the 黍 has simplified into 禾 and the form of the bottom component 甘 has become akin to the unrelated 曰.

馬.originText: a horse with its head facing the left, showing a flowing mane in the wind, standing vertically on two legs. In the bronze inscriptions, the head was often simplified into an eye (目). The legs eventually evolved into four dots (灬, unrelated to 火). Contrast with 鹿, which saw a very different development, and 𢊁 (as in 薦), which is a hybrid: it has the legs of 馬 (灬) but the head of 鹿.

駄.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 馬 + phonetic 太.

駐.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|馬|主|ls=psc|t1=horse|c1=s|c2=p}}. Cf. {{zh-m|住}}, with the {{zh-m|*人}} radical replacing {{zh-m|*馬}}.
駐.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 馬 (horse) + phonetic 主. Cf. 住, with the 人 radical replacing 馬.

駒.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 馬 (horse) + phonetic 句.

騎.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|馬|t1=horse|奇|ls=psc|c1=s|c2=p}} – to ride horseback
騎.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 馬 (horse) + phonetic 奇 – to ride horseback

騰.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|朕|馬|c1=p|c2=s|t2=horse|ls=psc}} – a horse's gallop, prance.
騰.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 朕 + semantic 馬 (horse) – a horse's gallop, prance.

驚.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|敬|馬|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s}}, as horses are [[skittish]] (easily startled and frightened).
驚.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 敬 + semantic 馬, as horses are skittish (easily startled and frightened).

骨.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|冎|肉|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|no_och1=y}}. {{och-l|*冎}} is the original pictogram for this character; {{och-l|*肉}} was added later to distinguish.
骨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 冎 + semantic 肉 + no_och1=y. 冎 is the original pictogram for this character; 肉 was added later to distinguish.

骸.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 骨 (bone) + phonetic 亥.

高.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}

{{liushu|p}} – a tall building. Compare {{zh-l|*京}}, which however is not a Kangxi radical.
高.originText: a tall building. Compare 京, which however is not a Kangxi radical.

鬱.originRaw:
{{Han etym}} {{Han compound|ls=ic|林|大|勹|t1=forest|t2=standing person|t3=leaning person}} — people hiding in a lush forest. Later, an abbreviated {{och-l|爵}} was added, leading to the current form.于省吾 「釈（⿱林勹）」 『甲骨文字釈林』 中華書局、1979年、328-330頁。
呉振武 「説“苞”“鬱”」 『中原文物』1990年第3期 第32—36頁。
張世超、孫凌安、金国泰、馬如森 『金文形義通解』 中文出版社、1996年、1286-1289頁。
季旭昇撰 『説文新証』 芸文印書館、2014年、433-434頁。
王子楊 「甲骨文“鬱”的用法」 『文史』2016年第3輯 43-56頁。
鬱.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 林 (forest) + semantic 大 (standing person) + semantic 勹 (leaning person) — people hiding in a lush forest. Later, an abbreviated 爵 was added, leading to the current form.

鬼.originText: a kneeling man or figure with an ugly face (甶). The ugly face could be a mask. The lower right “dot” is a small 厶; it is a residual tail that was added later – compare 离. Related to 畏 (variant 𠂽), which originally depicts a ghost standing with a stick in hand. Compare 異, in which the 田 also derives from a face and indicates a mask. Compare also 禺, in which the top component represents either a mask or a monkey's head.

魂.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 云 + semantic 鬼.

魅.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 未 + semantic 鬼 (spirit).

魔.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 麻 + semantic 鬼 (demon).

魚.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{liushu|p}} – a fish. A conservative variant is [[𤋳]].
魚.originText: a fish. A conservative variant is 𤋳.

鮮.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 魚 (fish) + phonetic 羴. Alternatively, may be Ideogrammic compound: semantic 魚 (fish) + semantic 羊 (sheep) – delicious.

鯨.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 魚 (fish) + phonetic 京.

鳥.originText: a bird with a dangling tail. Compare 烏, which is very similar, of similar origin, and 隹, which originated from a similar image of a bird, but is today rather more abstract and less recognizable. Compare to Egyptian 𓄿

鳴.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 口 (mouth) + semantic 鳥 (bird) – to cry.

鶴.originText: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 寉 + semantic 鳥.

鹿.originText: a deer. Current form is highly abstracted – legs have transformed to 比 – note grouping of front and rear legs, which are bent – head has transformed to middle component (similar to 凸/曲), while antlers on top and extended lip/mouth on left transformed into 广. This transformation occurred during seal characters. Contrast the very different development of 馬, and the transformation in 廌 (as in 薦), which has the head of 鹿 but the legs of 馬 (灬).

麓.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 林 + phonetic 鹿

麦.originRaw: Corruption of {{zh-l|八|tr=-}} into a horizontal stroke.
麦.originText: Corruption of 八 into a horizontal stroke.

麺.originRaw: Variant of {{l|mul|麵}}, {{Han simp|麵|f=麥|t=麦|nocap=y}}. The modern Japanese usage is of reform ([[shinjitai]]) nature.
麺.originText: Variant of 麵, 麵麥麦. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.

麻.originRaw:
{{Han etyl}}
{{Han compound|厂|𣏟|ls=ic}}: a representation of hemp leaves.
麻.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 厂 + semantic 𣏟: a representation of hemp leaves.

黒.originRaw: Variant of {{l|mul|黑}}. {{Han simp|黑}}, replacing two dots with one stroke. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature. Compare {{m|ja|毋}}, the shinjitai of {{m|mul|母}}.
黒.originText: Variant of 黑. 黑, replacing two dots with one stroke. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature. Compare 毋, the shinjitai of 母.

黙.originRaw:
Japanese shinjitai {{Han simp|默|f=黑|t=黒}}; further, 黒 is split into [[里]] and
[[灬]] (on the bottom). Compare [[点]] (from [[點]]).
黙.originText: Japanese shinjitai 默黑黒; further, 黒 is split into 里 and 灬 (on the bottom). Compare 点 (from 點).

鼓.originRaw:
{{Han etym}}
{{Han compound|壴|支|t1=drum|t2=hand holding drumstick|ls=ic}}. Compare [[殸]]. See also the right component of [[段]].
鼓.originText: Ideogrammic compound: semantic 壴 (drum) + semantic 支 (hand holding drumstick). Compare 殸. See also the right component of 段.

鼻.originText: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 自 (nose) + phonetic 畀 + no_och1=y. 自 originally referred to this word, but came to be used to refer to 自 instead, so the sense of “nose” has been replaced by this character. Some scholars interpret 鼻* as a combination of a nose (自) and two lungs (畀), however sc=Hani on oracle bones represents an arrow.

𠮟.originRaw: Found in the historical {{w|Longkan Shoujian}} 《{{lw|zh|龍龕手鑑}}》 dictionary compiled in 997 AD.
𠮟.originText: Found in the historical 《龍龕手鑑》 dictionary compiled in 997 AD.
